News.title: Families of two police officers killed in crash say they were heroes
News.content:
Two police officers who died when a car travelling the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle have been hailed as heroes by their families.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died when a Volkswagen Passat, which officers had been pursuing until seconds before, collided with their marked armed response car on the A66 near Middlesbrough on Saturday.

The Passat's occupants - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17 - also died.

In tributes released by Cleveland Police, PC Clough's family said he had been "willing to help anyone", while PC Blades' wife described him as "loved beyond words".

"No words will ever feel like the right words to honour our Matt," she said, adding that he had been a "beloved husband" and the "most devoted father" to their two young sons who would grow up knowing what an "incredible" dad he had been.

"He gave his life in the line of duty, protecting and serving others with courage, dedication and selflessness," she said.

"The pain of losing him is beyond words, and our lives will never be the same.

"Neither will the love he gave us ever fade.

"He may have left this world committed to the duty he believed in, but his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave to his family."

She ended the tribute to her husband: "Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever our superhero. Our Matt and Dad."

News.title: How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends where you live
News.content:
Sykes says that none of his friends in his graduating class in dentistry still works in the NHS. "My friends have gone private, retired or teach - any pathway to avoid NHS dentistry."

Shiv Pabary, chair of the British Dental Association's General Dental Practice Committee, says the situation is "the direct result of choices made by successive governments". He warns that unless ministers "fix and fund NHS dentistry", more dentists could choose to reduce their NHS work or leave the service altogether.

Overall dentist practice numbers have risen in England over the last decade.

"This is not a shortage of dentistry but a shortage of NHS dentistry," says Dayan. "Practices will need to be incentivised back into NHS work in the places where the NHS footprint has thinned most."

While most parts of England recorded declines in practices offering NHS dental care, the reductions were smallest in North West London, the Black Country and North East London.

North East London was the only area to see any increase during the period, recording one additional practice offering NHS treatment compared with a decade ago.

Every other region of England saw the number of NHS dental practices fall.

Looking at the number of practices doing NHS work is not the same as looking at exactly how much health service capacity there is - practices can vary in size. But if you look at other measures such as the amount of treatment being done, the numbers are still down, although not as steep as the fall in practice numbers.

The government says that it is changing the dental contract and training more dentists in the areas most in need. The government says it will also make it a requirement for newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for a minimum period of at least three years.

Campaign group 38 degrees calls the current dental crisis "shameful", with people being "forced to pay money they can't afford or suffer with the pain, shame, and further complications that come from being denied vital NHS healthcare".

News.title: 'It's not Alton Towers' - rows break out over queuing at Wales' highest mountain
News.content:
Visitors to Wales' highest mountain are being urged to respect others by not skipping queues to reach the top following rows among climbers.

Recent hot weather means there have been bumper summer crowds at Yr Wyddfa, also known as Snowdon, where people have reportedly waited more than one hour to reach the 1,085m (3,560ft)-high summit.

Social media videos have shown arguments among queue-jumpers and those patiently waiting their turn to touch the metal plate that marks the top.

A recent video showed Marc Screeton, from Manchester, being heckled as he bypassed the line, saying: "Imagine queuing on a mountain? No chance."

But others have said queuing is necessary for safety reasons.

The mountain's growing popularity in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia, has led to bottlenecks, and queues are now common on the stone steps leading to a metal plate or trig point where people pose for photos and videos.

Speaking to BBC Wales, walkers on the mountain had mixed views about those jumping the queues.

Lucy Taylor said: "I think you should queue because it's really quite dangerous and everyone's trying to get up there - it's just not safe."

News.title: Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
News.content:
An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 34, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; Â£289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

In an interview with Nine Network's 60 Minutes, due to be aired this weekend, Stewart described seeing the shark's "horrific" face.

"I'll never forget its face - it was a monster," she says.

"It was holding onto my leg and I just thought of (my daughter) August, and I thought, 'she's not going to have a mum. She's gonna grow up without a mum'."

Fighting back tears, she goes on: "I couldn't handle that, I didn't want her to not have a mum. I just thought, I've got to fight it, do everything I can to be here."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

News.title: Pubs and hotels could see business rates reformed after review
News.content:
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.

The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.

Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.

Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.

According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.

Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.

James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."

The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade (FMT) - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.

Jonathan Lawson, the chief executive of Butcombe Group, which has 120 pubs across the south and south west of England, told the BBC's Today programme that the use of FMT meant pubs were effectively being "punished for success", while large online retailers that operate out of warehouses were not subject to revenue-based rates calculations.

Their rates, he said, "are calculated based on what is deemed to be the market rent for that area, and takes very little on board in terms of revenue driven through that site".

"You can have a very large site paying a relatively low level of business rates versus a relatively small pub... paying a very high level of business rates."

Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.

Northern Ireland and Scotland set their own valuations, while Wales presently chooses to align its methodology with England. As the same approach is used across England and Wales, the review will be looking for responses from both nations.

Schurder's appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".

However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.

Tom Ironside from the British Retail Consortium also welcomed the review but said it was "vitally important that the needs of retailers are not overlooked".

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".

"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".

News.title: Reform says it will prioritise young British-born workers for social housing
News.content:
Reform previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".

Tice will set out how Reform intends to pay for the 50,000 affordable homes during Monday's news conference, the party added.

"It is time for us to prioritise young British workers, and that is what our policy is about," Tice said on Sunday.

"I have spent my entire career in property development, as a private citizen I have led companies which delivered thousands of new homes. In government I will break down the barriers to getting generation rent onto the housing ladder."

He added it is "time to get Britain building" and give "our young people the homes they deserve".

UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.

That means around 11.5% of main householders, the perÂ­son in whose name the social home is renÂ­ted, were non-UK or Irish nationÂ­als.

For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.

Labour rubbished Reform's plans and insisted social housing is already "tightly controlled".

"Illegal migrants, asylum seekers and migrants on student or work visas are not eligible for social housing," the Labour spokesperson said.

Labour said the Reform plan would target long-term UK residents that have contributed to our country but are not British citizens, including NHS staff.

"It would leave more families at risk of homelessness and drive up use of temporary accommodation at the taxpayers' expense. It would also mean renegotiations with the EU, resulting in years of wrangling."

The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.

The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.

Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.

"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."

Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".

News.title: Trump waves green flag to start IndyCar race through Washington streets
News.content:
US President Donald Trump was among hundreds of people who gathered to see the IndyCar race through the streets of Washington DC on Sunday, marking the culmination of a series of summer events to celebrate the country's 250th birthday.

Driver Kyle Kirkwood won the race, earning his seventh career Indycar win.

Ahead of the race, the president and First Lady Melania Trump took a ceremonial lap of the 1.7-mile track in his presidential limousine, The Beast.

As they reached the finish line, Trump's new Air Force One completed a flyover above the capital.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is the first time professional road racing has been hosted in the capital.

News.title: Doctors said I was too young to have endometriosis at 13 - I had to take morphine to cope
News.content:
But the most frustrating thing for Grace, and why she contacted BBC Your Voice, is because she does not feel medical experts recognise that teenagers and adolescents can suffer from endometriosis.

Grace's GP did not diagnose her condition and nor did the first consultant she saw privately.

She says: "Even a specialist didn't believe me. And if a specialist won't listen to me, who will?" It was not until the family pushed for a second private opinion that she got a positive diagnosis.

Endometriosis, which occurs when tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside it, can cause debilitating symptoms, such as pelvic pain, heavy periods and fatigue. About 10% of women are affected by it, according to NHS data.

This week BBC presenter Emma Barnett revealed she had to have a hysterectomy for her endometriosis - which she said she never wanted to have.

It can develop at any age once periods begin - and it is a common misconception that only older women suffer from the condition, says the charity Endometriosis UK,

Faye Farthing, a spokesperson for the charity, says the government, NHS and health practitioners need to improve menstrual health education for young people "if we are to ensure the next generation are not robbed of the future they deserve".

The charity says it can take a long time to diagnose endometriosis - an average of nine years in older women.

And in the early stages, for example with teenagers, it often doesn't show up on an ultrasound scan. However, new tests are being developed which will help spot the condition earlier.

Getting pregnant can be more difficult - even aged 14, Grace says she has been warned it is likely to affect her fertility. She's been advised she may not be able to have children after the age of 30 because of damage to her reproductive organs.

She feels rushed: "I have to have kids within the next 15 years, otherwise I might not be able to."

News.title: 'It took 30 years to talk about my teacher raping me'
News.content:
It wasn't until 2022 when she had grief counselling that she confronted what had happened.

The following year she made a formal complaint to police.

"I am a mum now and my children are the age that I was then - and that cannot happen to them," she said.

She said finding the courage to contact police was difficult and it "took me a few days just to pluck up the courage".

Det Con Andrew Jones, from West Midlands Police's Major Crime Team, said: "I would like to express my gratitude to the brave woman who came forward to report what Allen had done to her as a child.

"She has been so brave throughout the investigation and court process."

Allen was sentenced at Birmingham Crown Court in July.

His defence argued the offence was committed during a difficult period in his life while he was experiencing anxiety.

But, during his sentencing remarks, His Honour Judge Paul Farrer KC, said he did not accept Allen's judgement was impaired at the time and said he had abused a position of trust.

That his offending remained undiscovered for more than three decades meant he was able to enjoy life in the community, the court heard.

It was noted the defendant was now in poor health, had diabetes, glaucoma and impaired hearing, had previously had a heart attack and might be experiencing the onset of Parkinson's disease.

The woman said it was not the sentencing but the guilty verdict that had been most important to her.

"I felt heard, I felt people have listened and they believe me," she added. "It is really validating and it raises your self-esteem a little bit, it means a lot."

News.title: Rain to return this week with chance of thunderstorms and flooding
News.content:
The weather is set to turn more unsettled this week as rain returns with a chance of thunderstorms and localised flooding.

Some places could see a return to showery conditions by Tuesday, but it is from Wednesday onwards that more widespread and persistent rain will arrive from the south.

The wet weather will be welcome for parched regions of the UK, but a lot more will be needed before drought conditions start to ease.

As well as the rain, temperatures will also be on the rise once more, as warmer air moving in could push midweek highs close to 30C (86F) in places.

News.title: CrossCountry to run full train service after power outage causes major disruption
News.content:
Train operator CrossCountry says it expects to run a full service on Monday after cancelling nearly all of its UK services the day before following a power cut at its control centre.

The outage in Birmingham at the weekend brought disruption from Glasgow to Penzance.

Major routes were affected between Birmingham and Manchester, which pass through Stoke-on-Trent, Coventry and Wolverhampton. Journeys from Leeds to York and Cheltenham to Cardiff were also caught in the travel chaos, leaving passengers frustrated.

On Monday morning, CrossCountry reported a handful of service cancellations, although these were put down to trains departing late and staff shortages.

Customers are advised to check their journey before travelling.

The operator on Sunday thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the disruption.

Tickets purchased for travel on CrossCountry services on Sunday will be valid for travel on CrossCountry services until Wednesday, the company has said.

News.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
News.content:
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.

The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.

Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.

"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool united in tribute to legend Keegan
News.content:
Kevin Keegan's family were in attendance as Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters came together to pay tribute to the former England captain.

Keegan, who played for both clubs, before going on to manage Newcastle, died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer.

As the teams met for the first time since his death, in their Premier League season opener at St James' Park on Sunday, members of Keegan's family were present in the directors' box.

A number of Keegan's former players from this memorable first spell in charge of Newcastle, between 1992 and 1997, were also at the game.

News.title: Scammers increasingly using QR codes to steal money and data
News.content:
When Les Howard could not find change for parking during a trip to the coast, a quick response (QR) code on the meter seemed to be the answer.

But the next day, the 61-year-old realised he had become the victim of an increasingly common scam as criminals started taking money from his bank account in Â£60 chunks.

Reports of QR code-related scams have gone up by 700% in the past four years, figures by Report Fraud have revealed.

Experts say criminals are finding different ways to exploit the codes as they become a common part of everyday life.

This could be disguising suspicious links in emails, gaining access to victims' messaging apps or convincing people who are out and about to download fraudulent apps to steal their money and data.

That is what happened to Howard, from Widnes, who was visiting Caernarfon in North Wales with his wife.

"We went to the car park where we normally go," Howard told the BBC Scam Secrets podcast.

"I normally have change in the car to pay for the parking, but this time I didn't.

"So there was a QR code to download and get an app and pay via an app."

News.title: Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
News.content:
Mayors across England will be given new powers to overrule local councils on some planning decisions.

The change would apply to proposals with more than 150 homes, more than 15,000 square metres of commercial space or buildings over 30 metres.

Mayors in 13 areas including Manchester, Liverpool, the West of England and the West Midlands will gain similar powers to Sir Sadiq Khan in London, who is already able to "call in" planning decisions.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the powers were an "essential part of the toolkit that mayors need to effectively deliver new homes and regeneration".

The Conservatives questioned whether it was right for councils to lose the "ability to make planning decisions in their own communities".

The powers will also be available to mayors in the Combined Authorities in North East England, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, York and North Yorkshire, Hull and East Yorkshire, Greater Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, East Midlands, and Tees Valley.

Paul Bristow, the Conservative mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, told BBC Breakfast that if he had local powers, he would approve "tomorrow" a couple of blocked schemes that he said would "get new homes built that families could move into and charge economic growth".

Bristow said "it's not about overriding what local people want", but about developers and councils finding a compromise on projects instead of just saying no - which he believed the "perceived threat of intervention" would help.

In London, where Khan already has the power to review decisions on certain developments, external, housebuilding has fallen in recent years. But Pennycook insisted the "call in" powers had helped the mayor "unblock strategic growth sites" in the capital.

Bristow said if he had a similar local plan it would be "much more light touch" than London.

In the 2024 general election, the Labour government promised to build 1.5 million homes in England by the end of the decade, but housebuilders have warned the target could be missed.

Pennycook said the government was "absolutely determined to stick with that ambition".

He acknowledged the target was "really stretching" but said nearly 180,000 children were in temporary accommodation and "any smaller target wouldn't be commensurate with the scale of the challenge".

Bristow said the government has "no chance whatsoever" to meet its 1.5 million target.

"We need economic growth in this country, we need to get building and families need places to live, and at the moment, the planning system just isn't working."

In addition to gaining the new "call-in" powers, mayors are set to be able to grant "up-front permission", which the government says will allow building to begin "without a developer having to apply".

A consultation on how the powers will work is due to be published next week.

The government has sought to stress that local councils will continue to decide the majority of applications and that all decisions must still follow planning rules.

It has also said mayors will get a "bigger say" over how housing funding is spent in their area, with the government directing national agency Homes England to focus on local mayors' priorities.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who served as mayor for Greater Manchester for nearly a decade, has repeatedly expressed his desire to transfer more powers to local mayors.

"Challenge does need to be made to local decision-making and actually it cuts both ways," he told the Sunday Times.

"Sometimes it's the other way round. It's the local authority putting forward something that's unacceptable in terms of the impact on the community. It's a two-way street."

Last month, Burnham promised to give all mayors a share of income tax revenue, saying he wanted to "bring power home" to "every postcode".

Earlier this week, he announced a secondment programme to send high-performing civil servants to work in mayoral offices.

The approach has faced criticism from some in his own party and the Liberal Democrats, who fear it could create a "two-tier system" that discriminates against those areas that do not have an elected mayor.

News.title: Restriction zone scheme for offenders to start in October
News.content:
A scheme that could see serious sexual and violent offenders confined to areas just a few miles wide after leaving prison will be launched in October, Justice Secretary Alex Norris has announced.

Government ministers say this is designed to give victims greater freedom and further reduce the possibility of unwanted contact

The intention to introduce "restriction zones" for violent offenders who leave prison and who are on probation was first announced by the government last year.

Probation officers will be able to limit where serious offenders can go for as long as it is deemed necessary. Those who breach their new boundaries could be recalled to prison.

This would go beyond the current practice of imposing "exclusion zones" which ban offenders from specific locations such as a victim's home or place of work.

Norris is expected to come up with proposals to further restrict the early release of some prisoners when Parliament resumes next month.

But the Conservatives say that the best thing Labour could do to protect victims is to bring forward emergency legislation which would stop the early release of thousands of criminals.

There is a risk that serious sexual and violent offenders and victims could encounter one another outside exclusion zones.

The new scheme will specify confined areas for offenders in plans tailored to them and developed in consultation with victims.

Norris said the scheme would use GPS technology monitored by probation officers so that "those who step outside the boundaries can be quickly identified and face being sent back to prison".

"Offenders should carry the consequences of their crimes, not their victims," he added.

Amy Glover, director of domestic abuse services at Advance, a charity supporting women and girls who have experienced domestic abuse, praised the "change in focus".

However, she also called for reform to the criminal justice system saying many survivors of abuse chose "not to pursue a criminal conviction, and for those that do only 5% reach conviction."

A domestic abuse survivor named only as Kristina called the restriction zones a "fantastic concept" but noted that a perpetrator had continuously breached her indefinite restraining order "without consequence".

"The biggest challenge would be to gain victims' confidence in authorities to follow through their promises of protection," she added.

The announcement of the restriction zone scheme's start date comes after a change to the government's early release scheme following a backlash.

Introduced to ease prison overcrowding, on 4 August the policy was updated so people sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming would not be eligible for early release.

The Prison Governors' association warned this change to plans at a "very late stage" put further pressure on prison staff.

The restriction zone scheme was criticised when it was announced last year for potentially putting pressure on probation staff, something the government says it hopes to alleviate with more staff and a greater use of technology.

If you are suffering from domestic abuse, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

The father of an American sailor serving aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln has been taken into federal immigration custody while his son is deployed in the Middle East, according to a statement posted online by the service member.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security stated on Sunday that U.S. Border Patrol officers apprehended Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, originally from Nicaragua, during a vehicle stop in Key West, Florida.

Joshua Aviles, the detained man's son, reflected on his situation in a Facebook message: "I've been deployed for over nine months, out at sea in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country that has given me everything."

open image in gallery The U.S. Navy Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, which is supporting U.S. military operations in the war with Iran, conducts a replenishment-at-sea with fleet replenishment oiler USNS Henry J. Kaiser, August 16 ( US Navy )

Relating how he received the news on Saturday, the sailor noted his father possessed a driver's license, Social Security card, and employment authorization. "I just got a call that my dad was taken by ICE," he wrote.

Aviles detailed the family's ongoing effort to legalize his father's status, writing: "We have done everything through immigration to get his green card approved, and we are just waiting. This is heartbreaking for me. I don't know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal,"

According to the DHS, Aviles Roa entered the U.S. unlawfully and will remain in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody pending removal proceedings. "Having a family member in the military is not a free pass to violate our nation's laws," the agency said.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump pictured with advisor Stephen Miller, largely seen as the architect of the administration’s immigration policy ( AFP/Getty )

President Donald Trump has defended the immigration measures as vital to domestic security. However, civil rights advocates contend the policies infringe on free speech and due process rights, exacerbating racial profiling concerns among ethnic minorities.

The aircraft carrier left the Middle East on Saturday after remaining at sea for more than 200 consecutive days without port access—a modern record that prompted inquiries from Democratic lawmakers after family complaints about shipboard conditions.

News.title: Cleveland police and crime commissioner condemns ‘absolutely idiotic’ wrong-way driving social media trend
News.content:
The Cleveland police and crime commissioner has condemned an “absolutely idiotic” social media trend showing people driving the wrong way down roads.

When asked about reports that at least one of the young men who died in a wrong-way collision Teesside early on Saturday (22 August) had been involved in filming dangerous driving in social media videos, Matt Storey told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “Without being able to say whether that was anything like involved in this case, it’s absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100 per cent focused on the road when they’re behind the wheel of a vehicle.”

The government has told TikTok and other social media companies to take down content related to the trend.

Shelley Fabares, the actor who spent decades as a television fixture from The Donna Reed Show in her youth to One Day at a Time and Coach, has died aged 82.

She passed away on Saturday in Los Angeles, her family said in a statement to The Associated Press. No cause of death was given.

“To her family and friends, Shelley was a source of love, strength, laughter, and comfort,” her family wrote. “She had a remarkable ability to make people feel welcomed, valued, and cared for.”

Fabares was born in Santa Monica, California, in 1944, and started acting as a young child. Her first television credit came at age 10 when she appeared on The Loretta Young Show.

open image in gallery She had been married to M*A*S*H actor Mike Farrell since 1984 ( Getty )

Many movies and television shows followed. She acted with Paul Newman, Frank Sinatra and Eva Marie Saint in a Producers Showcase production of Our Town; was in the Rosalind Russell movie The Girl Rush and the Rock Hudson drama Never Say Goodbye.

Other early credits include Annette, Captain Midnight and the “Black Leather Jackets” episode of The Twilight Zone.

Her biggest break came when she was cast as Mary Stone on The Donna Reed Show, where she was a regular from 1958 through 1963.

During that time she also got a recording contract and had two Top 40 hits including “Johnny Angel.”

In the early 1960s, she also co-starred in three movies with Elvis Presley: Girl Happy, Spinout and Clambake.

“I think the years on ‘The Donna Reed Show,’ the years from 14 to 19, were so incredibly important,” Fabares told the Los Angeles Times in 1993.

“Donna Reed was simply an extraordinary woman, a woman of great strength, kindness, integrity and compassion. I am not trying to make her sound like a saint, but she had the most profound influence on me. I carry her with me today.”

In the late 1970s, Fabares made an impression as Francine Webster on the CBS sitcom One Day at a Time. She also played James Caan’s wife in Brian’s Song.

One of her biggest roles came when she was cast as Christine Armstrong in Coach, although the show took a minute to find its audience.

open image in gallery Shelley Fabares attends The 22nd Annual Screen Actors Guild Awards Behind-The-Scenes Day 1 on January 28, 2016 ( Getty )

“I did always feel from the very beginning if they could find the right spot for us, this was a show that would last,” she said in the 1993 Los Angeles Times interview.

Fabares married twice, first to producer Lou Adler in 1964. She had been married to M*A*S*H actor Mike Farrell since 1984. She was also a devoted advocate for Alzheimer’s awareness, which affected her mother.

In early 1999, a visit to the emergency room for an esophageal bleed revealed that she had progressive liver failure. After spending 22 months on a waiting list, she had liver transplant surgery in October 2000.

In an interview with Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles three years after the transplant, she said she'd been “changed by the experience” and was eternally grateful to Farrell who was with her “every step of the way.”

Her family, in their statement, said “we will remember Shelley for her kindness, loyalty, wit, courage, and beautiful spirit. We will miss her deeply — not only as a celebrated performer, but as the loving and extraordinary person she was in our everyday lives.”

The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous “Hand of God” goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold for £2.5m at auction.

Maradona struck twice in a 2-0 quarter-final win in Mexico City 40 years ago, the first via his hand after beating English goalkeeper Peter Shilton to a ball in the box.

The Argentina captain added another, sublime solo goal soon afterwards as his side went on to secure World Cup glory.

open image in gallery Diego Maradona outjumped England goalkeeper Peter Shilton to score a controversial goal ( Getty )

The ball sold for $3.3m (£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday – though fell short of an expectation that it might command a figure of around $10m (£7.3m).

Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser, who refereed the match in 1986, collected the Adidas Azteca ball at full-time and kept it for more than three decades before selling it at auction in 2022 for $2.37m (£1.74m).

It was again listed at auction a year later, but did not sell as bids failed to match the minimum value.

Bin Nasser failed to spot Maradona’s misdeed, allowing the goal to stand and Argentina to progress. The No 10 told reporters after the game that it had been scored “a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".

A Chinese research institute located in the southwestern metropolis of Chengdu apologised on Monday for initially issuing a higher magnitude earthquake warning than what other monitors said occurred, sparking some panic among people.

China's Earthquake Networks Center said a 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck Yibin in southwest China's Sichuan province at 8.26am (0026GMT) on Monday.

However, the Institute of Care-Life, a Chengdu-based disaster reduction laboratory, issued a 7.7-magnitude earthquake alert just five seconds after the quake struck.

The institute used the name of the "China earthquake early warning network" – a seismic alert system developed by Care-Life – without authorisation to issue the 7.7-magnitude alert to the public through Honor and Vivo smartphones, as well as Xiaotiancai smartwatches, according to state-backed newspaper the ​Global Times.

A damaged building and cars (C) are seen after an earthquake at Liunan district in Liuzhou, China's southern Guangxi region ( AFP/Getty )

Addressing the significant discrepancy, it said that the network revised the ⁠estimate lower to 6.4 at the sixth second, 3.7 at the seventh second, 4.1 at the eighth second and 3.9 at the 16th second.

The Institute of Care-Life said it will investigate the cause for the deviation as soon as possible to improve its services. The false ⁠alert caused panic among many users, ‌the ​Global Times ‌said.

A magnitude-5.7 earthquake struck a remote province in China in July with a second quake of magnitude 5.8 following just 18 minutes later.

The earthquakes in Xinghai county in the northwestern Chinese province of Qinghai struck at 11.16am and 11.34am on Tuesday at a depth of 10 kilometres (6 miles), with the epicentre located in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area about 244 km (152 miles) from Xining, the capital of Qinghai.

In May, a 5.2-magnitude earthquake struck the south Guangxi region, killing two people, toppling buildings and triggering the evacuations of thousands.

Four others were injured, while more than 7,000 residents were evacuated from Liuzhou city.

Morrisons has promised shoppers it will match or beat the prices of its main supermarket competitors across hundreds of essential everyday products.

The "unbeatable prices" initiative, introduced on Monday, vows that the retailer will not be undercut by any of its five largest rivals. This pledge points to a potential escalation in the ongoing price war among UK grocers competing to attract customers.

Operating roughly 500 supermarkets and 1,700 convenience stores, Morrisons hopes the pricing strategy will help reverse recent declines in its market share.

According to Worldpanel figures for the 12 weeks to August, the company held an 8.5 per cent market share, making it the sixth-largest UK supermarket chain behind Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Asda, Aldi, and Lidl, which recently overtook it.

The promise will cover more than 500 weekly essentials, to ensure they can buy products at the same price or less than they would at rival stores.

The Bradford-based chain said it will guarantee low prices on fresh products including bananas, tomatoes and carrots, as well as staples such as bread, butter and chicken fillets.

Morrisons, which runs around 500 supermarkets and 1,700 convenience shops, will be hoping its pricing strategy can help drive a recovery in its share of the UK grocery market, which has slipped back in recent years

It also extends to fresh lines across the retailer’s Market Street counters, such as its fishmongers and bakeries.

It comes two years after Morrisons first launched a price match against hundreds of Aldi and Lidl products as part of its fightback against the German discounters.

Alex Paver, customer and marketing director at Morrisons, said: “Customers shouldn’t have to choose between great prices and great quality – and at Morrisons, they don’t have to.

“Our unbeatable price commitment means customers can trust that the prices on these products simply won’t be beaten by Asda, Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Aldi or Lidl.

“And uniquely at Morrisons, that unbeatable value comes alongside the quality, freshness and expert service we’re famous for – from bread baked fresh in store to food prepared by our skilled Market Street colleagues.”

It comes days after accounts showed that Morrisons shed almost 5,000 jobs last year as part of efforts by the private equity-backed grocer to shore up its finances and turn around its performance.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: Raphinha sparks frenzy with ‘Julian Alvarez’ celebration in Barcelona’s win over Elche
Sports.content:
RAPHINHA set tongues wagging with a Spider-Man celebration on the same day Julian Alvarez was heckled by Atletico Madrid fans.

Alvarez, whose nickname is La Araña (The Spider), has been trying to force his way out of Atleti this summer.



And Raphinha‘s Barca are one of multiple teams the Rojiblancos have turned away.

So it appeared telling that, on the same day Alvarez was given a hostile reception at the Metropolitano, Raphinha performed a celebration with the same Spider-Man hand gesture used by the Argentine after scoring Barca’s first goal in a 5-0 rout at Elche.



The conspiracy theories were busted by Raphinha’s wife after the game, however, as she revealed on Instagram that it was actually his son, Gael, who had requested the celebration.

Alvarez was jeered and whistled when he was brought on in the 67th minute of Sunday’s 2-2 draw with Villarreal.



And he was not even allowed to face the supporters after the game, with boss Diego Simeone admitting his dart down the tunnel was pre-planned.

He said: “It was a club decision to not let Julian Alvarez go over with his team-mates to greet the fans.”

Fans had been chanting during the game: “Get him out of here, tell him to get out of here.”

Evidently, Alvarez going public with his desire to leave Atletico has not gone down well.

Barca reportedly had an £85.6million bid for Alvarez turned down earlier this summer but they are now understood to be prioritising other targets.

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero’s son makes top-flight debut during Newcastle vs Liverpool
Sports.content:
ANDONI IRAOLA handed a league debut against Newcastle to a rising star with a name that will be familiar to Prem fans.

The Reds kicked off their competitive season with an emotionally-charged clash against Newcastle at St James’ Park.



The Magpies led the match twice but an injury-time penalty handed Dominik Szoboszlai the chance to equalise from the spot, sharing the points in the North East.

But while it was not the dream start to the season Liverpool as a whole were hoping for, it was a dream come true for young Lewis Koumas.



The 20-year-old winger arrived for his first Prem appearance as he was substituted on in the 78th minute in place of Ryan Gravenberch.

He didn’t get too much time on the ball, but was on the pitch to celebrate a memorable moment after the late penalty rescued a point with almost the last kick of the game.

It must have also been an equally special day for his dad, Premier League cult hero Jason Koumas.

The 46-year-old was himself released by Liverpool as an academy star, before making the switch to Tranmere Rovers.

He made over 100 appearances for the EFL side before joining Prem outfit West Brom.

He impressed in his first season with the club despite suffering relegation, winning their player of the season award.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He went on to add stints with Wigan and Cardiff in his native Wales.

He made 34 appearances for the nation, another avenue down which his son has followed him.

At 20, he already has 12 appearances for the Dragons, scoring his first goal in a friendly against Ghana in June.

While Sunday marked his first Premier League outing, he has already developed considerable experience in the English game after loans with Stoke, Birmingham and Hull over the past two seasons.

Sports.title: FA hammer a split-second handball but let West Ham’s Taty Castellanos off the hook despite blatant cheating — it’s crazy
Sports.content:
THE FA are living in cloud cuckoo land.

And their latest absurd retrospective ban proves just how out of touch they really are.



West Brom forward Aune Heggebo was slapped with a two-match suspension for “successfully deceiving a match official” after scoring against Norwich last weekend.

The ball deflected off the keeper and hit his arm just 0.1 seconds before going into the net.



It was an instinctive, split-second movement as he threw himself at the ball.

Did the ball hit his arm? Yes. Did Heggebo know much about it? Not a chance.



Yet the decision-makers in So decided Heggebo is a master fraudster.

Are we seriously suggesting Heggebo should have run up to the referee and confessed?

Can you imagine the outrage from Baggies fans if he marched over and said: “Sorry ref, I handled it”?

He would not have been a popular figure in his dressing room, that is for sure.

We all love to remember former West Ham star Paolo Di Canio catching the ball instead of scoring when Everton keeper Paul Gerrard went down injured.

Robbie Fowler once famously tried to persuade a ref not to give a penalty against Arsenal.

Those moments of supreme sportsmanship are wonderful — but let’s get real.

By banning Heggebo, the FA are setting a bizarre precedent where players are effectively expected to self-referee on the pitch.

Are we really moving toward a game where a striker faces a multi-match ban unless he immediately stops play and admits to an accidental touch?



Modern footballers dive constantly and try to deceive officials every single week.

Take West Ham striker Taty Castellanos against Charlton on Saturday.

The Argentine took a blatant, pre-meditated dive inside the box to try and win a penalty. He was correctly booked by referee Andrew Kitchen for simulation.

Taty knew exactly what he was doing long before his boots left the turf. His intent to cheat the official and the opposition was 100 per cent clear.

So how on earth is an involuntary handball judged worse than a deliberate dive?



The only difference is that Taty was unsuccessful in his attempt to fool the ref.

Why should a player escape serious punishment just because the referee caught him in the act?

If the FA are truly serious about stamping out deceit, intent must be punished severely.



Taty’s yellow card for that shameless plunge should be retroactively upgraded to a red.

Instead, the rulemakers let deliberate cheaters off with a slap on the wrist while hammering accidental handballs.

It is absolute madness from blazers who simply do not understand the reality of professional football.

There is no VAR in the Championship and most fans, myself included, agree that is a good thing.

We accept human error as part of the natural rhythm of the game.



West Ham’s Konstantinos Mavropanos appeared to be fouled before Charlton scored their second goal at the London Stadium. With VAR, that goal may have been chalked off.

Yet we take the rough with the smooth because the alternative is endless delays.

But if the FA are going to sit in offices on Monday morning re-refereeing matches, what is the point?

If they are going to hand out stupid retrospective bans, they might as well just bring in VAR.

This half-baked middle ground is creating the absolute worst of both worlds for EFL clubs.



Did Heggebo intend to cheat? No. Did Taty intend to cheat? Absolutely.

It is time the FA stopped punishing split-second accidents and started cracking down on actual cheats.

And the latest gem to be plucked out of nowhere is striker Taïryk Arconte. The Guadeloupe international looks unplayable, proving once again that while rivals splash millions on big names, the Lions quietly find proper talent.

How much more pain for Leicester?

RUSSELL MARTIN is putting Leicester through early pain after back-to-back defeats has left them reeling in League One.

The new boss is facing serious heat as his signature style stutters out of the blocks at the King Power Stadium.

Martin always seems to put his teams through torture early on, as Southampton fans know only too well.



He eventually steered them to promotion — but how much patience will Leicester fans have?

Crashing into the third tier was already a bitter pill to swallow.

Now watching their side drop six points from six has alarm bells ringing loudly across the East Midlands.

My view is — especially in the third tier — pragmatic football is the best way to go.

Sports.title: Fans claim Enzo Maresca is COPYING Pep Guardiola after spotting Man City manager’s passionate antics after first game
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE fans have claimed that Enzo Maresca was imitating Pep Guardiola after Manchester City’s Premier League opener on Sunday.

The former Chelsea boss was appointed the successor to Guardiola after Pep’s incredible decade-long Prem journey came to an end last season.



The Italian tactician managed to get off to a winning start after a stunning late comeback against Bournemouth at the Etihad.

The Cherries took an early lead through Marcus Tavernier, but an 84th-minute Marc Guehi equaliser and an injury time winner from Josko Gvardiol reversed the host’s fortunes late on.



But during the considerable post-match celebrations, Maresca was spotted speaking to some of his players in a way that reminded fans of Guardiola’s iconic mannerisms.

The 46-year-old – who wore a suit for the match – was especially animated as he gestured at and put an arm around Rayan Cherki, before leading him away from cameras on the pitch.



Guardiola was also known for his energetic conversations with his own players on the pitch after matches, especially ones that he was frustrated with.

Fans were convinced that Maresca was trying to ‘copy’ his predecessor’s style.

One disgruntled fan of former club Chelsea wrote: “Such a poor attempt trying to mimic Guardiola’s post-match talks with his players. Temu Pep.”

Another added: “He never did this at Chelsea and he never wore a suit on the touchline trying too hard to be Pep.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

While a City fan joked: “I genuinely thought this was a clip from last season.”

It seemed he emulated Pep not just in outfit but in results, with the win snapping Bournemouth’s 18-game unbeaten run in the competition – the longest across Europe’s top five leagues going into the contest.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Jaissle brutally shuts down Schmeichel on live TV after he claims Man Utd are in for Lewis Hall transfer
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE boss Matthias Jaissle shot down Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel’s suggestion Lewis Hall could still leave this summer.

The German head coach got his first point in the Premier League on Sunday in a dramatic opening weekend draw with Liverpool – and Hall gave away a stoppage time penalty.



Dominik Szoboszlai ruthlessly converted to salvage the score at 2-2, but it was Jaissle and Newcastle who impressed the most.

Despite barely being in the job two weeks, the former RB Salzburg head coach had his depleted squad perform admirably on an emotional day at St James’ Park.



And Hall, subject to much transfer speculation over the past few months, was one of the standouts – until his last gasp blunder.

The England defender, who brutally missed out on World Cup selection, fouled Victor Munoz with just seconds to play.



He was gutted at full-time but had kept Liverpool quiet until then.

And Jaissle is determined to keep the ex-Chelsea academy ace in the North East.

When discussing his plans for the rest of the window, Jaissle admitted: “I think it will be a stressful period for the sporting director [Ross Wilson].

“We have some needs, definitely.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He was then urged to say where upgrades would fit in, and started to answer, “Position wise…” before stopping himself.

Schmeichel, on punditry duty for Viaplay, laughed: “You can tell us.”

And Jaissle replied: “Because you ask, I was about to tell you but I [will] keep it a secret.”

He added: “If you are bringing players in, maybe there will also be some players out.”

United icon Schmeichel then interjected to say: “We’re [Manchester United] looking at your left-back.”



But Jaissle gave the idea short shrift, jumping in and grinning as he said: “No chance! No chance!”

Hall, 21, has been linked with a move away from the Toon for a while – and that has only intensified with United’s expected focus on a left-back over the next week.

SunSport understands that the youngster would find it hard to turn down a switch to Old Trafford – but any deal would be extremely expensive.

Newcastle signed Hall from Chelsea in 2023 on loan before making it permanent for £32million 12 months later.



Now he is established as one of the league’s best left-backs, but has seen a host of key team-mates depart when some have questioned the ambition and direction of the Saudi Arabian project.

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon as well as midfield pair Bruno Guimaraes (club captain at the time) and Sandro Tonali.

Last year Alexander Isak joined Liverpool on deadline day.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But reports say Hall is set to be offered an enormous new contract in order to tie him down.

And Jaissle is willing to make him part of a new-look leadership group including Big Dan Burn.

Sports.title: I managed both Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck – here’s why they are the smartest of transfers for Chelsea
Sports.content:
GOLDEN oldies Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck will do what Chelsea legend John Terry did and galvanise Blues’ young guns.

That is the verdict of Prem legend Steve Bruce who managed both the dynamic duo during their Sunderland days — and Terry at Aston Villa.



As far as former Manchester United skipper Bruce is concerned, there is simply no substitute for experience.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso signed midfielder Henderson, 36, and striker Welbeck, 35, from Brentford and Brighton respectively this summer.



Bruce saw first hand the benefits of having a wise old head after luring centre-back Terry to Villa on a free in the twilight of his career in 2017.

The former England skipper was 36 and able to provide vital know-how to the then Championship side to get the club moving in the right direction again.

Bruce said: “The prospect of Chelsea getting Jordan and Danny at their age was deemed daft by some but for me they’re the smartest of signings.

“It’s a bold move but also a very, very shrewd move by Xabi Alonso to bring in two relatively old heads.

“And I wasn’t surprised at all that they’ve been snapped up because I brought in John Terry to do exactly the same thing — bring leadership to a young group at Villa.

“This is Alonso stamping his mark on the club because young players often need the voice of experience beside them. It’s clear Chelsea have recognised the merits of a better blend which bodes well for them.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And after being handed the captaincy by Bruce, JT galvanised Villa and ended up playing 36 games, finishing with a heartbreaking play-off final defeat by Fulham, Chelsea’s opponents in their Prem opener tonight.

Bruce explained: “As well as defensive qualities, I wanted John to influence the players in terms of how to train and what you needed to do to reach the top and stay there.

“And I have to say JT was inspiring — he set standards and was a real breath of fresh air as a role model, and the younger players relished following his example.

“Villa were still fighting back after being relegated and there was lots of doom and gloom.

“It needed someone like JT to show the players the way forward and lead by example on and off the field.



“He brought drive to the dressing room and that’s invaluable to managers.

“In a similar way, Chelsea’s dressing room will look up to Jordan and Danny for what they’ve achieved and the type of pros they are and that will pay dividends.

“It’s a real statement of intent and a priority is clearly to bring stability to his dressing room.

“And there’s no better way to do it than to bring in two of the English game’s finest elder statesmen, so to speak.

“All the young players at Chelsea will look up to these two in admiration and learn vital lessons and they’ll create a feeling of togetherness.



“They have thought the average age of the squad is too much on the young side and Danny and Jordan will redress the balance with experience.

“They’ve gone out and signed two seasoned Premier League campaigners who will lead from the front.

“They won’t play 50 games but they look after themselves, and if they get 25 to 30 games under their belt they’ll have done their jobs.”

Bruce worked with the pair fairly on in their careers.

Henderson was coming through the ranks at Sunderland and Bruce’s United connections got rising star Welbeck to Wearside on loan for the 2010-11 campaign.



And they combined to fabulous effect at Stamford Bridge as Sunderland chief Bruce masterminded a stunning 3-0 win on November 14, 2010.

Bruce added: “The reason Jordan got into the first team was based on his leadership qualities, even as a youngster.

“Even though he was just 18, he helped the more experienced players work their way through the challenges of pre-season.

“That ability to lead by example got him in the team and kept him in the team and earned him a move to Liverpool where he won the lot.



“It’s one thing being driven and being a good pro, you’ve also got to have technical ability and he’s shown he’s got it in abundance time and time again for club and country.

“He made the best of his natural ability due to hunger, desire and commitment to better himself. And there’s still that determination to succeed which was there for all to see when he was a teenager.

“His potential was vast and over the years at Liverpool, Jordan proved to be a hell of a signing by Kenny Dalglish.

“You can’t deny anyone the chance to move to a club of Liverpool’s stature and he grabbed the opportunity with both hands and became a mainstay of the side.



“To keep himself in such good nick for so long is down to his desire, which is born in you, and his commitment to his profession.”

Bruce tried to bring in Welbeck when he was Hull boss but he joined Arsenal in 2014.

He said: “I always felt that Manchester United got rid of Danny too quickly.

“He’s got the lot as a forward, two good feet, clever movement, good finishing ability, and what’s key is he seems to be getting better with age.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca fires clear transfer message to Man City board after fielding shock lineup in first game for club
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA played Marc Guehi as a makeshift midfielder in perhaps a pointed message to Manchester City’s board.

City are on the brink of an £86million deal for Lille wonderkid Ayyoub Bouaddi but Maresca wants more players in the engine room.



Maresca was forced into finding a “solution” after Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders left the club, while Nico Gonzalez is linked with Newcastle.

England centre-back Guehi scored City’s equaliser as new boss Maresca oversaw a comeback 2-1 win over Bournemouth, with Mateo Kovacic on the bench.



Maresca said: “I had to find a solution. I don’t know if Marc can play there for the next game again. Now we need a different solution.

“I know Marc from Crystal Palace and I always thought he could be a good midfielder. So sometimes you visualise things you need to try.”

Maresca revealed he planned to “see the board” following the final whistle, unaware that City were already on the verge of landing Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old, who starred for Morocco at the World Cup, is set to become the most expensive teenage signing in Prem history, beating the £59.9m rivals United paid for Leny Yoro from the same club in 2024.

City, who signed Elliot Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest, want Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez while Adam Wharton of Crystal Palace and Roma’s Manu Kone have also been on the club’s wishlist.

As well as Guehi, Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola this summer, also picked full-back Nico O’Reilly in an attacking midfielder role.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Asked if City have finally tracked down a “new Rodri“, a deadpan Maresca said: “Marc Guehi.” It brought a laugh, but relying on an England defender in central midfield is clearly no long-term fix.

Maresca celebrated his first Prem win as City boss, but admitted plenty of work needs to be done before the window closes on September 1.

The Italian added: “At the moment I don’t have a best XI but day by day I can see more clearly.”

City survived a late scare while a freshly trimmed Erling Haaland had a close shave of his own, drawing a blank on opening day for the first time in his Premier League career.

Maresca revealed Rayan Cherki was “not happy” about being benched — before coming on to deliver an “unbelievable impact” with two assists to spark City’s thrilling turnaround.



Maresca turned to blow kisses at his family in the stands after Josko Gvardiol‘s stoppage time winner was given after VAR overturned the on-field officials offside call.

The former Chelsea boss, who watched as a section of fans unearthed a welcoming tifo at kick-off, said: “It was the perfect day. I was very emotional.

“I was very pleased when the game started to watch the banner on the other side. I was happy at the end because we walked away with three points.”

City forward Omar Marmoush was on the bench ahead of a potential move to Spurs, while Jack Grealish was brought on in the final eight minutes and was serenaded by the home crowd in what could have been his final match for the club, with a return to Everton looming.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maresca said: “He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best from him. The window is open for one more week and we will see what happens.”



Asked where he will play next week, Guehi jested: “Who knows? Maybe up front. We’ll see.”

Sports.title: Arsenal star Christos Tzolis kicks off derby for his former club and is given hero’s welcome by fans
Sports.content:
NEW Arsenal fan favourite Christos Tzolis “kicked off” for another team just days after his Premier League debut.

The Greek winger, who joined the Gunners for £34million earlier this summer, made the most of some time off following Friday’s 3-0 win over Coventry.



He returned to former side Club Brugge over the weekend and got a standing ovation from fans.

Tzolis, 24, was paraded in front of the Jan Breydel Stadium despite leaving barely a month ago.



And after getting a rapturous pre-match reception, he took a fake kick-off ahead of the Brugge derby.

Played between Club and Cercle, who both have home games at the same ground, Tzolis returned to the stands to watch his ex-team-mates come away with three points.

They won 1-0 and continued their 100 per cent start to the league campaign.

Although still early on in his Prem and Arsenal career, Tzolis has become an immediate hit at the Emirates after a sparkling opening performance and strong pre-season showings.



He spent just two years in Belgium after arriving from Dusseldorf – where he moved following a forgettable spell at Norwich.

And Tzolis was an output machine, scoring 43 times in 108 appearances with 45 assists.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Last season alone he bagged 17 times with a staggering 23 assists in just 36 league outings.

He rocked up in Brugge in a white t-shirt and a giant smile on his face.

Wearing several bracelets on his right wrist, Tzolis had his name sung by the Brugge faithful.



He even shook hands with the ref as Cercle and Club lined up on either side of the pitch.

In baggy black trousers and white trainers, he turned to all sections of the crowd and applauded.

Patting his chest with his hand, Tzolis was given the match ball and placed it on the centre circle.

The ref blew a fake starting whistle and Tzolis kicked it back to Club Brugge and got another big cheer.

He put his arms in the air before heading off the pitch and embracing with boss Ivan Leko.



Tzolis also got a touch from the mascot.
