Unai Emery hinted that Ollie Watkins refused to play in Aston Villa's humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brighton as the saga surrounding the striker's future turned sour. Watkins, 30, was absent for Sunday's drubbing, with Villa conceding all four goals inside the opening 31 minutes before going down to 10 men.

‌



It was a nightmare start to a Premier League season ahead of which Villa have lost several key players. Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne have all left the Europa League winners for pastures new.

‌



And their rebuild looks set to get even tougher, as Watkins pushes to join Al-Hilal. The Saudi Pro League side have agreed personal terms with the England international, although they've seen four bids rejected.

‌



Al-Hilal's most recent offer came in at £45million and it's thought that £50m would be enough for Villa to accept. But Emery said that 'silence' was the best way to respond to questions regarding Watkins' future and whether he refused to be involved on Sunday.

Sports.title: UEFA chief Aleksandr Ceferin destroys Gianni Infantino over FIFA sale saga – 'Plan is dead'
Sports.content:
UEFA chief Aleksandr Ceferin destroys Gianni Infantino over FIFA sale saga – 'Plan is dead'

Gianni Infantino has come under increased scrutiny since the 2026 World Cup after controversially plotting to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms before he backed down

View 2 Images Aleksandr Ceferin and Gianni Infantino do not see eye to eye (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has hit out at Gianni Infantino over his ill-fated plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms. The Swiss Italian is under growing pressure after his controversial idea sparked global outrage.

‌



The move saw European football's governing body, UEFA, threaten to boycott all FIFA events, including the World Cup. Infantino was eventually forced to withdraw his plan, but pressure on the 56-year-old has not gone away.

‌



UEFA were joined by Concacaf, the federation for football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, as well as the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), in a joint letter accusing FIFA of a "fundamental breach of trust" and "deception".

‌



Trent Alexander-Arnold delivers brutal verdict on World Cup sell off plan READ MORE :

Jean-Philippe Mateta calls in FIFA in bid to rip up Crystal Palace contract READ MORE :

European football's governing body has since said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while the football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for the former UEFA general secretary.

And Ceferin has spoken strongly to the Rest is Politics podcast on why Infantino's decision was so flawed. The Slovenian believes it was worse than the controversial European Super League plan, which saw Europe's biggest club sides threaten to break away before it collapsed in April 2021.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said: "I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan.

"Super important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong, and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

"I'm absolutely sure that the plan is dead. It's hard to to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone. We will not allow that to happen."

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Ceferin claims that UEFA had no prior knowledge of Infantino's plan. The 58-year-old says he learned about it through the media while on holiday with his family.

"He didn't contact me since this happened," Ceferin said. "They [FIFA] play on, you know, '[how] arrogant Europe is against us: They have enough money, but I help the small and the poor'.

‌



"But I think someone should remind him that he is a European, and that he was supported by UEFA, which he forgot."

Questions are now being raised over a potential successor to Infantino ahead of FIFA's presidential election in March. However, Ceferin has ruled himself out.

"I'm not interested because of two reasons," the UEFA president said. "One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point it's time also to enjoy life a bit.

‌



"And the second point is, my credibility is much, much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position."

Sports.title: Lewis Hall transfer response live on TV shows Newcastle's true stance over Man Utd move
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall transfer response live on TV shows Newcastle's true stance over Man Utd move

Newcastle United left‑back Lewis Hall has been linked with a move to Manchester United this summer, but the Magpies have stood firm

Jaissle initially misinterpreted the remark, before responding: "No chance! No chance!" The German could not have been more emphatic - Hall is not for sale. Hall remains one of the most highly regarded young full‑backs in the Premier League, widely viewed as a future England regular.

Nevertheless, having already parted with Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, it's extremely doubtful Newcastle would offload Hall this summer, with merely days remaining of the window.

Carrick's side are seeking to strengthen the left-back position in their squad, but now appear as though they'll need to identify other alternatives. Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde is amongst those being touted for a switch to Old Trafford, and was notably absent from their squad for Sunday night's clash with Elche.

Barca manager Hansi Flick addressed that absence and said: "I spoke with Alejandro Balde today and said to him that I think you're not here 100%, so it's best that you stay at home and clear your mind. We will talk again tomorrow.

‌

"But I have NOT told Alejandro Balde to leave. I spoke with him this morning, I told him to think about it and that we'll talk again tomorrow."

‌



Hall played the full match against Liverpool, but his afternoon soured when he brought down Victor Munoz in the penalty area.

Speaking on Sky Sports commentary duty, Gary Neville said: "There was no touch on the ball, and it looked like a penalty - and it is. Hall has been incredible but that is not going to be overturned.

"One thing I recognised straightaway was there was no touch on the ball. It looked like a penalty right away. Lewis Hall in all parts of this game, against Munoz and Ngumoha, has moved his feet. He’s not taken the lazier option to stand there and just put his leg out.

‌



"He’s got low, he’s been really sharp in his defending and in the final seconds… I think Hall knows deep inside that it was a penalty."

Dominik Szoboszlai's late penalty earned Liverpool a share of the spoils at St James' Park.

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes demand over Liverpool duo after dire display - 'We've been kind to them'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville makes demand over Liverpool duo after dire display - 'We've been kind to them'

Liverpool stars Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak both failed to make an impact as the Reds had to settle for a 2-2 draw against Newcastle at St James' Park on Sunday

View 3 Images Gary Neville issued a warning (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has told Liverpool stars Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to 'sort themselves out' and justify their huge price tags. The Reds duo were among the weakest performers for Andoni Iraola's side, who needed a stoppage-time penalty to snatch a 2-2 draw away to Newcastle in their opening Premier League game on Sunday.

‌



Isak, who joined Liverpool from Newcastle last summer for a record-breaking £125million, missed two big chances and only had six touches in the opposition box. Meanwhile, £115m signing Wirtz - one of Europe's most sought-after players before his move from Bayer Leverkusen - was hooked on the hour mark after failing to put his stamp on the game.

‌



Both players had difficult first seasons at Liverpool, who sacked Arne Slot in May and appointed Iraola in the hope that the former Bournemouth boss will get the best out of them. But if that doesn't happen, they've been warned that they'll face a pile-on.

‌



Speaking on his Gary Neville Podcast, the Manchester United legend said: "The big thing for Liverpool is they've got this quarter-of-a-billion-pound front two, Isak and Wirtz and bloody hell, we've been kind to them.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"They're going to have to start playing sooner or later or else, to be fair, they're going to get quite a lot of criticism. For a start, they're too nice, and if you're going to be nice, you'd better be incredible at football.

"I don't see the tenacity in Wirtz in particular. I just see a nice player moving around the pitch, not really ever looking like he's busting a gut to do anything.

"Now, that can happen. Sometimes players have that flow about them, but I want to put a rocket up him. I want to put a rocket up him because there's ability there, there's talent there, the understanding of his position.

‌



"The biggest disappointment for me [Sunday] is those two." Neville added: "I've watched them both for 12 months, and I do actually have faith in them.

"I think Isak's an exceptional player and we've seen it. I never saw anybody give Gabriel [Magalhaes] and [William] Saliba or [Virgil] Van Dijk and [Ibrahima] Konate a tougher time as Isak did when he played at Newcastle in a black and white shirt.

Do you agree with Gary Neville? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



3 View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was subbed off against Newcastle (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images Alexander Isak didn't get on the scoresheet (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

"I've seen him be devastating. Now Liverpool fans and his team-mates and coaching staff, they need to see that - because that's £125m they've spent on him.

‌



"And then Wirtz, he needs to sort himself out. Enough's enough now, we've talked about him enough. He's young and he's come to a different country - and I'm all for willing him on.

"They have both had a bit of a free ride. Obviously Isak was injured last season but Arne Slot loses his job, and Wirtz has played like that, so let's be clear, this has got me to start some real focus now.

"I can see a real player there, but can't keep watching this stuff and he's been subbed after an hour and they need a goal, but they're 2-1 down, so no that's not right."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Fresh Julian Alvarez meeting held as update issued on £85m target
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Fresh Julian Alvarez meeting held as update issued on £85m target

A big development has emerged in Arsenal's pursuit of Atletico Madrid superstar Julian Alvarez

View 2 Images Arsenal are still pursuing Julian Alvarez (Image: Getty )

Arsenal’s pursuit of two elite forwards made headlines this weekend. After ending their 22-year Premier League trophy drought last term, the north Londoners appear to be on course for another stellar season.

‌



They began the 2026/27 campaign by blowing away Manchester City in the Community Shield earlier this month. Mikel Arteta’s men then sent out a clear message by dismantling Coventry City in their Premier League opener last Friday, making it two 3-0 victories from their first two competitive fixtures of the campaign.

‌



Having already boasted a strong enough squad to reach the Champions League final last term while challenging for the league, Arsenal made a clear effort to strengthen this summer through the transfer market. Sporting director Andrea Berta successfully brought in five players worth a combined £200million - and the Gunners have been rewarded with stellar performances.

‌



Yet, Arteta believes the final piece of the jigsaw puzzle before the window closes on September 1 is a world-class forward, who has so far eluded him. Here, Mirror Football brings you the latest regarding the English champions’ pursuit of Julian Alvarez and Kenan Yildiz.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Granit Xhaka confirms how close he came to Chelsea transfer after Xabi Alonso talks READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez meeting held

Fabrizio Romano reports that Arsenal officials met with Atletico Madrid in London on Friday over a potential deal for Alvarez. The Argentine forward is widely reported to be Arteta’s dream signing this summer but several obstacles have prevented the Gunners from getting their man up to now.

‌



The 26-year-old is desperate to leave Atletico but has always been clear that his preference is to sign for Barcelona. Atletico, meanwhile, insist they will not sell their talisman to a La Liga rival, and would demand a substantial club record-breaking fee from Arsenal if the player even agrees to join the north Londoners.

Romano has now detailed the talks that unfolded between Atleti and Arsenal late last week, stating that Alvarez hasn’t rejected the English champions despite wanting Barcelona. Arsenal are said to be respectful of that fact and know any deal would be expensive.

The Italian journalist claims Arsenal made it clear they want to be kept updated by both the club and player on any changes in the next seven days before the window shuts, so that they can re-enter negotiations if an opportunity presents itself. Amid his stand-off with club bosses, Alvarez was included in Diego Simeone’s squad to face Villarreal on Sunday.

‌

Arsenal’s hunt for a marquee forward signing has also led them to pursue Yildiz, though their hopes of bringing in the Juventus talisman have now reportedly ended. The Turkey international, 21, is said to be another one of Arteta’s dream acquisitions and has been a long-term target.

‌



The Gunners are even understood to be willing to pay £85m for his services. But Juventus are in a strong position, given Yildiz only signed a four-year contract extension in February.

Manager Luciano Spalletti has now thrown cold water on the growing rumours surrounding Yildiz’s potential move to north London. "I am perfectly relaxed, because dealing with Yildiz is easy for me,” Spalletti said at a press conference held ahead of Juventus’ Serie A opener at Frosinone on Sunday.

"They can offer whatever they like, I want Yildiz here and will always put him on the field. He's a perfect lad to talk to, he's mature, and knows he doesn't need to rush anything.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser

Alexander Isak and Liverpool snatched a late point at Newcastle, where the Swedish striker faced a hostile reception on his return to St James' Park

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was public enemy No 1 on his return to Newcastle

Alexander Isak offered a little wink as he left the St James' Park pitch after Liverpool rescued a point at Newcastle.

‌



The Swede was back at his former home for the first time since forcing his exit from the Magpies, and he was widely booed by the home crowd. They jeered his every error but the striker was able to celebrate a late equaliser with his team-mates.

‌



Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty in the 99th minute made the game 2-2 late on, denying Newcastle the three points. Isak led the line for Liverpool but found it hard to impact the game. The forward's best chance came in the second-half when he fired in a shot from the edge of the box.

‌



It blazed over, with the Newcastle fans taking great joy in cheering his miss. Isak was able to avoid losing on his return to Newcastle and offered a wink after the final whistle, reports the Chronicle.

Given the acrimonious nature of his exit from the north east Andoni Iraola admits he knew a hostile reception was coming from those who used to cheer his name.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Liverpool boss said: "I think he expected a little bit the atmosphere, I don't think [it] has been a big surprise for him. I think he has tried everything, has given us good positions on the ball.

"[He] probably has had a couple of situations to finish inside the box, but probably not the clearest that he wanted or we wanted, but I value that. He has continued pushing on in the game, fighting, and I think it's a good step for Alex for being the first game."

Once Liverpool were awarded the stoppage time penalty attention turned to who may take it, especially with Mohamed Salah now gone. Isak was a contender but in the end Szoboszlai stepped up, and hammered home emphatically.

‌



View 2 Images The Swede had struggled to impact the game on Sunday afternoon

Iraola insists Liverpool could go in a number of directions with their penalty taker, but praised the quality of his Hungarian midfielder. He said: "I think we have not only Dom and Alexander [Isak] – we have more very good specialists. Alexis [Mac Allister] also was on the pitch and he's a very good penalty-taker, Cody – we have a lot. But I think Dom showed the level. It's an almost impossible penalty to stop.

"I was happy obviously because at the end we recovered one point. I also think there is a clearer penalty before the Victor [Munoz] one to Victor again, but I think the referee whistles just before, so they cannot give it to you, but I think it was even more clear than the second one. I'm happy also for Victor because he has created problems to his opposition and I think these players from the bench that can alter games are going to be important for us."

Sports.title: Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer

Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move away from Atletico Madrid and the Arsenal target was booed by his own fans during the 2-2 draw with Villarreal on Sunday

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. (Image: (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Diego Simeone says it was planned that Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez would not stand with his teammates to show appreciation to Atletico Madrid supporters after the full time whistle on Sunday. The forward was jeered off the pitch by his own fans and had to be escorted down the tunnel by club staff after Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

‌



Alvarez forward has been heavily linked with a departure from Simeone's squad throughout the summer transfer window. The club turned down an approach from city rivals Real Madrid at the start of the window, before Barcelona made their intentions clear that they were keen to snap up Alvarez.

‌



The former Manchester City star has made no secret of his desire to leave the club, publicly declaring his wish to join the reigning La Liga champions. However, Atleti have stood firm in their refusal to sell to their domestic rivals, leaving Alvarez increasingly frustrated.

‌



Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'contacted' by Mikel Arteta as Arsenal transfer response given READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alvarez was named amongst the substitutes for the 2-2 draw with Villarreal, entering the fray in the second half to a chorus of boos from the home faithful. He played his part as ten-man Atletico fought back to salvage a point, yet was met with a hostile reception from his own supporters throughout his time on the pitch.

Alvarez was led down the tunnel by staff while his teammates went over to applaud the supporters at the final whistle. As he departed the pitch, Alvarez was once again subjected to jeers and whistles, casting further uncertainty over his future at the club.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal continue to pursue a transfer for Julian Alvarez (Image: (Photo by Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

Addressing the situation, Simeone said: "It was a club decision to not let Julian Alvarez go over with his teammates to greet the fans."

Ahead of the match, the Atleti manager said: "For me, Julian is an extremely important player for us to achieve our objectives. As long as he's with the team, I'm going to look after him."

‌



Arsenal are believed to be strongly interested in securing the striker's services as they look to strengthen Mikel Arteta's squad. The Gunners are aiming to defend their Premier League title and go one step further by lifting the Champions League trophy.

Landing Alvarez would send out a powerful message of intent, and according to reports emerging from Spain, Arsenal could be the sole remaining route for the Argentine frontman should he wish to depart the club.

Alvarez's remarks about joining Barcelona have sparked a fierce backlash, with posters appearing around Atleti's training ground on Friday morning reading "JULIAN FUERA" ("JULIAN OUT") and featuring the striker's No. 19 crossed out.

Sports.title: Brighton fan dies after Aston Villa win as club chief speaks on 'heartbreaking' incident
Sports.content:
Brighton fan dies after Aston Villa win as club chief speaks on 'heartbreaking' incident

Brighton secured an emphatic win over Aston Villa to begin their Premier League season but a fan was taken unwell as he left the Amex, later dying despite the efforts of the emergency services

View Image A Brighton fan was taken ill after Sunday's win and later died

A Brighton fan who attended their Premier League win over Aston Villa has died, the club have confirmed.

‌



The Seagulls enjoyed the perfect start to their campaign as they hammered Unai Emery's side on Sunday, recording a 4-0 win. However the club have since confirmed that a fan felt unwell as he left the Amex, but the emergency services couldn't save him.

‌



A Brighton statement read: “Following today’s game against Aston Villa, sadly a 72-year-old male Brighton & Hove Albion supporter passed away after the match. The gentleman took unwell as he was leaving the stadium to board a supporters’ club bus in the coach park. Despite the best efforts of emergency services and club staff, the medical team were unable to save him.

‌



“South East Coast Ambulance Service paramedics, St John’s Ambulance, Sussex Police, MB Medical Solutions, the club’s crowd doctor and our stewards worked together to ensure the individual was given the best possible care, including prolonged CPR on the scene.”

Sports.title: Meet the Filipino tennis superstar-in-waiting with a punch to rival Pacquiao's
Sports.content:
"Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.

The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Alex Eala against Jessica Pegula in Washington

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.

Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

Her remarkable run of victories mark her down out as a ​dangerous outsider for the US Open, starting August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

"It's an incredible milestone for me," said Eala, who moved to Spain to attend the Rafa Nadal Academy on a scholarship at the age of 13. "Coming into the tournament, I knew that the competition was super strong and my draw was quite tough. Every match was a ‌different set of obstacles. I'm really proud.

"I ended the tournament in better shape than I started. Each match I kept improving and kept learning things about myself. So it definitely gives me ‌a lot of confidence.

"It's really nice to see all the things I've been working on off court or during training being implemented in matches."

Rise of the Filipino superstar-in-waiting

As Eala's reputation grew, so ​too did her following, with large groups of Filipino fans packing ​the stands at tournaments around the world to back a player many see ​as a pioneer for tennis in their country.

Her popularity - like Pacquiao in his heyday - was evident in the final ⁠of the WTA 500 event in Washington. By the time the tournament ended, the phrase written across the Nike T-shirt she had worn earlier that week had become a reality: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped."

Sky Sports analyst Annabel Croft believes Eala can be one of the "biggest stars" and is "just what the tour needs" following her success in Washington.

The former British No 1 said: "I've never seen anything like it. The stadium, you could not get a seat. The noise, the excitement levels, and she just takes it all in her stride. And you could see in Washington what she brings to the court and she plays with such grace.

"There's a certain class about her. I love her attitude. I love the way she goes after the ball. She's a very deceptive tennis player. Being a lefty, she's quite awkward, but that forehand it's not a huge strike, but it does damage."

Image: Eala has a similar serve to 2018 Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber

Croft has likened Eala's serve to that of former Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber who relied heavily on her left-handed spin, placement, and variation.

She said: "I would imagine that she has built up some kind of locker-room respect right now where you build a certain aura and then that counts for quite a lot on the tour as well because players don't want to face you because of the record that she's building up.

"There's something awkward about a lefty serve, a little bit like Kerber. I remember she didn't have a big serve, but it was so well placed into the court. But also when you put a lot of spin on it and it sometimes has less pace on it, you're forcing your opponents to generate pace and they start to get a bit jittery.

"She keeps notching up the big wins, but she's also backing up the pressure wins.

"She plays under a lot of pressure with all of that excitement from the Filipino community. They turn out in their droves to watch her. That for some people would be a pressure, but she embraces it. She loves it."

Asked whether Eala could be a contender at the US Open, Croft said: "She's obviously somebody who enjoys being on a big stage. There will be a lot of players that won't want to face her because she's very in form. And I think the hard courts really suit her game."

Eala partnered American tennis legend Venus Williams in the doubles in Toronto this month, resuming their pairing from the Bad Homburg Open in Germany earlier this year.

Williams had high praise for Eala, saying: "Alex is a world star. She's just incredible. Besides the fact of her tennis, she's an incredible person, well spoken, and just an impressive young lady."

Image: Eala has the potential to rival the popularity of legendary Filipino boxer Manny Pacquiao

Meanwhile, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has thanked Eala for bringing the Filipino community to tennis.

"I think it's great," said the Japanese star. "I finished my match and the little go-kart was taking me back. I looked at the practice court and it was completely full. I was like, 'who's practising right now?' She didn't even go on court yet and then I saw the Filipino flags and I was like, 'um-hum'.

"I think it's awesome. It's so cool that she's building a new community and obviously great for the tournament, because she sells a lot of tickets."

Sports.title: Yamashita equals LPGA Tour record in dominant CPKC Women's Open win
Sports.content:
Miyu Yamashita equaled the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record in claiming a dominant, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open..

The Japanese star's closing birdie on Sunday signed off a four-under final round of 66 to take her total for the week to 23 under par and 257 strokes, securing a wire-to-wire win in Edmonton.

Sei Young Kim also shot 257 in the 2018 Thornberry Creek LPGA Classic in Wisconsin, finishing 31 under.

A stroke ahead after Thursday's opening round, thanks to a course-record 62, Yamashita posted a 64 on Friday to open a five-shot lead, before carding a 65 on Saturday.

That had her six strokes ahead entering the final round at Royal Mayfair, Yamashita pushed her winning margin to nine for a tournament record in the Canadian national championship, breaking Jin Young Ko's 262 set in 2019 at Magna in Aurora, Ontario.

Yamashita's four LPGA Tour titles have come in four different countries. She won the Meijer LPGA Classic in the USA in June, after claiming a first major success at the AIG Women's Open title in Wales along with taking the Maybank Championship title in Malaysia last year. She has 13 Japan LPGA victories.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights from Miyu Yamashita's maiden major victory at the AIG Women's Open in 2025 at Royal Porthcawl.

Fellow Japanese player Yuri Yoshida was second at 14 under after a closing 69. Kim was a further shot back after her final-round 67.

Seventeen-year-old Anna Huang was the top Canadian, signing off her week with an impressive 65 to tie for fourth at 12 under.

Aphrodite Deng, the 16-year-old amateur who won the 2025 US Girls' Junior, tied for seventh at 11 under after shooting 67 on Sunday.

Two-time winner Brooke Henderson finished seven under after a closing 70. World No 1 Nelly Korda shot 69 to get to five under.

Sports.title: Nev on title race: Liverpool, Man City nowhere near levels required
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Manchester City are well below the level required to win the Premier League title this season, says Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville.

City are entering the unknown after Pep Guardiola's departure, while Liverpool are rebuilding under Andoni Iraola.

A last-gasp Josko Gvardiol winner handed Enzo Maresca a 2-1 win in his first Premier League game in charge of City against Bournemouth and Liverpool also left it late to draw 2-2 with Newcastle.

Arsenal's opening win was far more straightforward, swatting aside Coventry City 3-0 with minimal fuss. With only one week gone, the Gunners are already odds-on with bookmakers to win the Premier League despite there being 37 games to go.

And Neville is struggling to see a situation where City or Liverpool challenge Arsenal this season.

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, he said: "Last week when we were previewing the season, all I kept thinking about was that this is going to be the most unpredictable season. It's going to be intriguing because you've got new managers, you've got lots of new players, you've got so much change at the top.

"Arsenal should win this league by a street - and I don't sit here on Sunday evening thinking anything differently, we've seen Tottenham get beat, we've seen Manchester United get beat, we've seen Liverpool nearly get beat, we've seen City scrambling for a win at home, so everything we thought we would see, we're seeing. "Man City are the same as Liverpool, these two clubs were getting nearly 100 points, six, seven years ago. Treble winners, four times Premier League winners, Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool, Arne Slot's champions, that's just happened and so we're measuring these two clubs by the standards that they've set, but they're nowhere near that standard.

"This Liverpool team are nowhere near the levels of a Premier League title winning team - they need a lot of work.

"I think they'll be happy with the point [vs Newcastle], a good finish for them, and they're celebrating, but I think deep down when you're measuring yourself and the standards that Liverpool have in the last five, 10 years of winning titles, I think they'll travel home, back to Liverpool and back to Merseyside, and they'll be thinking, we've got a lot of work to do.

"And Man City, they're well below where they need to be. Losing Rodri is a massive blow."

Sports.title: Gauff 'dangerous' for US Open after cruising to second Cincinnati title
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in straight sets, 6-2 6-4, to capture her second Cincinnati Open women's singles title.

It means the world No 4 becomes just the third player in the Open Era, after Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka, to win multiple titles in Cincinnati.

Pegula had beaten defending champion Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals, while Gauff disposed of unseeded Sara Bejlek - who had knocked out world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka - to set up the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years.

Gauff stormed out to a 5-0 lead in the first set, taking it 6-2. Pegula battled back to 5-4 in the second before Gauff, who converted five out of six break points in the contest, closed out the win.

Image: Coco Gauff claimed her second Cincinnati Open title with her victory over Jessica Pegula on Sunday

"I think it was a long journey, but I'm happy," Gauff said. "I think it's night and day, the player I was last year to now.

"I don't think that this is an indicator that I'm going to do well in New York [at the US Open]. Just knowing the quality wins that I had this week, hopefully I can use that experience."

Gauff had five wins in straight sets in Cincinnati.

"I thought she just played at a really high level and didn't really have many dips," Pegula said. "I didn't really think I played bad.

"The more you construct the point [against her], the worse it is because she almost likes to run. It was tough today. A dangerous, confident Coco is going to New York."

The head-to-head series between Gauff and Pegula is now tied at five apiece. Sunday was their second meeting in a final, with Gauff winning at Wuhan last year.

Sports.title: Late Clark magic holds off McIlroy and Cantlay in PGA Tour thriller
Sports.content:
Wyndham Clark overcame blowing a five-shot lead to edge out Rory McIlroy with a dramatic three-shot victory at the PGA Tour's BMW Championship.

Clark saw his big overnight lead disappear during a thrilling Sunday at Bellerive Country Club, where the US Open champion bogeyed three of his first 10 holes to give hope to McIlroy and the chasing pack.

McIlroy found three birdies in a four-hole stretch around the turn to sit level with Clark heading into the closing stretch, only for his playing partner to post a three-birdie finish to cap off a roller-coaster victory in style.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy's chances of victory slipped away with a bogey on the 17th at the BMW Championship

A level-par 70 was enough for Clark to end the week on 17 under and close out a third PGA Tour victory of the season, following on from the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and the US Open, with Patrick Cantlay claiming solo second to progress through to next week's season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy was tied for the lead with three to play but ended four back after a penultimate-hole bogey and Clark's impressive birdie burst, while Gary Woodland, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup shared fourth place.

How Clark held off McIlroy to BMW Championship win

Clark's overnight advantage was immediately cut with a two-shot swing at the first, where he three-putted from 65 feet for bogey as McIlroy holed from 10 feet for birdie.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy makes a dream start on the final round of the BMW Championship to chase Wyndham Clark, who bogeyed the first

McIlroy failed to get up and down to save par at the fourth but holed from seven feet to avoid back-to-back bogeys, as Woodland - two groups ahead - made three birdies in his first five holes to get within two.

Clark bogeyed the par-three sixth after a clunky chip from just off the green, with Woodland halving his advantage by birdieing the par-five eighth before inexplicably topping his tee shot into water at the next.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Woodland made a huge error by topping his tee shot on the ninth at the BMW Championship

McIlroy made a two-putt birdie at the eighth and picked up a shot at the ninth to reach the turn two back, only to pull level with a birdie at the 11th after Clark had started his back nine with a bogey.

Cantlay also briefly shared the lead until a double-bogey at the 11th, while McIlroy and Clark traded pars to leave the pair tied at the top of the leaderboard with three holes to play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy had overturned a five-shot deficit to share the lead with Wyndham Clark late in the final round

Clark was birdie-free during the final day until he edged ahead with a 15-footer at the 16th, before adding another at the par-five next - after McIlroy went from bunker to bunker and carded a bogey - to extend his advantage.

Cantlay reduced the lead by birdieing each of his final three holes to set the clubhouse target at 14 under, as Clark closed out his fifth PGA Tour win by pouring in a 15-foot birdie to extend his winning margin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the late birdie burst that saw Wyndham Clark close out BMW Championship victory

"As much as I would have loved to have run away with this, it was fun to get the juices going," Cantlay told CBS Sports. "I think it shows that I'm one of the best players in the world. Three wins in one season is my best year yet, coming off my worst year ever and I'm just very pleased with where I am at right now."

On claiming third, McIlroy said: "I'm still not in a spot where I'm super happy with where my game is or where my swing is, so I just have to keep working on it. It's nice to know even when I'm not super happy with everything I can still piece it together and get it around and still give myself a chance to win tournaments."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Rory McIlroy's roller-coaster round at the BMW Championship, where he threatened a Sunday comeback

Morikawa delivered a stunning eagle at the par-five 17th but bogeyed the last to finish on 12 under with Woodland and Gotterup, who carded a final-round 69, as Scotland's Robert MacIntyre extended his season after a five-under 65 lifted him to tied-seventh.

What's next?

The PGA Tour season reaches its climax at the Tour Championship at East Lake GC, where only the top 30 players in the standings are eligible to compete for the FedExCup and $10m first prize.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from opening weekend of the season
Sports.content:
1 Wright laments Martinelli treatment

Arsenal’s treatment of Gabriel Martinelli has been questioned by Ian Wright after the Brazil forward was left out of their squad for Friday’s opening game against Coventry. Martinelli turned down a move to Galatasaray last week after Arsenal had agreed a fee with the Turkish club and the former striker Wright revealed on Sky Sports after the Coventry game that no one at the club has spoken to the 25-year-old to discuss his future. “I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, ‘yeah, it’s time for him to move him on’. But there’s ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave,” said Wright. “He’s done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he’s being treated with at the moment.” Ed Aarons

2 Has Watkins tarnished legacy?

It was only one game after 278 for Aston Villa, accumulated over the previous six seasons – a period in which Ollie Watkins has scored 108 goals and made himself one of the most popular players in the club’s Premier League history. But the rules are the rules. Nobody can refuse to play and emerge without a mark against their character. This is the charge against Watkins, brought in none-too-subtle fashion by Unai Emery after Villa’s 4-0 defeat at Brighton – a match that Watkins missed as he considers an approach from Al-Hilal. We do not yet have Watkins’s side of the story. Or that of his agent. But given Emery had no other available No 9, it feels pretty clear the manager did not choose to omit Watkins. Villa claim they are not close to any agreement with Al-Hilal, having rejected more than one offer from them. Perish the thought that this could drag on. Villa have one more game before the window shuts – against Arsenal at home next Monday night. David Hytner

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Villa in their sobering defeat. Photograph: Glyn Kirk/AFP/Getty Images

3 United falter as No 9 options look thin

Michael Carrick was limited in his options during Manchester United’s opener because Benjamin Sesko was unable to feature at any point in pre-season but Matheus Cunha was completely ineffective as a false nine. Hull’s back three enjoyed a very quiet lunchtime as they returned to the Premier League. Cunha did not embrace the physical battle and went missing, leaving United with barely any presence in the final third as they failed to threaten their opponents. Sesko was brought on to change the dynamic but was equally ineffectual, while fellow striker Joshua Zirkzee was left on the bench, implying how little trust the coaches have in him. Carrick needs to get Sesko up to speed and sell Zirkzee soon, freeing up funds to find a better alternative if United are to compete this season, especially with the false nine tactic looking flawed. Will Unwin

4 Tigers delight in Tzolakis’ debut

Manchester United were impressively unthreatening in their approach to losing at Hull. There was the odd half-baked attempt at scoring or putting a cross into a dangerous area but nothing that made the highlights reel. This was unfortunate for the Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who had an impressive, if somewhat uncomplicated, debut between the sticks. After being signed for £20m from Olympiakos, United should have made a greater effort to test him. What duties the Greek international was forced to do, were carried out with ease, instilling confidence in the defence in front of him. If he continues to look so calm and assured, Tzolakis could prove himself one of the smartest signings of the season. “We bought him and we spent some money there,” Sergej Jakirovic said. “He’s a national team player of Greece, an Olympiakos player. If you’re following Greek football, Olympiakos, it’s a huge stress, huge pressure there, and he’s used to it. For him, I think this is like a cup of tea.” WU

5 Cherki’s crucial cameo after disquiet

Rayan Cherki wrested the three points in a cameo that consisted of the corner for Marc Guéhi’s equaliser and the cute pass for Josko Gvardiol’s winner. Enzo Maresca gave an insight into the Frenchman’s disquiet at not starting. “Rayan is quite a nice and clear boy, if he is not happy he wants to show it. If he’s next to me and he’s not happy, you all realise that he is not happy because he is doing anything just to show that he is not happy. I know that he was not happy today but at the end I had to take a decision,” said the manager. Jamie Jackson

6 Sangaré shines against big spenders

At a time when some Premier League are willing to spend over £100m on midfielders there is unlikely to be a better bargain than Mamadou Sangaré. Brentford’s new signing was excellent for Lens last season and was outstanding on his debut against Tottenham. Sangaré dominated midfield, even with Spurs able to field upwards of £175m worth of talent in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, and his performance raised the question of why the league’s bigger clubs are not willing to look further afield for signings. Brentford, after all, only paid £39m for Sangaré. Yet it seems inevitable there will be clubs willing to pay double the price if he has a good first season in England. Jacob Steinberg

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

7 Isak struggles on return to Newcastle

At gut-wrenching as it must have been for Newcastle fans to see their side concede a stoppage-time penalty to Liverpool, at least they can take comfort that it wasn’t Alexander Isak that scored the Reds’ dramatic equaliser from 12 yards. The former Newcastle striker had a torrid time on his return to St James’ Park – booed at every touch, crunched by Lewis Hall in the tackle and sending his only real chance of note into orbit – but he would surely have fancied taking his revenge with the last kick of the game before Dominik Szoboszlai converted the 99th-minute spot-kick. Worryingly, Isak is lacking the fluency that convinced Liverpool to spend £125m last summer and with Hugo Ekitiké still sidelined with a long-term injury, Andoni Iraola doesn’t have a natural replacement at No 9. If Liverpool are to be successful this season, Isak has to turn it on. Michael Butler

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak watches the ball during his return to Tyneside. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images

8 Ipswich combat set pieces with O’Shea

A defensive tactical shift from the Ipswich Town manager, Gary O’Neil, demonstrated the changing nature of the Premier League. O’Neil, an astute reader of the game, chose to play the tall centre-back Dara O’Shea at right-back to counter the threat of set pieces that have become so prevalent, in Ipswich’s surprise win against Sunderland. “Aerially the Premier League is such a test now, from long throws and set pieces,” O’Neil said. “To have three centre-half types in your back four helps us from set pieces, size-wise.” In the first season since Pep Guardiola departed, the top flight is already shifting away from his neat, passing football to a different beast. Sam Cunningham

9 Dewsbury-Hall on path to complete midfielder

David Moyes felt his young Everton team might have been uncomfortable chasing the game against Crystal Palace and were therefore indebted to Jordan Pickford’s save from Eddie Nketiah, plus Jean-Philippe Mateta’s finishing, for not having to do so. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s guidance was instrumental too. The performance of both teams altered once the midfielder imposed himself, while his superb strike beyond Dean Henderson underlined the quality of a player who will be crucial to Everton’s aspirations. “I want to be better than last season,” said Dewsbury-Hall, who delivered eight goals and four assists in his first Premier League campaign at Everton. “That’s not just goals and assists, it’s my overall play. A couple of years ago I probably wasn’t getting goals and assists but was influential in play. I want to mix that together and when you do that that’s when you become a complete midfielder. I know I have the ability to do it so fingers crossed I do.” Andy Hunter

10 Farke hopes Leeds can cement status

Optimism abounds at Leeds. An encouraging opening-day victory at Nottingham Forest gave credence to the idea that Daniel Farke’s side are capable of cementing their place in the league. Last season, survival was the aim but after investing about £80m to sign James Trafford, Tarik Muharemovic and Nico Elvedi, plus Harry Wilson on a free, they are seeking to build on a 14th-placed finish. Leeds and Forest, who meet again in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, have both been linked with a move for Chelsea’s Liam Delap; a striker to share the load with Dominic Calvert-Lewin would surely elevate Farke’s side. “If we want to establish ourselves and after a few years perhaps speak about something else, then we need to add individual quality,” Farke said. “The last time this club was able to have two solid seasons at this level, you will perhaps find it in black and white photos.” Ben Fisher

Sports.title: Chelsea change course with Alonso primed to banish the chaos of youth
Sports.content:
It is a necessary reset. Although it would be pushing it to say that Chelsea have switched from development centre to retirement home, even after the signings of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, there has been a clear shift in strategy this summer. Some grownups are in the room at last and, for Xabi Alonso, the hope is that bringing in more experience will help a squad still packed with youngsters show more composure when adversity strikes.

Discipline was a problem for Chelsea last season: they had 11 red cards in all competitions and a lot of the wounds were self-inflicted. Chelsea were impetuous, on the receiving end of too many bookings for dissent and prone to collapsing at the first sign of trouble. No wonder Alonso, who was the epitome of calm during his playing career, has focused on maintaining “emotional control” before opening his tenure as manager with Monday’s trip to Fulham.

It will be a test of Chelsea’s mentality. Craven Cottage has been the setting for some spectacular implosions during the BlueCo era, the path to two 2-1 victories for Fulham over their neighbours smoothed by João Félix earning a red card on his Chelsea debut in 2023 and by Marc Cucurella getting himself sent off after 22 minutes last season.

Chelsea need to change, and hiring Alonso was a tacit admission that their approach required fine-tuning. Internally there was a recognition that the club had undervalued the importance of aura when it came to hiring coaches.

They blundered with Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior, neither of whom were capable of standing the heat. Alonso is a different breed. The 44-year-old burnished his reputation by leading Bayer Leverkusen to the Bundesliga title in 2024 and he wowed Chelsea during his discussions over the role, so much so that they broke with the past by naming him manager rather than head coach.

Now the players can look to the dugout and see an authority figure. Alonso has not seized absolute power – he is still part of a wider structure, collaborating with an extensive recruitment team – but there is no doubt that his arrival has lent credibility to a project that was in danger of falling apart when the Rosenior experiment ended.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior struggled at Stamford Bridge, lasting less than four months. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

Of course, it remains to be seen if success in Germany means Alonso can dominate in England. Leverkusen was special but Real Madrid left him with a scar. Then again, the Bernabéu is not exactly where managers go to develop. It makes Álvaro Arbeloa, who stepped in at Madrid after Alonso’s sacking last season, a similar unknown after replacing Marco Silva at Fulham.

Yet there is optimism around Chelsea. Can they mount a title challenge for the first time in a decade? There is a lot of ground to make up after finishing 10th last season. Weaknesses linger, particularly in goal, and a push for the top four looks likelier.

However, no European football could be a blessing, giving Alonso more time in training. He looks tactically flexible. Chelsea switched between a back four and a back three during pre-season. Cucurella has joined Madrid but Marco Palestra, signed from Atalanta for £43m, and Pep Chavarría, a £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano, could play as wingbacks.

The recruitment looks purposeful. After years of buying promising youngsters Chelsea have targeted ready-made players. Maxence Lacroix, the 26-year-old France centre-back, is a sensible signing from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers, signed from Aston Villa for £117m, can play in a range of positions in attacking midfield and could form an exciting partnership with a rested Cole Palmer, who has a point to prove after missing out on England’s World Cup squad.

There is talent here. There always has been, though. The flaw has more been around mindset. It is a footballing norm to have wise heads around to protect young players. Chelsea went too far in the opposite direction and it is one of the first areas Alonso has addressed.

Perhaps he has heard the tale of one of his predecessors having to deal with a player prioritising a haircut over a team meeting. Either way it did not feel on brand when Chelsea made an unsuccessful attempt to sign the 33-year-old Granit Xhaka from Sunderland in June. Yet it underlined their desire for more leadership and the box was ticked when Welbeck, 35, joined from Brighton in a cut-price deal and Henderson, 36, was brought in on a free transfer from Brentford.

View image in fullscreen New signing Danny Welbeck offers experience, maturity and a reliable source of goals. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

They could be canny moves. Perhaps there is an element of overkill, a sense of Chelsea taking their new direction too far, but Welbeck and Henderson still have something to offer. Welbeck scored 13 league goals for Brighton last season and will provide cover for João Pedro up front, while Henderson did not look out of place for Brentford and, according to Jude Bellingham, is someone coaching staff will always go to when there are problems to resolve.

Alonso needs order. There are still rumblings of instability off the pitch, with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter looking to sell their stakes in the club to the majority shareholder, Clearlake Capital. Quiet is rare. Chelsea need to shift a host of players before the transfer window shuts and questions hover over Enzo Fernández, who favours a reunion with Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

There has been a lot of noise around Fernández. The midfielder has made no secret of his desire to leave but speaking out so much when Chelsea were wounded underlined the decline in standards. Alonso needs leaders. He needs trust. He still has to prove the hype is justified but his attempts to change Chelsea’s mentality is an encouraging first step.

Sports.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled Fifa counterpart that he will face an opponent if he runs for re-election next March.

Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament.

In an interview with the podcast The Rest is Politics: Leading, Ceferin denounced Infantino’s project as more damaging than the breakaway Super League that was shelved in 2021 after large-scale protests. “I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan,” he said. “In the first case, super-important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

“I’m absolutely sure that the [FFE] plan is dead. For me, the most important thing is that we stopped another try to sell the sport. It’s hard to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone.”

Earlier this month it was reported that Infantino had held talks about running the Super League under Fifa branding. Ceferin is confident that any revival of that plan would be decades away. “It might happen in 20 years, you never know, but for now we cooperate with everyone in a great way. I’m sure it cannot happen in the next 10 years,” he said.

Infantino spent much of the weekend courting support from Concacaf members at a meeting in the Dominican Republic, infuriating many of those present. Ceferin, who revealed the pair had not been in contact since the FFE scandal broke, believes the Fifa president’s path to survival is narrowing.

“I didn’t speak with him, he didn’t contact me since this happened,” he said. “But there are two options. One option is that he realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option [is] that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.” The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been tipped as a potential opponent for Infantino if he chooses to run in Rabat.

Ceferin has proponents of his own but ruled out making his own bid for the Fifa presidency. “My credibility is much, much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position,” he said. The Slovenian is expected to run unopposed for a fourth term at the helm of Uefa, with the election due next April.

Asked whether Infantino had become too close to Donald Trump, with whom he forged a close relationship before the recent World Cup, Ceferin said: “To be honest, I think you are naive if you think that a politician like that, or any politician, is your good friend. The moment you are a problem, you stop being a friend of a politician.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That friendship came under the spotlight last month when Trump said he had called Infantino to ask for a review of the red card given to the US striker Folarin Balogun, whose ban for the last-16 tie against Belgium was later suspended. “That was more than shocking,” Ceferin said. “We have rules and if you don’t respect your own rules, then the game doesn’t make any sense. That’s shocking and, trust me, almost everybody was shocked. Just not everybody dared to speak.”

Meanwhile, in a fresh show of European opposition to Infantino, the six Nordic football associations issued a statement saying they had “lost confidence in the Fifa president and have serious concerns about the governance and high-level decision making of the organisation”. They asked for binding assurances that Fifa will never again “open its governance or competitions to private ownership” and called for a full third-party review into the FFE scheme.

Earlier in August the Norwegian Football Federation was the first member association to call directly for Infantino to step down.

Infantino travelled straight from the Dominican Republic to Paris on Sunday, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup. Television footage showed him exchanging greetings with the president of France, Emmanuel Macron.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Alvarez set for Arsenal after being booed at Atlético?
Sports.content:
Booing Julián Alvarez during Atlético Madrid’s draw with Villarreal on Sunday has seemingly convinced the Argentinian forward to consider joining Arsenal in the window. The former Manchester City man has been kept out of the reaches of Barcelona, who may not have the funds to complete the signing, whereas the Gunners have plenty of cash to splash.

Alejandro Balde was left out of the Barcelona squad as they roared past Elche, as the Catalan club open the door for a move to Manchester United. A new left-back should solve all of the problems at Old Trafford, that’s for sure.

Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to West Ham, despite them being relegated and starting the Championship season in desperate fashion. Despite all that, perhaps he will be tempted by a £50m bid from Crystal Palace after a welcome to the Championship to forget? The Eagles were blunt at Everton over the weekend and could be about to initiate panic stations by splashing out quite severely for the Hammers skipper.

Losing 4-0 at Brighton is not going to do much for morale but it will make a team take drastic action in the market. Aston Villa have lined up Joel Ordóñez to solve all of their problems for the remainder of the season, if Club Brugge are willing to sell the centre-back.

There is only one way to bounce back from losing at Ipswich and that is to chase a £34m Barcelona player. Sunderland have tracked Marc Casadó throughout the summer and could be about to pounce for the 22-year-old, who has also been linked with most of the Premier League in recent weeks.

It is difficult to decipher if Cruzeiro’s Jonathan Jesus would sign for Strasbourg or Chelsea, but the talk in Brazil is that ownership group BlueCo want the 22-year-old centre-back. Real Betis, Valencia and Benfica are equally keen, adding a bit of jeopardy to the chase.

With Chelsea always looking to move on a few players, they will be ecstatic to hear that Napoli are contemplating a move for the striker Marc Guiu. Whether the Italians are up for splurging £25m on the Spaniard remains to be seen because the Serie A club currently believe the Blues’ valuation is a touch on the high side.

As alluded to, it was a fantastic start to the season for Hull on Saturday when they gave Manchester United a bit of a shooing. To help build on that, they have agreed a £15.4m deal to sign forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.

Sports.title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
Sports.content:
Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Aston Villa in their sobering 4-0 defeat by Brighton at the Amex on Sunday. The head coach had a selection crisis up front with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham injured. However, he did not include Watkins in the matchday squad as the England striker considers a move to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Emery was forced to rely on the attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency striker and his team disappeared without trace on the south coast. They were 4-0 down after 31 minutes and had their new signing João Gomes sent off on his debut in the 40th minute. Gomes kicked up and out at the Brighton striker Georginio Rutter after being dispossessed by him.

Al-Hilal have made a number of bids for Watkins, all of which have been rejected. It is understood the 30-year-old is open to the move and Emery talked on Friday like a manager who was realistic about the sale happening. Villa would plainly like to replace Watkins should he depart as they approach the end of another difficult summer window. They have already sold Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans, while they are expected to move on Emiliano Martínez.

Emery was asked why he had not picked Watkins against Brighton. “This question is for him,” he said. “I can answer only with my silence.” Emery was then asked if Watkins had refused to play, to which he said: “I think you can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond.”

The Guardian have contacted Watkins’s agent for comment.

“He [Watkins] can only explain his answer, I can’t,” Emery added, after being asked if he felt let down by Watkins.

Emery reported that Madjo would be out for “two weeks more … more or less” while attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi – who has been the club’s marquee summer signing – would “need maybe some days more [than that]”. He was unclear about a timeframe for Abraham’s return.

Quick Guide How do I 

Emery talked up the resistance of his players in the second half against Brighton and said he was optimistic about finding solutions for the season ahead. But he returned to the difficult preparations for the opening fixture, noting that: “Two strikers are injured and another striker gives his answer.”

The head coach added: “This problem [with the transfer market] … we had every season and every season we overcame it. It’s something we have to accept and always we reacted, especially the players. This is something hard for us every year but we are calm. With this result, it’s more difficult to explain but calm, work, be positive and find solutions for the next week and after the transfer window.”

Sports.title: Newcastle and Liverpool crank up the entertainment for emotional send-off | Sam Dalling
Sports.content:
It’s 4.35pm on Tyneside. William Osula sets Anthony Elanga away, slightly right of centre and just short of 50,000 draw collective breaths. Pace is no issue; Elanga has no shortage of that, and Milos Kerkez won’t catch him.

But Newcastle fans have seen this clip before and remember the ending. Muscles tighten, cheeks clench, as they brace themselves for it to start again like it carried on before. (Yet) another memeable‑moment inbound.

A tiny part of each of them, though, thinks: “Wait, hang on, this is a new season, a fresh start.” The slate is not just clean but has been entirely replaced and is now AI-operated.

Elanga takes a touch, a tad heavier ideal but it pushes the ball away from Alisson. A moment of composure follows and Newcastle lead. An entirely goalless league season passed after Elanga’s £55m transfer from Nottingham Forest and now, within five minutes of a new one, his drought is broken.

Elanga missed a much easier opportunity against Aston Villa on the 2025-26 opening day, and his confidence never recovered. Can you walk back through a sliding door?

Nearly two hours later, there remain just a few precious seconds for Liverpool to salvage something. Victor Muñoz is brought down clumsily by Lewis Hall. Dominik Szoboszlai converts the resulting penalty. 2-2.

Muñoz apparently gave Newcastle positive noises about joining them during summer. Then, in a flexing of financial muscle, Liverpool met the Osasuna forward’s release clause and to Anfield he went. What was that about sliding doors?

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Víctor Muñoz – a summer target for Newcastle – is brought down by Lewis Hall to hand the visitors a late penalty. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/AP

Those two goals bookended an afternoon that was, if you want to do go down that road, a fitting tribute to the recently departed Kevin Keegan. Entertaining but flawed.

As a term, legend is so chronically overused now that it is meaningless. But Keegan is a prime example of the word’s proper application. Shortly before kick-off everyone present paid an emotional tribute to him. Legend. Hero. King. All subjective labels essentially turned objective.

With Liverpool, Keegan’s seven trophies in six years – including three titles and the European Cup – set the club up to be the behemoth they now are. Across three spells at Newcastle, he jabbed syringes of hope into a flailing, helpless shell.

St James’ Park is not quite the house that Keegan built, but it is no stretch to say it is the house built because of him. Without his steering Newcastle to Second Division safety in 1992 as manager, the club in its current guise might not exist.

So, why does Keegan remain so adored? He is in effect a symbol of what football once was and should still be, can be even. Maybe.

Forget spreadsheets, financial acronyms and PR-doused messaging. Ignore expected this and that, low blocks and cancelling each other out. Find the joy. Forget perfect; take a risk. Failure and fallibility? Both absolutely OK.

Those are sentiments Andoni Iraola and Matthias Jaissle would do well to remember as they look to settle themselves into new gigs.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The former, with Liverpool being champions two seasons ago, will be under the greater pressure. A repeat of his start at Bournemouth, where he won only at the 10th time of asking, would be difficult to tolerate.

There were promising signs for Iraola, sure. Jérémy Jacquet grew into his debut. Cody Gakpo had only just whipped a strike narrowly off target before his fine equaliser just after half-time. Rio Ngumoha was quiet but that he has impressed sufficiently to start the season opener is itself a plus.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz (centre) and former Newcastle man Alexander Isak again both struggled to make an impact for Liverpool. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

But there were familiar failings, too. The full-backs looked shaky and Iraola needs more (much, much more) from both the sums and the whole of the £241m Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak combo.

Isak is about as popular in Newcastle as government-mandated balaclava wearing in a heatwave would be, but the stick-cum-abuse he received didn’t seem to bother him. However, what should keep Isak up at night is how he can and must refind the level that rightly saw him tagged one of the Premier League’s best forwards not so long ago. A skied left-footed effort was the closest he came to silencing the heckles.

Jaissle is likely to get more slack. Everyone is aware of what Newcastle have, where they are and, most pertinent, what they have lost.

Something fresh was absolutely needed but that requires time and patience. There are, and will continue to be, warts, imperfections, things that Bruno Guimarães might have done.

A midfield pair sold for north of £180m were replaced on Sunday by a double pivot with a combined aged of 38 and less than 50 league starts. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur looked the part but made mistakes. That they did so seeking the positive option will only endear them to fans. As will more similar performances from Yoane Wissa. A player who last season looked sluggish and largely static, was suddenly full of everything in the No 10 role.

A decent start. Room for improvement. Apply that to both sides.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 3: Birmingham City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st (WSL2)

Prospects

Founding members of the Women’s Super League when it launched in 2011, Birmingham are back in the top flight after four years in the second tier, having won promotion as WSL2 champions on the final day of last season. After a decent summer transfer window, Birmingham look to have a fighting chance of staying up, and perhaps even surprising a few teams, while off the pitch they are the best-equipped of the three promoted sides to cement themselves in the top division.

Forwards Lily Crosthwaite and Wilma Leidhammar and defender Neve Herron, are all 23-years-old and likely to continue improving. Birmingham have also added players with WSL experience, such as the former Brighton goalkeeper Sophie Baggaley and the centre-back Millie Turner.

Inconsistency was nearly their downfall last season; they won the most games in WSL2, but also lost six times. They delivered under pressure, boosted by the performances of Leidhammar after her club-record arrival in January, ensuring they avoided a repeat of the heartbreak of 12 months earlier when they missed out on promotion on the final day. Nonetheless, Birmingham are still a long way off from the days when they were runners-up in the top tier and their first two away fixtures are against Manchester City and Chelsea. They also host fellow promoted sides Crystal Palace and Charlton relatively early in the campaign and those home fixtures could be key to building confidence.

Off-field picture

Birmingham’s women’s team were sold to the club’s ownership group in February, with Shelby Companies Limited – an affiliate of Knighthead Capital Management – owning 97%. The remaining 3% was purchased by investors including the former England midfielder Karen Carney and the four-time grand slam tennis champion Kim Clijsters. The club appear to be in a relatively healthy position with ambitious owners determined to reestablish the 2012 FA Cup winners as a regular, competitive presence in the WSL. They train at the recently renovated Knighthead Performance Centre, on the same site as the men’s team’s former Wast Hills training base, with a new gym among other extensive refurbishments.

The manager

Amy Merricks has been in charge since April 2024 She holds a Uefa Pro Licence and was 30 years old when she was appointed by Birmingham. She has previously coached within the England youth setup as well as at Gillingham, Millwall and Brighton, where was stepped up to be interim manager three times.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Lisa Naalsund arrives from Manchester United to boost Birmingham’s midfield. Photograph: DeFodi Images/Getty Images

Birmingham have recruited players with international experience, including the Canada defender Marie Levasseur from Montpellier, but their two most eyebrow-raising additions are Turner and Lisa Naalsund from Manchester United. They were starting members of United’s FA Cup-winning side of 2024 and played in a Women’s Champions League quarter-final as recently as April. Naalsund will be an influential force in the midfield – she has won 39 caps and was part of Norway’s squad at last year’s Euros.

Stat attack

Birmingham topped WSL2 last season despite not scoring the most goals or conceding the fewest. One stat they led was big chances, Opta’s metric for opportunities where it is reasonable to expect the attacker to score. While their tally will be much harder to repeat in the top flight, their attacking process looks in good order.

Set for a breakthrough

There is plenty of excitement at Birmingham about another of their new signings, the 19-year-old France youth forward Chancelle Effa Effa, who arrived from Le Havre for a fee understood to be about €120,000 (£100,000) this month. She broke into Le Havre’s first team at the age of 15 and scored 17 times in 28 games for France’s Under-17 and Under-19 teams, having helped France win 2023’s Under-17 Euros.

What they say …

“We know it’s going to be a massive challenge, but it’s a challenge that, as players, you thrive upon. As long as we can take that togetherness, that relentlessness, into the games, I’m sure we’re going to be just fine” – Chelsea Cornet.

Where are they playing their home games?

Birmingham play their home fixtures at St Andrew’s, which has been the women’s team’s home since 2021. They set a club record attendance for a women’s game there on the final day of the 2024-25 season – 8,749. Long-term, the club have announced plans to build a new women’s team stadium as part of the ‘Sports Quarter’, which also includes the proposed 62,000-seater men’s team Powerhouse Stadium as well as an indoor arena, training ground facilities and a new railway station.

Sports.title: Maresca concedes Manchester City ‘a work in progress’ after hair-raising escape
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City remain a “work in progress” after Sunday’s last-gasp win over Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium.

Marc Guéhi’s 85th-minute equaliser and Josko Gvardiol’s 91st-minute winner gave City’s new manager victory in his first game, after Marcus Tavernier’s first-half strike for the visitors.

Maresca thought his side performed similarly to last Sunday’s 3-0 Community Shield loss to Arsenal. “I feel in the same position as after Arsenal,” the Italian said. “It’s normal you judge after results but I don’t see big changes. Unfortunately, this is a work in progress and I’m looking for solutions. For sure when you win games it helps.

“If you think of the Premier League – it won’t happen that you will concede nothing. The goal we conceded was their first shot. They had two or three dangerous moments but it’s how you react. We’ve still got [Erling] Haaland, Elliot [Anderson], Marc [Guéhi], Nico O’Reilly [who all started], who are in pre-season still. It’s a huge difference in terms of physicality and we are going to get better and better.”

Before the game City unfurled a huge tifo bearing his image that said: “Welcome back Enzo.” He said: “It is the perfect day. I was very pleased to see the banner when the game started. We gave them [fans] the joy at the end. It was quite emotional. The spirit was fantastic. It’s a game we deserved to win [but] you don’t need to wait for the last five minutes. We missed chances, then they scored and it became more complicated.”

Maresca fielded Guéhi in an unfamiliar midfield role. “I know Marc from [ Crystal] Palace and I always thought he could play as a midfielder because he is very good,” the manager said. “So we tried it for a few days and I think he was quite good. He gives us a solution for the future,.”

In his first game managing Bournemouth, Marco Rose came close to leading them to a first away win against City. “We’re competitors, we came here to win for the first time,” said the German. “We were in a good way to do so. But we did many good things. We have a lot of things to improve. At the end, how the game went was quite unlucky to lose that way. We had two situations – one corner kick and one attacking [move] – when we defended too passively.
