Sports.title: Verstappen suffering from "flu-like" illness as Zandvoort exposes Red Bull's fundamental problems
Sports.content:
With three victories since the Dutch Grand Prix returned to the calendar in 2021, Max Verstappen can already look back on a very successful period. The final edition in 2026 has proven an ordeal so far, both in terms of Red Bull’s pace and Verstappen’s physical condition.

"I've felt better before, yes," Verstappen admitted during the Dutch media session in the paddock after qualifying. "I feel a bit flu-like and I’m just not feeling as much energy as normal."

Asked whether that also affects his performance behind the wheel, he continued: "No, I don’t think so. I think once you’re in the car, it’s actually fine."

It does mean Verstappen is experiencing his final home race somewhat differently and is mainly looking forward to the moment he can get some rest: "Of course I still enjoy all the fans in the grandstands, but apart from that, I’m mostly looking forward to getting some sleep."

Why Zandvoort exposes some fundamental Red Bull problems

Aside from Verstappen’s physical condition, Red Bull is also struggling for performance at the circuit in the dunes. The home hero had to settle for seventh on the grid and was more than four tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris in qualifying.

"We changed quite a lot on the car after the sprint, but none of it made any difference," Verstappen said when asked by Autosport.

According to Verstappen, the Zandvoort circuit exposes some of Red Bull’s weaknesses to an exaggerated degree Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The balance of the car is the biggest problem. It’s just not consistent throughout the entire corner, but it has been like that all season. It’s just a little worse at some circuits than at others."

In that respect, Zandvoort is a track that exposes the RB22’s weaknesses more than most.

"It depends on the tarmac sometimes, but also on the layout of the track. This one is for sure not our best layout, but we just need to work on it. We can guess on what track it might be a little bit better, but we need to try and just dial it out."

Verstappen added that, in his view, it is not so much related to set-up, as Red Bull has tried everything in that respect: "I think we’re now simply more limited by some fundamental problems with the car that we need to solve.

"At this circuit you also have some fast corners and we’re lacking there as well. In general, if you don’t have a good balance, you can’t really attack the corners. And if you don’t have traction either, you can’t get out of the corners properly, so all of that costs time."

It means Verstappen considers seventh place the maximum achievable result on Sunday under normal circumstances, particularly if there is no chaos caused by rain.

Without rain, Verstappen reckons that P7 will be the best he can hope for in his final home race Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

It may not be the Zandvoort farewell he had hoped for, although the four-time world champion stresses that the Dutch GP era as a whole has already been a great success.

"It’s absolutely the end of an era," he said. "To have had your own home race and to have been able to win it a few times is very special. Of course, it’s a shame that it’s going away, but on the other hand, it has also given me a lot of great moments and memories."

Whether another memorable moment will be added remains to be seen, but Verstappen took a pragmatic view in conclusion.

"I’m really only satisfied when we win, but that’s going to be very difficult tomorrow," he said. "We’ve been a little too slow throughout this season and that’s not suddenly going to change in Zandvoort, but we’re just going to try to enjoy it one last time."

Sports.title: Mercedes is “clearly not the fastest car on the grid any more” claims Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes are no longer the team to beat in Formula 1 claimed Andrea Kimi Antonelli after McLaren’s second consecutive victory in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Lando Norris passed Antonelli on his way to victory in yesterday’s race at Zandvoort, as he did in the previous round in Hungary.

“For sure, we’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid,” said Antonelli, who holds a 59-point lead in the drivers’ championship. “We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However Antonelli has high hopes for Mercedes’ forthcoming upgrade for its W17. “The team has been working super-hard on this next package that is coming up and they just want to make sure that it’s going to work out well once we put it on,” he said.

“So for sure, in this race, it’s going to be more difficult, it’s going to be challenging, but we’re ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity. And then hopefully it’s going to be our turn to bring the package that’s going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again.”

Antonelli’s team mate George Russell believes McLaren’s strength in the last two races has been partly due to the similarities in the track layouts.

“I don’t think it’s a major surprise for us, seeing how competitive Lando was this weekend, considering he won in Budapest,” he said. “It’s a very similar circuit with the long corners, high tyre degradation, with the two-stop strategy, so there’s a lot of similarities between the two circuits.

“I think this may continue for the coming two or three races until we start to bring more to the car, and fingers crossed our competitors don’t.”

He expects Mercedes will be “slightly more competitive” in the next race at Monza, the fastest circuit on the calendar. “However, I believe Ferrari have an engine upgrade incoming, and the truth is we just don’t know.

“But I do believe that these high-degradation circuits really suit McLaren very well, and especially Lando. He’s always been a bit of a specialist in those conditions. We also saw it last year. Monza may be slightly different, but I think they are the team to beat right now.”

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Williams pair apologise for crash: ‘It’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Both Williams drivers apologised for their roles in the collision between the pair during the Dutch Grand Prix.

However the stewards ruled Carlos Sainz Jnr was responsible for the collision which ended his team mate Alexander Albon’s race.

The collision occured as Albon tried to overtake Sainz on the outside entering Tarzan corner. Sainz locked up and made contact with the other Williams.

“It was a situation of the race put us with Alex on a fresher medium [tyre] behind,” Sainz explained. “I was struggling already a lot with my hard tyres there towards the end of the race and all of a sudden when I went to defend, a big bump in the braking area into turn one surprised me.

“I triggered a massive front lock and without wanting, obviously, I took Alex with me, which is the last thing you want to do with a team mate. But honestly I was caught off guard with that big bump there in the braking and triggered a massive front lock that I couldn’t recover later.

“So apologies for that and we will move on as a team. I think it’s just not the position we want to be in.”

The stewards handed Sainz a 10-second time penalty, ruling he “locked up and caused a collision between both cars” and was “wholly at fault”.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However Albon also apologised for his role in the collision. He said it was not as serious as other clashes between team mates, notably the 2018 collision between Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took both drivers out.

“It’s not good for the team,” said Albon. “Obviously we apologise to the team, but it’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation.

“We’ll review it for sure but I think he maybe just locked up and I tried to avoid it as well but we had damage so we had to retire.”

Sports.title: Hulkenberg explains how he avoided team mate Bortoleto in “scary” near-miss | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nico Hulkenberg described how he made an “instinctive” last-second swerve to avoid T-boning his team mate in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Gabriel Bortoleto overtook Hulkenberg moments before spinning in front of him on the first lap of the Dutch Grand Prix.

“It was scary, sketchy,” said Hulkenberg. “You’re a passenger to some [extent].”

Bortoleto lost control of his car in the final corner, moments after Max Verstappen did the same and hit the barrier on the outside. Bortoleto kept his car on track but Hulkenberg had to make an immediate call whether to swerve to the left or right of the other Audi.

“I tried to react as late as possible and then just instinctively chose the side,” Hulkenberg explained. “Obviously I was waiting to see if he’s going to slide up or down. On a wet track it’s sketchy and difficult, but luckily we managed to avoid that.”

Bortoleto suspected he lost control of his car partly because he saw Verstappen going off ahead of him.

“I just saw big smoke coming out,” he said. “I think it was Max that crashed and then I maybe made a small reaction on the steering.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But I just felt something and then I also lost the car. I did a 360, came back.”

Both Audi drivers finished the race, Hulkenberg claiming points for eighth while Bortoleto’s poor start and spin left him 13th. Bortoleto said he had other “issues” in his race but was unwilling to elaborate on them.

“I don’t want to go too much into details, because I don’t know if I can say, or whatever. But we just need to understand some stuff that happened today, and we’ll move on.

“I had a few start problems today that almost made me not probably manage to run out of the grid box, but I appreciate the work of the team. They were really on it to make it happen and to fix everything.

“It’s a shame the result was not what we wanted today, but Nico scored some points, so that’s good. We brought some points for the team at home, so good.”

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Takes Credit For Zepeda, Teofimo Title Wins
Sports.content:
His loss was not as one-sided as the official scores of 118-110, 118-110, and 119-109 suggested. Stevenson landed 295 of 565 punches, compared with Zepeda’s 272 of 979. Shakur was far more accurate, connecting at approximately 52% against Zepeda’s 28%, but only 23 landed punches separated them across 12 rounds.

A later victory over Lamont Roach Jr. gave Zepeda the WBC lightweight title that Stevenson previously held. It was his first full world championship, but he had already reached interim title status before meeting Shakur.

What was interesting is how Shakur handled it publicly. Before Zepeda fought Lamont Roach Jr, Shakur openly predicted Roach would dish out a beating. Once Zepeda walked away with the full WBC lightweight title, Shakur immediately flipped his tune to build up his own credentials.

By comparison, Lopez had a much stronger championship history. He defeated Vasiliy Lomachenko at lightweight and Josh Taylor at light welterweight before surrendering his WBO 140-pound belt to Stevenson in January. Saturday’s majority-decision victory over Rolando Romero made Teofimo a three-division champion.

Those latest wins add value to Shakur’s record because they confirm that Zepeda and Lopez continued operating at the championship level. Stevenson deserves credit for beating them, especially his dominant performance against Teofimo at Madison Square Garden.

However, the WBC title came to Zepeda through his victory over Roach, while Lopez moved to welterweight and took Romero’s WBA belt.

At most, Shakur can use those wins as proof that he defeated quality opposition. He cannot take partial ownership of championships that Zepeda and Teofimo won through their own performances.

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Teofimo Lopez May Delay Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
Allowing Teofimo to take that fight first would only weaken Catterall’s position. Lopez could earn the enormous payday, lose the title in the process, or move toward another opponent, leaving Catterall waiting without any guarantee that his opportunity would retain the same value. His better business decision is to demand the Lopez fight next and pursue the Garcia–Benn winner afterward.

Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan

Jack Catterall says Teofimo Lopez does not have the freedom to select another opponent after capturing the WBA “Super” welterweight title from Rolando Romero on Saturday night.

When Ring Magazine asked who Teofimo should fight next following his majority-decision win, Catterall responded that the WBA had already provided the answer through its 180-day directive.

“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Mannix: Jaron Ennis vs. Josh Kelly Talks Are Advanced
Sports.content:
“Boots is chomping at the bit to get back in the ring, and I’m told there are advanced negotiations for Jaron Ennis to face Josh Kelly in a unification fight sometime in November or December,” Mannix said during DAZN’s Sources Say. “Josh Kelly, coming off a win this past month, had some injury issues after that fight. He had a nose injury, but Matchroom, Boots’ team, believes that injury will be healed. I’m told they are targeting that fight on the East Coast before the end of this year.”

If Kelly were a stronger champion, he might be able to make several defenses and earn money from the IBF title before pursuing a unification. His July 25 showing against Caoimhin Agyarko demonstrated why waiting would carry considerable risk.

Heavy punishment left Kelly with a badly damaged nose as he squeezed out a narrow 12-round unanimous decision in Jeddah. Agyarko is ranked No. 15 by the IBF, yet Kelly struggled to keep him under control.

Higher in the IBF rankings are Brandon Adams, former champion Bakhram Murtazaliev, Nikita Tszyu, Israil Madrimov, Ben Mahoney, Xander Zayas, Milan Prat, Giovani Santillan, Yan Marcos, Pavel Sosulin, Ibrahima Diallo, and Bilal Fawaz. Kelly would have a difficult time holding the belt for long against that group.

His title-winning victory over Murtazaliev in Newcastle was also viewed by many as a hometown gift. Kelly stayed mobile rather than engage for long. Near the end of rounds, he used quick shoeshine combinations to impress the judges. Murtazaliev landed the heavier punches and dropped Kelly in the ninth, yet lost on two cards.

Ennis presents a far more severe test. The WBA and WBO champion has more speed, power, combination punching, and offensive variety. The difference is wide enough that placing the fight in Newcastle probably would not change the outcome.

That nose injury may be the greatest immediate concern. If it breaks down during sparring, the unification may have to be postponed. Assuming Kelly gets through camp, taking the Ennis fight now makes more financial sense than continuing with lower-paying title defenses.

Sports.title: Regis Prograis Calls Rocky Marciano Overrated
Sports.content:
“For me, I think Rocky Marciano was overrated,” Prograis said on social media. “He retired undefeated, right? But in this book, I bought this book about Sonny Liston. It said right here about Rocky Marciano that ‘his good fortune was to rise to prominence at a time when his major competitors were either old, like 37-year-old Joe Louis.’ He was 37 when he fought him. Joe Walcott was 37 years old. A natural light heavyweight like Ezzard Charles was 34 years old, and then Archie Moore was 41 at the time.”

The overall point has some merit, but several ages quoted by Prograis are inaccurate. Louis was 37, but Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his heavyweight title in September 1952. Charles was 32 in their first fight and turned 33 before the rematch, not 34. Moore’s birth year remains disputed, leaving him either 38 or 41 when he challenged Marciano in 1955.

Prograis also accused Marciano of avoiding 6-foot-3 Cuban contender Nino Valdes because of his size.

“They had a Cuban fighter called Nino Valdes, and he didn’t want to fight him,” Prograis said. “He said he was too big. So I know a lot of older guys say that Rocky Marciano was this and undefeated this. But I feel Rocky Marciano was overrated at the time.”

Valdes had a legitimate case after rising to the top of the heavyweight rankings, but saying Marciano simply refused to face him leaves out part of the story.

The Cuban lost a 15-round title eliminator to Moore in May 1955. Marciano then met Moore four months later and stopped him in the ninth round. Valdes also suffered numerous defeats during Marciano’s championship reign, making the claim that he was deliberately avoided difficult to prove.

Marciano’s leading opponents were older, and his era lacked the talent found in later generations. Still, Walcott, Charles, and Moore remained dangerous elite fighters. Those victories do not settle every historical argument, but dismissing his entire career as fortunate goes too far.

Sports.title: Rick Glaser Tattles on Eddie Hearn to Turki
Sports.content:
“Turki Alalshikh, you have a great event in the deep planning stage for November 20 on Netflix at the Mecca of Boxing Madison Square Garden in New York And as you know, Eddie Hearn is attempting to undermine your great event,” said Glaser on X. “Whatever Hearn’s reasons may be, personal gain, or other motives, it’s causing havoc in Boxing circles, & the sporting public, especially with Hearn saying on video’s “I don’t care who this upsets” as he mouths off. “Turki Alalshikh, you deserve much better than you are receiving from Hearn in his lack of respect. Best regards from Sonya & I.”

The sign-off completes the effect. Having reported Hearn’s alleged misconduct and lavished Turki with praise, Glaser closes the message as though he were sending a polite letter to a school principal.

Nothing in the post proves that Hearn is trying to damage the event for “personal gain” or any other hidden motive. He represents Anthony Joshua, who signed for the fight to take place at a UK stadium. Joshua prefers Wembley, while Turki and Tyson Fury favor New York.

As Joshua’s promoter, Hearn is supposed to argue his position, even when it clashes with Turki’s plans. That does not automatically make him disloyal or disrespectful.

The message presents the dispute as something more serious. In Glaser’s version, Hearn is creating chaos, sabotaging Turki’s work, and failing to show proper gratitude toward the man financing the event. It is an extraordinary display of public loyalty. Glaser did everything except ask Turki to send Hearn to the headmaster’s office.

Sports.title: Julio Cesar Chavez Broke Edwin Rosario Piece By Piece
Sports.content:
Rosario presented the kind of danger Chavez had not encountered. The WBA champion had knocked out Livingstone Bramble in two rounds the previous year and possessed genuine power in both hands. He also attacked Chavez’s opposition before the bout, dismissing many of his previous opponents as “guys right out of the bar.”

Rosario Could Not Keep Chavez Away

Any doubts about Chavez at lightweight disappeared quickly. Rather than feeling his way into the contest, the 25-year-old Mexican closed the distance and began digging hooks into Rosario’s body.

Rosario had success during the third and fourth rounds. He landed several hard punches and briefly forced Chavez onto the ropes, but nothing discouraged the advancing challenger. Chavez absorbed Rosario’s best shots, turned him, and reclaimed control with short combinations. Once the bout moved into close range, the difference became brutal. Chavez did not simply walk forward and throw punches. He slipped Rosario’s right hand, blocked shots with his elbows and gloves, then answered before the Puerto Rican champion could reset.

The body attack gradually robbed Rosario of his movement and power. Chavez mixed hooks downstairs with uppercuts and straight rights to the head, rarely wasting a punch. HBO’s PunchStat count credited him with landing 450 of 743 punches, an extraordinary 61 percent. Rosario connected with 263 of 731.

A Beating That Lasted Too Long

By the later rounds, Rosario’s left eye was swollen shut, his face was cut, and blood covered his nose and mouth. Still, he refused to go down. His courage allowed the punishment to continue far longer than it should have.

Chavez looked almost untouched as he drove Rosario into a corner during the 11th. With the champion taking another sustained attack, his corner threw in the towel. Referee Richard Steele stopped it at 2:38. All three judges had Chavez far in front: 98-92, 99-91, and 100-92.

The performance made Chavez a two-division champion and erased every question surrounding his move to lightweight. He had taken one of boxing’s most feared punchers, neutralized his power, and broken him down without ever needing a knockdown. Rosario brought danger into the ring that night, but Chavez made it disappear.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Sports.title: Moises Garcia Derails Mike Tyson Look-Alike’s Hype Train
Sports.content:
Coming into the bout, D’Angelo Evans was the featured attraction due to his look, his KO percentage, and his most recent knockout that went viral. Most fight fans didn’t know D’Angelo Evans existed until his viral moment.

Back in May 2026, with 2:05 remaining in the second round, D’Angelo “Muscle” Evans landed a vicious left hook that knocked Cesar Villarraga out cold. The match came to an abrupt end as Villarraga was immediately attended to.

Once the knockout video hit the internet, casual fans started comparing Evans to a young Mike Tyson because of his facial features and his KO power. Some casuals went as far as making fake videos claiming Evans is Mike Tyson’s son.

Going into his August 22nd bout, the people who jumped on the D’Angelo Evans hype train were expecting another viral moment. Unfortunately, they witnessed a moment that no one predicted.

Prior to the August 22nd bout, Moises Garcia lost two fights in a row. Garcia went back to the drawing board, and he bounced back by putting together a two-fight win streak.

In his April 2026 fight, Garcia lost by way of unanimous decision to Top Rank’s rising undefeated prospect Deric “Scooter” Davis. Four months later, Garcia was scheduled to fight another prospect who was rapidly gaining momentum.

On the night of August 22nd, with 1:47 remaining in the 5th round, Garcia landed a hard left hook that staggered Evans. D’Angelo Evans showed his inexperience by retreating straight backward rather than clinching or angling out.

Garcia pressed forward and landed a flurry of shots that produced a knockdown. D’Angelo Evans was unable to get up, and just like that, the hype train got derailed.

With the victory, the Puebla, Puebla, Mexico native Moises “Bam-Bam” Garcia improved to a record of (8-6-3, 4 KOs). Now the question is, will the big promotional companies take a chance on matching their rising prospects against the upset-minded Garcia?

For D’Angelo Evans, it’s time to regroup. From an offensive standpoint, Evans has some tools, but to bounce back effectively, he must work on his defense and learn to fight off the back foot.

Ghana News.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO’s Role in Strengthening Corporate Governance
Ghana News.content:
Insight.

Strong governance provides the foundation upon which sustainable organizations are built. CEOs have a responsibility to ensure that decision-making is transparent, accountable, ethical, and aligned with the organization’s strategic objectives.

Governance is not simply a board responsibility. It must be reflected in the conduct of management, the quality of decisions, the treatment of stakeholders, and the systems that hold leaders accountable.

A strong governance culture protects the organization while strengthening confidence among investors, employees, customers, and other stakeholders.

Key Strategies:

1. Strengthen accountability at every leadership level.

2. Maintain transparency in major decisions.

3. Clarify roles between the board and management.

4. Reinforce ethical standards.

5. Review governance practices regularly.

CEO Leadership Actions.

✅ Maintain open and constructive engagement with the board.

✅ Ensure executives understand their governance responsibilities.

✅ Address governance weaknesses promptly.

Actionable Tip.

*Review one major governance process and ask whether it provides sufficient accountability, transparency, and oversight.

Why This Matters?

Strong governance strengthens trust, reduces organisational risk, and supports sustainable long-term performance.

About the Author

Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

Ghana News.title: ‘One day NPP may return to power’ – Afenyo-Markin warns against ‘You do me, I do you’ politics
Ghana News.content:
Alexander Afenyo-Markin

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has warned the government against what he describes as excessive intimidation of the opposition, cautioning that the New Patriotic Party could one day return to power.

Speaking on Joy News’ The Probe on Sunday, he said the government’s approach to accountability could create a cycle of political retaliation if not moderated.

Afenyo-Markin said some NPP MPs were being investigated over what he considers mere allegations.

“The other challenge, really, is that, unfortunately, this government has made intimidation part of its strategy of silencing the minority,” he said.

“I tell you, how are they doing that? I’ll tell you for a fact. A couple of my colleagues are being investigated for things that, in my view, are mere allegations that are not supposed to take their time to those investigative agencies.”

He declined to name the MPs involved but said the situation was worrying.

“There are times that a colleague would have to speak, and he will boldly tell you that, Leader, if I make any submission today, the BNI guys will call me. It’s sad,” he said.

Afenyo-Markin said he had raised concerns about what he described as the excesses of investigations with senior government officials.

“I’ve had cause to complain to some of the senior members of government that, Colleagues, watch some of these things,” he said.

He stressed that the NPP was not opposed to accountability.

“By the way, I have said time without number, and for the umpteenth time, I repeat that our party is not against accountability,” he said.

“As for post-regime accountability, it’s there for everybody.”

But Afenyo-Markin said accountability must not be used to intimidate political opponents unnecessarily.

“I am dealing with the excesses thereto. You see, you can enforce the law with a human face without unnecessarily intimidating the person,” he said.

He argued that MPs should be allowed to perform their parliamentary duties without feeling that their submissions could trigger investigations.

“For instance, a member of parliament should go through investigations normally. You shouldn’t only call him when he’s arguing forcefully on the floor, and you think that that is going against the government,” he said.

The Minority Leader said he was warning against a political culture in which parties retaliate against one another upon gaining power.

He said his comments were intended to draw attention to a possible future that could affect the government itself.

“When I spoke about bail the last time and it was misconstrued to mean that I am aiming at a particular individual or somebody, I was giving my own colleagues a general picture of how these excesses, if they don’t moderate, one day NPP may come into office and there may be some hardliners who may also be pushing that they did it to us, let’s also do it to them,” he said.

“I am not the person who supports this you do me, I do you politics,” he added.

Afenyo-Markin said governments should instead focus on delivering on their promises and tackling Ghana’s challenges.

“I believe that governments that are elected can focus on their mandate of tackling the challenges in our economy,” he said.

“And in tackling, you don’t make your opponents a target.”

Ghana News.title: 101-year-old great-grandma arrested for selling drugs in sachets
Ghana News.content:
Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested a 101-year-old great-grandmother for dealing in illicit drugs.

The great-grandmother, identified as Esther Ogunmabo, was arrested in Ilisan, Ogun State, with retail sachets of skunk, a strain of cannabis, weighing 90 grammes, which she claimed she sold to locals.

A statement on Sunday by the agency’s spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the centenarian told operatives that she started engaging in illicit drug trade after her provisions shop was razed by fire.

The statement partly read, “Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have recorded significant breakthroughs across the country’s land and maritime borders, including the arrest of a 101-year-old great-grandmother for dealing in illicit drugs.

“NDLEA operatives on Saturday, August 15, 2026, arrested a 101-year-old woman, Esther Ogunmabo, in Ilisan, Ogun State, with retail sachets of skunk, a strain of cannabis, weighing 90 grams, which she claims she sells to locals.

“The centenarian told operatives that she resorted to the illicit drug trade after her provisions shop was razed by fire, adding that one of her daughters, who resides in Lagos, arranges the supply of the substance to her every four days, which she in turn sold in bits.”

Babafemi said the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (retd.), directed that the suspect be granted bail and placed on counselling because of her advanced age, while her daughter had been arrested.

In a related development, he said NDLEA operatives in Akwa Ibom State, acting on credible intelligence, intercepted a wooden boat on the high seas on Friday, August 21, conveying illicit drugs to fishing settlements in the Republic of Cameroon.

According to him, three suspects arrested aboard the boat, which was heading to Ine Isu, Ine Mbah and Ine Ikot Itie Udung fishing ports in Cameroon, included Etima Effiong Eekpo, 29, caught with 1.120kg of skunk; Otobong Eyoh Etukudoh, 33, who had 42.060kg of skunk in his possession; and 27-year-old Kingsley Effiong John, who was found with 20 grammes of cocaine cleverly concealed inside a large wrap of edible cassava fufu, alongside 435 grammes of skunk.

“A total of 42.622kg of narcotics was recovered from the trio,” Babafemi added.

In the nation’s maritime space, Babafemi said the agency recorded its first-ever seizure of illicit drugs shipped from Thailand through the maritime corridor, following the interception of two containers of cannabis indica, also known as Loud, at the Apapa and Lekki ports, with a combined street value put at over N4.4bn.

“Both containers were loaded at the Port of Laem Chabang, Thailand, underscoring the emergence of a new trafficking route being exploited by drug syndicates to smuggle synthetic cannabis into the country,” he added.

At the Apapa Port, Babafemi said a container declared to be conveying dry fish, rice, vehicle spare parts, turmeric soap and inverter batteries was found, during a joint examination of the shipment on Friday, August 21, by the NDLEA, Customs and others, to contain 1,090.5kg of Thai Loud packed in 54 cartons comprising 2,181 sachets of 500 grammes each.

“At the Lekki Deep Sea Port, a similar container, which had been placed on the Agency’s watchlist and monitored by its Marine Special Operations Unit, was jointly examined on Wednesday, 19th August. Of the seven pallets found in the container wrapped in black nylon, four were confirmed to be laced with Thai Loud, yielding 96 cartons made up of 400 parcels weighing a total of 400kg. The remaining three pallets contained 798 rims of A4 paper, which had been used as cover for the consignment,” he said.

In the Federal Capital Territory, Babafemi said NDLEA operatives on Saturday, August 22, intercepted three waybill packages containing 24,410 pills of tramadol capsules inside a Hummer bus travelling from Enugu to Zuba.

“A follow-up operation conducted in Niger State led to the arrest of the owner of the consignment, Sunday Eze, 28, in Kontagora, after which he was transferred to Abuja,” he said.

In Ondo, Babafemi said operatives raided a cannabis farm at Ijare forest, Ifedore Local Government Area, on August 19, following the earlier arrest of three suspected cannabis planters at the same location on August 16.

“The team destroyed a total of 10,000kg of skunk cultivated across four hectares of the forest. In a separate operation in the state, operatives, the same day at Ita-Ogbolu, Akure North LGA, recovered 210kg of skunk and a Toyota Camry car with registration number AGL 223 JH belonging to Sylvester Dibiagu Anthony, who is currently at large,” he added.

“A raid at Hadeija Road, Kano, on Monday, August 17, led to the arrest of Chibuzor Madueke, 31, with 98 blocks of skunk weighing 73.3kg recovered from him, while a similar operation by NDLEA operatives at Seme, Badagry area of Lagos, led to the arrest of three family members: Nasiru Tijjani, 52; Moshood Tijjani, 27; and Salami Tijjani, 27, at Ashipa area, near the Seme border, with 48kg of skunk.

“In Abia State, NDLEA officers on Thursday, August 20, raided the residence of Ikechukwu Anthony Iwuno, 36, at Umuobia Olokoro area of Umuahia South LGA, where 14.4kg of Loud, 2.3kg of Colorado, 386 grammes of tramadol and 134 grammes of rohypnol were recovered,” the statement added.

While commending the officers and men of the Ogun, Apapa, Lekki, Seme, Akwa Ibom, Ondo, Oyo, Kwara, Kano, Abia and FCT Commands for the various successful operations, Marwa enjoined them and their colleagues across the country to continue with the current balanced approach to the agency’s drug-control efforts.

Ghana News.title: Polaris Beauty Lounge – Unisex Salon in Accra: Beyond the finished look
Ghana News.content:
At Polaris Beauty Lounge - Unisex Salon in Accra, the most important part of a beauty appointment often happens before the first braid, lash, nail service or massage stroke: the consultation.

There is a brief moment at the start of many beauty appointments when a client shows a reference photo, answers a few questions and expects the visible work to begin. It can feel routine. In practice, that conversation is where comfort, suitability, maintenance and safety are often decided.

A braid can be beautifully parted and still place too much tension on the hairline. A nail design can look polished while the preparation or removal plan is wrong for the natural nail. A dramatic lash map may be unsuitable for the lashes expected to support it, while massage pressure that suits one client may be too vigorous for another. The picture shows the destination; the consultation works out whether the route makes sense.

At Polaris Beauty Lounge - Unisex Salon in Accra, that principle connects services that require very different techniques. From its studio at 12 Brenya Avenue, Floor 2, Accra, the salon's approach begins with practical questions about the client's hair, natural lashes, nails, comfort and routine.

Braids: should neatness come with pain?

No. Secure sections and clean parting matter, but tightness is not a quality standard. A client should be able to say when a braid feels uncomfortable, particularly around the temples and hairline, and the stylist should be prepared to adjust it before the style progresses.

The American Academy of Dermatology warns that frequently wearing styles that pull, including tight cornrows and braids, can lead to traction alopecia. Pain, stinging, crusting, or sections of scalp being pulled upward are warning signs that a style should be loosened or changed.

The issue is not simply whether a client chooses knotless braids, box braids, cornrows, twists or a loose-curled finish. Size, length, extension weight, parting and the condition of the edges all change how a style behaves. Knotless braids typically add extension hair gradually for a flatter transition; cornrows sit close to the scalp; and boho- or goddess-inspired looks include exposed curls that require more attention to tangling and upkeep. None of these labels removes the need for careful tension.

What should be agreed before the first braid is completed?

Size, length, colour, parting, added hair, finish and estimated appointment time should be clear at the start. A reference photo helps, but clients should explain what they like about it, what they do not want and where they are open to adjustment. If discomfort develops, it is better to speak up immediately than to hope the tightness will settle later.

Preparation and aftercare belong in the same conversation: whether hair should arrive washed and stretched, how the scalp can be kept clean, how the style should be protected at night and when it should be removed. The dermatology guidance advises against excessive length and weight and recommends wearing braids for no longer than six to eight weeks. The calendar is only a guide; persistent discomfort is a reason to act sooner.

Nails: why do preparation and removal matter so much?

Because the design is only one part of the service. The condition of the natural nail, the client's routine, the desired length and the maintenance plan should shape the choice between acrylic, Gel-X, builder gel or BIAB-style services, and gel polish. Acrylic can create strength and sculpted length; Gel-X uses pre-shaped soft-gel tips; builder gel can add structure to the natural nail; and gel polish provides colour without substantial added length.

At Polaris Beauty Lounge - Unisex Salon in Accra, nail services include acrylics, Gel-X, builder gel or BIAB-style options, manicures, pedicures and nail art. A useful consultation considers how much clients use their hands, how frequently they can return and whether there is lifting, thinning, discolouration or another concern that should not simply be covered.

Clients can also notice the basics: clean hands and work surfaces, properly disinfected tools and a hygienic pedicure basin. The American Academy of Dermatology's manicure and pedicure guidance advises against cutting or forcefully pushing back cuticles because they help protect against infection. Removal deserves equal care; peeling or forcing off product can injure the natural nail.

Lashes: should the fullest set always win?

Not necessarily. The natural lashes set the limit, and the desired effect should be balanced with what they can comfortably support. A classic set places one extension on each suitable natural lash for a restrained finish. Hybrid combines classic placement with light volume fans, while volume uses fans of fine extensions for greater fullness. Wispy and custom sets vary length and mapping to create texture or shape.

Polaris Beauty Lounge - Unisex Salon in Accra lists classic, hybrid, volume and wispy or custom lash services. Choosing among them is not only a trend decision: eye shape, natural-lash condition and the client's willingness to maintain the set should guide the recommendation. A thoughtful lash appointment adapts the inspiration rather than copying every length and density from a screen.

Is an eyelash-extension appointment only cosmetic?

No. Adhesive and tools are used close to the eyes, so hygiene, product handling and careful application matter as much as the lash map. The American Academy of Ophthalmology notes that possible complications include infection, an allergic reaction to adhesive and temporary or permanent loss of natural lashes.

Clients can ask how tools and reusable surfaces are cleaned, how single-use items are handled, which adhesive is used and how a history of sensitivity will be approached. Active eye irritation should be raised before the service. Burning, marked redness, swelling or pain during or after application should not be dismissed as a normal part of the process.

Extensions shed with the natural lash cycle, so no set remains unchanged. Many clients plan an infill after roughly two to three weeks, although retention varies with the natural lash cycle, application, lifestyle and aftercare. Gentle cleansing, avoiding rubbing or pulling and following product-specific guidance help protect both the set and the eye area.

Massage: is more pressure always more effective?

No. A massage should be matched to the client's goal and comfort rather than treated as a test of endurance. Swedish massage generally uses gentler, flowing work, while deep-tissue massage applies more focused pressure; hot-stone treatments add heat to the experience. The important question is not which sounds most intense, but which is suitable for the person receiving it.

Before the session, clients should share relevant health conditions, recent injuries and areas they want avoided, and should speak up if pressure becomes painful or uncomfortable. The US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health says the risk of harmful effects from massage is generally low, while noting that rare serious effects have been reported, including in some cases involving vigorous massage or people at increased risk of injury.

The common thread: consultation before commitment

Braids, nails, lash extensions and massage use different tools and skills, yet a strong appointment follows the same sequence: a clear request, an honest assessment, a clean process, realistic maintenance and useful aftercare. The reference photo remains valuable, but it becomes a starting point rather than an instruction that overrides the client's hair, eyes, nails, health or lifestyle.

Polaris Beauty Lounge - Unisex Salon in Accra serves clients across Accra, including Dzorwulu, Roman Ridge and Airport Residential Area, with appointments also coming from Cantonments, Osu, East Legon and other parts of the city. Appointments can be arranged online, by WhatsApp or through Instagram, with walk-ins accepted subject to availability.

The finished look still matters. But braids that respect the scalp, nails prepared and removed with care, lashes mapped with the natural lashes in mind and massage pressure adapted to the client tell a better story - one in which the result continues to feel right after the camera is put away.

Ghana News.title: I won’t be the first Minority Leader to suffer attacks – Afenyo-Markin
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, says he is prepared to withstand the political pressure and attacks that come with his position, stressing that he will not be the first Minority Leader to face such challenges.

Speaking on JoyNews’ The Probe, the Effutu MP said he understood the weight of the position when he accepted the leadership of the Minority Caucus and remained committed to discharging the mandate entrusted to him.

“Look, I won’t be the first minority leader to suffer attacks,” he stated.

Mr Afenyo-Markin said political pressure and legal challenges were not unusual for opposition leaders, citing the experience of current Majority Leader and former Minority Leader, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson.

He noted that Dr Ato Forson faced criminal proceedings while serving as Minority Leader under the previous administration but continued to perform his parliamentary duties.

Read Also: ‘Jesus was accused; he kept quiet’ – Afenyo-Markin on Sammy Gyamfi allegation

“In opposition, like I said, was Ato Forson not in court? Was his situation not worse than mine? Do you get what I mean?”

He also pointed to the experiences of opposition leaders in other jurisdictions, saying some had faced even more severe consequences while performing their roles.

“And I said, oh, sir, in other jurisdictions, minority leaders have been arrested. They are in jail. In other jurisdictions, minority leaders are made to report to investigative agencies all the time.”

Mr Afenyo-Markin’s comments come amid a public dispute with Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, who has accused the Minority Leader of making false claims about GoldBod and its operations.

Mr Afenyo-Markin had earlier threatened to pursue legal remedies over what he described as defamatory allegations against him, including comments portraying him as an “extortionist”.

However, when asked whether he would take Mr Gyamfi to court, the Minority Leader adopted a more measured position, saying he would not allow emotions to dictate his response.

“I have made certain statements. I would rely on them without more. Don’t rush. In the Bible, Jesus was accused; wild allegations. He kept quiet and watched them. He could have done anything.”

He said Ghanaians expected a certain level of maturity from him as Minority Leader and that he would not allow personal attacks to distract him from his responsibilities.

“So if I would be carried away with emotions, I would fail. It’s not an emotional game. It’s not a game that somebody attacks you, you should also react. No, you won’t get it.”

Focus remains on GoldBod losses

Mr Afenyo-Markin maintained that the Minority would remain focused on its concerns over the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP) and the reported losses associated with it.

“We want to focus. We promised the people of Ghana that we would file a motion; we have filed that motion.”

He described the Minority’s position as a matter of national interest rather than a partisan campaign against the government.

“This is an important national issue. It is not a partisan call. It is a patriotic call being made by a vigilant minority, however few our numbers.”

The Minority Leader said he understood the responsibilities attached to his position and was prepared to face whatever challenges came with it.

“So, I’m very clear in my mind. The very day I took this job, I knew the weight of it. Everything is on me. I’m ready to live up to the task. I rely on my God, and I thank the party for the support.”

He also called for the planned parliamentary hearing into the reported GoldBod losses to be broadcast live, arguing that the public deserved to follow the proceedings.

“But I pray for a live broadcast of the hearing. We expect that once the motion is carried, there will be a full public hearing of these GoldBod losses,” he stated.

Ghana News.title: Afenyo-Markin to face NPP MPs today over Sammy Gyamfi’s extortion allegations
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin is expected to face questions from members of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Parliamentary Caucus this morning over allegations of extortion made against him by Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi.

JoyNews understands that some senior members of the NPP Caucus consider the allegations serious and are demanding answers from their leader.

The allegations were made at the seat of the Presidency, where Mr Gyamfi addressed journalists in response to claims by the Minority in Parliament, led by Mr Afenyo-Markin, over reported losses associated with the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

Read Also: GoldBod row: Afenyo-Markin threatens legal remedies over “defamatory” attacks

Mr Gyamfi subsequently repeated the allegations in an interview on JoyNews’ Newsfile, where he challenged the Minority Leader to take legal action against him if he believed the claims were defamatory.

Mr Afenyo-Markin has categorically denied the allegations and indicated that he is considering his legal options.

However, his denial appears not to have fully satisfied some senior NPP MPs, who believe the Minority Leader needs to provide further clarification to the Caucus.

Read Also: ‘Jesus was accused; he kept quiet’ – Afenyo-Markin on Sammy Gyamfi allegation

JoyNews understands that pressure from some members has led to a meeting of the NPP Parliamentary Caucus being scheduled for this morning, ahead of Parliament’s sitting later in the afternoon.

The meeting is expected to provide Mr Afenyo-Markin an opportunity to respond to questions from his colleagues and clarify the circumstances surrounding the allegations.

Parliament has been recalled from recess to consider urgent legislative business.

The development comes as the dispute between Mr Afenyo-Markin and Mr Gyamfi intensifies, with the personal allegations threatening to overshadow the Minority’s substantive concerns about the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme and the role of GoldBod in the transactions.

Ghana News.title: GNFS responds to bus crash, trailer fire in Greater Accra
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has responded to two separate road incidents recorded in the Greater Accra Region on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

At Fise, personnel from the Amasaman Fire Station attended to a VIP Yutong bus which had collided with a concrete barricade. The impact caused a diesel leak and partially damaged the bus’s bumper, side glass and side door.

Firefighters contained the hazard and secured the scene. No casualties were recorded, while the cause of the incident remains under investigation.

Later at McCarthy Hill, the Weija Fire Station crew responded to a fire involving a MAN diesel trailer. The fire was brought under control at 8:13 a.m. and completely extinguished at 9:01 a.m.

The head section of the trailer was extensively damaged, while the trailer section also suffered partial damage. No casualties were recorded, and investigations are ongoing.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
