World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: EU, Russian aircraft help Serbia battle wildfires
World.content:
EU crews and a Russian aircraft help Serbia fight major wildfires as extreme heat and drought fuel fires across the Balkans.

Helicopters and firefighters from European Union countries, including crews from the Czech Republic and Romania, are working alongside Serbian teams to contain a large wildfire that has been burning for weeks in Deliblatska Pescara, a protected nature reserve near the capital, Belgrade, according to state media.

The operation continued into Monday as Serbia’s RTS reported that a separate fire in the southwestern Stolovi mountain range had been brought under control, with help from a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 water-bombing aircraft.

RTS said 168 tonnes of water have been dropped on the two fires — 126 tonnes in Deliblatska Pescara and 42 in Stolovi.

Serbia’s Interior Minister, Ivica Dacic, described the situation as “extremely difficult,” according to Euro News, with more than 400 personnel deployed to the area each day.

President Aleksandar Vucic said Belgrade had turned to both the EU and Russia once it became clear Serbia’s own resources were not enough.

“The very second we realised that our own forces were no longer sufficient, we immediately requested urgent assistance from Russia and the European mechanism,” he said.

Serbia is not an EU member but can request aid under the bloc’s Civil Protection Mechanism, a system that allows EU countries to pool emergency resources for disasters. The Serbs formally asked for help on Friday.

The EU response includes four Black Hawk helicopters from Romania, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, along with teams of firefighters and vehicles from Germany and Romania.



Some aircraft were already in action over the weekend and the rest of the deployment, including a German ground team, is due to arrive by Monday.

The EU’s mutual aid system has worked both ways during the summer there. Serbia sent a firefighting helicopter and response team to Spain earlier in the wildfire season, when various blazes stretched the bloc’s own resources thin.

Fires are also burning across the border in North Macedonia, where a blaze near the town of Strumica reportedly damaged at least one home.

“It was devouring everything,” said Ljubce Ivanski, a farmer near one fire, describing how strong winds overwhelmed firefighting planes and helicopters.

The wildfire season now unfolding across the Balkans has been driven by an unusually hot, dry summer that has left much of the region primed to burn.

Just across the border, a large fire that broke out over the weekend between Bosnia and Croatia forced the closure of the main road linking Trebinje to the Croatian tourist city of Dubrovnik, stranding thousands of travellers and prompting the evacuation of nearby villages.

Croatian firefighters crossed the border to help contain the blaze, which has spread across 16km of difficult terrain.

World.title: The right to health in Gaza is now a privilege
World.content:
The devastated healthcare system cannot reach Gaza’s most vulnerable – those who live in displacement camps.

These days, Gaza’s healthcare system is not in the news. There are no violent raids on hospitals, as happened to Al Shifa Hospital, while I was working there in November 2023; there are no bombings of hospital wards or sniper killings in their yards; there are no new claims of secret tunnels under medical facilities.

And yet Gaza’s medical system continues to suffer from worsening collapse. Perhaps, this is the most apparent in displacement camps, where the most impoverished and vulnerable people are forced to live. There, the devastated healthcare system cannot reach those who need it the most, nor are the ill and injured able to come to its few functioning points. Lack of sanitation, safe potable water and constant exposure to unbearable heat or cold make the health crisis even worse.

Last month, I had the opportunity to visit an informal camp that has emerged on the grounds of what is left of Hassan Salama school in the Nasr neighbourhood of Gaza City. The school was devastated after it was bombed along with the neighbouring Nasr school in August 2024, which resulted in the deaths of at least 30 people.

Today, hundreds of people who have been rendered homeless and destitute by the war live in tents in the schoolyard and what is left of the school building. No organisation runs the camp, so there is no provision of any services, including medical ones.

I joined a team of several medics from a local private clinic who offered free check-ups at the camp for a day. Our arrival was warmly welcomed. We saw at least 150 patients.



Complaints ranged from high blood pressure to chronic diseases, such as diabetes and kidney problems, and infections, such as hepatitis and scabies. We also saw many children with chickenpox, gastroenteritis, diarrhoea and respiratory infections.

Although we provided just basic services, the gratitude we received was immense.

For many patients in displacement camps, reaching a doctor has become an almost impossible journey that requires effort, energy and resources that are not available to everyone. Transportation costs, long distances and exhaustion caused by displacement and extreme heat all contribute to some patients delaying medical care, despite their urgent needs.

One patient we had, 46 years old, had a bad foot injury caused by shrapnel and needed crutches to move. He had hypertension problems but could not go to the nearby Al Rantisi Hospital as the facility is partially functioning and offering services mostly to children and oncology patients.

Walking a long distance to another hospital was clearly not an option for him. To get to a doctor to assess his hypertension problem for free and receive a prescription for medication, he would have had to pay at least $8 for transportation to the nearest health facility.

That is a large sum of money for most people in displacement camps who struggle to secure even their daily meals.

Delayed medical care, combined with the lack of medication and difficult living conditions, can worsen diseases and can even be fatal.

All of this could be prevented if basic healthcare returns to Gaza, particularly under the umbrella of a large organisation such as UNRWA.

After the Nakba, UNRWA played an instrumental role in setting up basic healthcare provision for the Palestinian refugees who came to Gaza. It established clinics in each refugee camp, which helped secure a basic level of free healthcare provision.

Before the war, UNRWA ran 22 clinics across the Gaza Strip. According to a recent report, only six of them are operational today. Just 19 of Gaza’s 34 hospitals are partially functioning – and “partially functioning” is the key word here. Most wards in these hospitals are not working because of the destruction they have sustained.

Today, in the whole of the Gaza Strip, there are just 2,200 inpatient beds available to serve 2 million people. Before the war, just Al Shifa Hospital alone had 700 beds.

Various medical services, including lab tests, surgeries and treatments, are no longer available because there are no supplies for them or living medics to perform them.



The destruction of medical facilities and the dispossession of Gaza’s residents have transformed the right to healthcare into a privilege.

We urgently need a healthcare intervention that focuses, not only on rebuilding hospitals, but also on re-establishing basic care clinics and reaching the most vulnerable in displacement camps.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Canada-US trade war: Who wins? Who loses?
World.content:
NewsFeed Canada-US trade war: Who wins? Who loses?

Canada has suspended trade talks with the US after negotiations collapsed, with Trump imposing 50% tariffs on about $20bn of Canadian goods and Ottawa vowing dollar-for-dollar retaliation. Al Jazeera’s Urooba Jamal explains how a trade war could drive up prices and put jobs at risk.

World.title: Ukraine’s allies convene in Kyiv as Zelenskyy seeks air defence boost
World.content:
‘Coalition of the Willing’ leaders gather on Independence Day as Kyiv presses for air defence supplies.

Ukraine will host a meeting with its key European allies to discuss air defence and press for greater pressure on Moscow as Russia continues to escalate missile attacks.

The “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in Kyiv on Monday will be jointly chaired by the leaders of the United Kingdom, France and Germany, with most leaders expected to join by video call and a small number of foreign dignitaries attending in person.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first foreign trip since assuming office last month. European Council President Antonio Costa is also set to attend in person.

Kyiv is expected to seek additional interceptor missiles from allies after weeks of Russian missile and drone attacks that have driven record numbers of the capital city’s residents to metro stations and basements to seek shelter.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made frequent public appeals for more air defence supplies from allies.

The meeting takes place on Ukraine’s Independence Day and comes a day after the country marked National Flag Day, when a group of leaders from Nordic and Baltic countries met Zelenskyy in Kyiv and pledged to boost their support for Ukraine.

Norway said it would provide another 85 billion kroner ($9.1bn) in 2027, matching the support it gave Ukraine this year.

Escalating air attacks

Russia and Ukraine have escalated air attacks with drones and missiles in recent weeks, striking targets far beyond the front line.

Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian logistics sites, carrying out attacks on locations linked to e-commerce companies Wildberries and Ozon.



Ozon reported fires early on Monday at its warehouses in Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.

Russian authorities said two children were killed and nine other people were wounded, including seven minors, when drone debris hit a private childcare centre in Krasnodar on Monday. Debris also fell on apartment buildings and set warehouses alight in the city, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.

In the Stavropol region, which hosts many chemical production facilities, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov said a drone attack on an industrial area had been repelled early on Monday.

In Ukraine, at least two women were killed and five people wounded when a Russian drone hit an electric train in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region on Sunday, regional officials said. An attack on the outskirts of Kharkiv city killed three people and injured eight.

Ukraine’s allies have pledged to boost Ukraine’s depleted air defences in the face of Russia’s growing missile attacks.

Before the meeting, Zelenskyy said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.

“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 – 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” he said.

“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.

World.title: Pakistan’s army chief Munir returns to Iran: Can he break US war deadlock?
World.content:
Pakistan says it can offer a channel between Tehran and Washington, but analysts differ over how much influence it really has.

Islamabad, Pakistan — Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Asim Munir, is traveling to Tehran on Monday for talks with senior Iranian officials, Iran’s Foreign Ministry announced on Sunday.

It will be Munir’s third visit to Iran this year as Islamabad continues its push to mediate an end to the United States and Israel’s war on Iran.

Pakistani officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed to Al Jazeera that the trip would take place but declined to elaborate on its agenda.

The Pakistani military’s media wing, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), as well as the Foreign Ministry and Information Ministry, did not respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment on the visit, which was unusually announced by Tehran rather than Islamabad.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the trip would build on Pakistan’s efforts to “help strengthen peace and security in the region”.

Munir will hold talks with senior Iranian officials during his stay, Baghaei told reporters in Tehran.

The visit follows two phone calls between Munir and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi within four days, on Wednesday and Saturday.

The two officials discussed “regional developments” and ways to strengthen “peace, stability and security” in West Asia, according to Iranian state media.

A third trip this year

Munir’s first visit to Tehran this year came in April, days after the Islamabad Talks, the first direct US-Iran negotiations in more than four decades, ended without a breakthrough.

He returned in May, arriving hours after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there had been “slight progress” in talks between Washington and Tehran.



His latest visit comes as the diplomatic track underpinning the Islamabad MoU has all but stalled, while Washington prepares a new round of sanctions.

The discussions are also expected to touch on this month’s announcement of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which Munir attended in Mecca.

Yemen’s Houthi fighters, whose attacks on shipping lanes have repeatedly threatened to widen the conflict, are also likely to feature in his conversations with Iranian officials. The Houthis are widely believed to receive support from Tehran.

The issue carries particular weight for Islamabad.

Three Pakistani sailors were killed and several others wounded when Houthi forces struck a Tanzania-flagged commercial vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait on August 11.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called the attack a violation of international law and “strongly condemned” it at the time.

Munir is expected to meet Iran’s newly appointed senior military leadership during the visit, according to Reza Afzal Samir, an Iranian journalist tracking the talks.

“He is well positioned to meet Iran’s newer senior military leadership, the new IRGC chief, the new Chief of General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, and the new Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council,” Samir told Al Jazeera, referring to Munir’s expected meetings with Major-General Ahmad Vahidi, Major-General Ali Abdollahi and Mohsen Rezaei respectively.

The officials were all appointed earlier this month.

A lapsed deal

The visit comes at a fraught moment for Pakistan’s mediation effort, which it has led after the war began six months ago.

The 60-day window set out in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed by Pakistan, Iran and the US on June 17, lapsed in mid-August without either side agreeing to extend it.

Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz shut, insisting that Washington first lift its naval blockade, end oil sanctions, unfreeze Iranian assets abroad and halt military threats. Tehran says the US has not met those conditions.

Munir’s trip also coincides with a fresh round of US economic pressure.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail on Monday what American officials have called the “toughest sanctions in history” against Iran, a package he has said is intended, alongside the continuing naval blockade, to “collapse” the government in Tehran.



Iran’s Foreign Ministry has called the plan “economic warfare”.

The trip also follows a month of regional realignment. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, a mutual defence pact under which an attack on one signatory would be treated as an attack on all three.

Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Tehran earlier this month to revive the stalled mediation push but returned without any concrete results.

Tensions elsewhere in the region have sharpened too.

The United Arab Emirates suspended trade and financial transactions with Iran last week after saying it had come under fire from two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory, a claim Baghaei denied.

But Munir’s visit, analysts say, signals that key regional mediators have not given up on efforts to revive talks, either direct or indirect, between Iran and the US, even as they try to balance their own relations with Tehran and Washington.

Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Albusaidi, who, like Munir, has held recent telephone conversations with Araghchi, is scheduled to visit Tehran on Tuesday, Iran’s state-owned IRNA news agency has reported.

What leverage does Islamabad have?

Analysts remain divided on what Munir’s visit can realistically achieve, given Pakistan’s limited ability to enforce any understanding it helps broker.

“Both sides see Pakistan as a country that has helped facilitate dialogue without any personal stake in the outcome, nothing to gain for itself,” said Qamar Cheema, a political analyst and head of the Islamabad-based Sanober Institute. “That gives it a certain clarity, and the ability to offer an off-ramp to everyone involved.”

Javad Heiran-Nia, director of the Persian Gulf Studies Group in Tehran, said Pakistan’s persistence was driven partly by self-interest.

“Pakistan is concerned about escalating tensions and the outbreak of another all-out war between Iran and the United States, which would further destabilise the region,” he told Al Jazeera, pointing to Islamabad’s reliance on energy imports from the Gulf and the risk of disruption to remittances from Pakistani workers there if instability spreads.

Zahid Mehmood, a retired two-star general and Pakistani defence strategist, went further, describing Munir as still carrying Washington’s own offer to Tehran.

“Pakistan is still carrying, in effect, Washington’s off-ramp to Tehran,” he told Al Jazeera. “The country remains the most trusted conduit available.”

Not every analyst sees Pakistan’s role as this central.

Andreas Krieg, an associate professor of defence studies at King’s College London, said Qatar, not Pakistan, remained the primary channel.

“Qatar is leading the political mediation and remains the essential communication bridge between Washington and Tehran,” he told Al Jazeera.

Munir’s contribution, he said, was narrower, a “military-to-military channel into an Iranian system in which the IRGC and wider security establishment have become increasingly important to decisions about war and peace”.



What Munir can deliver, and what he can’t

Iranian journalist Samir said Pakistan had a significant role in Iran’s calculus because of what it could do.

“Why should Iran listen to Pakistan? Because Pakistan still retains the leverage to actually do something and create a real opening for peace, rather than remaining silent and doing nothing,” he said.

Samir also predicted the Munir visit could be followed quickly by movement on Hormuz negotiations. “I think the timeline for a final agreement between Iran and Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is also drawing near,” he said. “If [Munir] succeeds in bringing Iran back to the table, I anticipate a new announcement from Oman and Iran on the strait shortly after.”

Krieg was more cautious about what Munir’s visit could deliver. The most meaningful outcome, he said, would be “confirmation that Iran’s security establishment would abide by a specific Hormuz deconfliction arrangement and restrain escalation through Yemen or Iraq if Qatar can secure reciprocal American movement”.

Without that, according to Krieg, “the communication bridge remains open, but the two sides continue moving towards another coercive cycle”.

Mehmood, the retired Pakistani general, was less equivocal.

“Pakistan is really the only exit card available to either side for their off-ramp,” he told Al Jazeera.

World.title: Salah scores two goals, has two disallowed in first start for Trabzonspor
World.content:
Salah started his first game for the Turkish Super Lig side, whom he joined on a free transfer earlier this month.

Mohamed Salah ‌‌opened his account in the Turkish ⁠⁠Super Lig ⁠⁠with a double as Trabzonspor beat Istanbul Basaksehir 2-1 to clinch their first win ⁠⁠of the season.

Salah, who joined Trabzonspor on a free transfer after leaving Liverpool ⁠⁠following a trophy-laden nine-year spell, also had two goals disallowed in a standout performance on Sunday.

Making his first league start after appearing as a substitute in Trabzonspor’s ‌‌season opener, Salah put his side ahead in the eighth minute, capitalising after Basaksehir goalkeeper Muhammed Sengezer failed to hold on to the ball.

Basaksehir’s Eldor Shomurodov equalised from the penalty spot in the 19th minute, but Salah restored ⁠⁠Trabzonspor’s lead three minutes into the ⁠⁠second half, bursting down the right, exchanging passes with Ernest Muci and slotting the ball into the far corner.

The 34-year-old ⁠⁠winger had a stoppage-time effort chalked off for a foul in ⁠⁠the build-up and another ruled ⁠⁠out for offside when he found the empty net from long range with the goalkeeper upfield for a corner.

He will ‌‌now turn his attention to Thursday’s Europa League playoff second leg away to Ferencvaros after his ‌‌side ‌‌suffered a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg.

World.title: Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit
World.content:
European football chief doesn’t want to lose credibility over FIFA job but says Infantino will face a challenger.

European football chief Aleksander Ceferin says he is “not interested” in replacing Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president must quit or face a leadership challenge.

Ceferin has been vocal in his criticism since Infantino revealed his controversial plans to seek private investment in a company to run FIFA tournaments. However, ruling himself out of a bid to take Infantino’s place, the 58-year-old Slovenian told The Rest is Politics podcast on Monday that he is “not interested because of two reasons”.

“One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point … it’s time to also enjoy life a bit,” he said.

“And the second point is, my credibility is much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position.”

Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down as head of world football’s governing body over his now-abandoned plan to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

Ceferin now believes Infantino’s previously impregnable position is under threat, with him forecasting the Swiss will have to stand down or face a leadership challenge if he seeks re-election at the next FIFA Congress in Morocco in March.

Infantino, a former UEFA secretary-general, had the broad backing of European nations when he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.



But Ceferin, who revealed he has not spoken to Infantino since the controversy started, insisted the current situation was very different.

“There are two options,” he said.

“One option is that he [Infantino] realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option, that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.”

UEFA has been backed by the regional blocs for Asia (AFC) and North and Central America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF).

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and AFC boss Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa are considered two of the most likely challengers for Infantino’s position.

Infantino seeks support in the Caribbean

Infantino was in the Dominican Republic over the weekend for meetings with local and regional football officials, despite Montagliani reportedly asking him to stay away from a youth tournament there.

In video remarks released by FIFA on Sunday, the 56-year-old Infantino appeared to reference the furore surrounding him.

“It’s important to engage, to have a dialogue, to express views and opinions,” he said.

“A lot has been happening the last few weeks, and it’s important that you hear, you listen, and you’re able to also express what your feelings are.

“So I think overall positive, very, very happy with all the support I get here.”

Infantino ⁠⁠laid out his manifesto for re-election as ⁠⁠the champion of poorer football nations.

FIFA has not responded to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment on Ceferin’s criticism of Infantino and FIFA.

Infantino has shown no signs of walking away from the position he has held since 2016 and made it clear that he was banking on ⁠⁠his appeal to the less well-off national associations to win re-election until 2031.

He has support from the African and South American regional blocs and ⁠⁠has looked to sideline the confederations and appeal directly to individual members throughout the crisis.

World.title: Gauff, Fils win Cincinnati tennis titles in run-up to US Open
World.content:
Gauff beat Pegula for her second Cincinnati Open trophy and Fils overcame Tiafoe for his first Masters 1000 title.

Coco Gauff has defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula, 6-2, 6-4, to capture her second women’s Cincinnati Open title as she looks ahead to the US Open starting in New York next week.

Arthur Fils of France overcame American Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0, in the men’s final for his first Masters 1000 title, with Sunday’s decider marking the first time two Black players competed in an ATP Masters 1000 final.

Gauff, who won the 2023 title beating Karolina Muchova and then went on to win her first Grand Slam at the US Open, stormed to a 5-0 lead in the first set before winning it 6-2. Pegula battled back to 5-4 in the second before Gauff closed out the win. Gauff won five of six break points.

The last time two American women played in the Cincinnati final was in 1970, when Rosie Casals beat Nancy Richey.

Pegula’s best finish in Cincinnati came in 2024, when she lost to Aryna Sabalenka in the final.

In Saturday’s semifinals, Pegula beat defending champion Iga Swiatek and Gauff defeated Sara Bejlek to set up the first all-American women’s final at the Cincinnati Open in 56 years.

“I think it was a long journey, but I’m happy,” Gauff said after the match. “I think it’s night and day, the player I was last year to now. I don’t think that this is an indicator that I’m going to do well in New York. Just knowing the quality ones that I had this week, hopefully I can use that experience.”

Gauff had five wins in straight sets in Cincinnati.

“I thought she just played at a really high level and didn’t really have many dips,” Pegula said.



“I didn’t really think I played badly. The more you construct the point [against her], the worse it is because she almost likes to run. It was tough today. A dangerous, confident Coco is going to New York.”

The head-to-head series between Gauff and Pegula is now tied at five apiece. Sunday was their second meeting in a final, with Gauff winning in Wuhan last year.

Meanwhile, Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won twice in Canada, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won in Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

At 22 years old, Fils is the youngest French champion in Masters 1000 history. He became the second French player to win a Cincinnati final, joining Guy Forget in 1991.

“Very happy with that,” Fils said. “It’s been a tough last year. I didn’t play the French Open [due to a hip injury]. I lost early in Washington. People think that I’m done. But here we are. I got the title.”

It was the second time Tiafoe has appeared in the Cincinnati Open final, losing to Jannik Sinner in 2024. He was looking to become the first American man to win in Cincinnati since Andy Roddick in 2006.

Tiafoe saved three championship points in the final game before Fils closed out the victory.

The Frenchman had 11 aces and won 71 percent of his points on first serve. He improved to 10-0 in deciding sets this year and 8-0 against American opponents.

Fils also won his only previous meeting with Tiafoe in Miami last year, also in three sets.

“It feels very good to have a trophy next to me, especially Masters 1000,” Fils said. “Never won one before. You just have to stay positive and find a way to make it work. Being positive is going to help me in the next weeks in the US Open.”

World.title: Divorce, smartphones and control - BBC sees how Taliban run Afghanistan
World.content:
Governor Abdullah Sarhadi gives money to treat a boy's broken arm and hands out funds for a local mosque - then, in his office in northern Afghanistan, an astonishing exchange unfolds.

A young woman tells the grey-bearded former Taliban commander that she wants to divorce her husband, who she accuses of months of abuse and beatings.

She will not take no for an answer.

In a country where girls are banned from secondary education, the 18-year-old argues her case calmly and confidently, her face completely hidden behind a full-face veil and sunglasses.

"If there was any chance to live together, I wouldn't be hereâ¦ I have taken my decision," she says.

After trying to persuade her to avoid divorce, the governor later comments that women are "mindless" and "deficient in intellect", to laughter from the male officials, bodyguards and elders around him.

The moment gives a rare glimpse into the day-to-day realities of the Taliban's rule, five years after they swept aside the US-backed government in 2021.

World.title: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits' of being US state after trade talks collapse
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said Canada wants "the benefits of being a state, without being one" after trade talks between the two countries collapsed late on Friday.

The breakdown of negotiations triggered new 50% US tariffs on a range of Canadian goods. Trump also said American farmers had been charged "massive amounts of Tariffs" for years.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the fresh tariffs a "miscalculation" designed to "hurt and divide us".

Carney confirmed he would match Trump's tariffs "dollar-for-dollar" from 8 September, including levies on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics, saying the US and Canada were now in a trade war.

Both countries were optimistic of a deal earlier in the week, but talks fell apart after both sides accused the other of making last-minute changes.

"They asked too much and they offered too little," Carney said on Saturday. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked."

Trump's latest comments echo his repeated references to making Canada the "51st state" of America since returning to office, sparking frustration among its leaders and residents.

The collapse of the trade talks upended a deeply integrated trading relationship with no clear path to resolution.

"We cannot accept what they've offered and we will not give what they've asked," Carney said.

Trump told Fox News on Sunday that the Canadians were "foolish" to engage in a trade war with the US and think they will "actually win".

The new 50% US tariffs will apply to a range of Canadian goods, in addition to existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber.

They are limited in scope, covering about $20bn (Â£15bn; C$28bn) of imports from Canada, or about 5% in total, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

The prime minister said Canada was retaliating "reluctantly" to protect its interests, with details of counter-measures to be released in the coming days.

World.title: Shein aims for almost $27bn valuation in stock market debut
World.content:
Fast-fashion giant Shein could see its stock market valuation reach almost $27bn (Â£19.8bn) when its makes its debut in Hong Kong on 1 September.

The long-awaited move comes after failed attempts to list in the US and London due to regulatory challenges amid scrutiny of the firm, which has its headquarters in Singapore but was founded in China.

Since it was founded in 2008, Shein has risen to become one of the world's biggest fast-fashion retailers, with customers in more than 150 countries.

The e-commerce giant is known for selling ultra-cheap clothes, backed by a vast network of factories in China that are able to quickly manufacture new products based on the latest trends.

Shein said in a filing on Monday, external that it will offer nearly 280 million shares for between HK$47.60 ($6.07; Â£4.45) and HK$49.50 each.

At the top of the range, the share sale would raise $1.77bn (Â£1.3bn) for the company and give it a market valuation of $26.8bn.

But that is much lower than the $100bn it was worth in 2022, reflecting weaker sales growth and higher costs.

The initial public offering (IPO) is being backed by Wall Street investment giants Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and JP Morgan.

The company will make its highly anticipated debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange after efforts to go public since 2023.

Hong Kong has been revived as "one of the largest IPO markets" after attracting more firms from mainland China, said economics associate professor Feng Qu from the Nanyang Technological University.

Shein is likely to command a higher valuation in Hong Kong than it would in London, where regulatory scrutiny derailed its plans to sell shares there, Feng said.

Chinese companies may also be wary of selling shares in the US as tensions between the world's two largest economies could result in firms being de-listed, he added.

World.title: China probes use of formaldehyde to keep cabbages fresh
World.content:
Authorities in China have launched an investigation into reports of formaldehyde being used to preserve the freshness of cabbages for human consumption.

Officials in the north-eastern Hebei province confirmed that they had verified footage showing individuals dipping cabbages in a solution before loading them onto trucks for transportation.

An environmental blogger first released the footage last week. Using formaldehyde, a colourless chemical used for preserving biological specimens that is known to cause cancer, for keeping food fresh is strictly prohibited in China.

China is the world's largest producer of cabbages, most of which are exported to neighbouring countries in Asia.

Police have taken legal action against the individuals involved, according to state media.

Officials are now moving swiftly to prevent panic and restore confidence by carrying out spot checks on markets across the country.

Chinese state media says investigators will also establish how widespread the practice is and take measures to trace affected vegetables.

Local authorities in Kangbao county said in a statement issued on Saturday: "Any illegal or non-compliant practices discovered will be dealt with strictly in accordance with the law to ensure the safety of the vegetable supply."

Xinfadi market in Beijing, one of the major sources of fresh produce in the capital, issued a statement saying that it had investigated the source of its cabbages, adding that none of the affected vegetables had entered its market.

The incident has generated widespread media attention in China.

An editorial in the People's Daily wrote: "The wholesalers focused solely on their immediate economic interests while completely disregarding the lives and health of consumers. [They] crossed a legal red line and breached the moral bottom line."

China produces well over 30 million tonnes of cabbages each year, nearly half of the world's annual total. Vietnam, South Korea and Russia are among the largest export destinations for the vegetable.

Exposure to relatively high quantities of formaldehyde in some workplaces has been linked to some types of cancer in humans, but the effect of exposure to small amounts is less clear, according to the American Cancer Society.

World.title: Ex-cricket captains urge 'proper medical care' for Imran Khan
World.content:
A group of former cricket captains, including Indian batting legend Sunil Gavaskar and one of England's longest-serving skippers Sir Alastair Cook, have called on Pakistan to ensure its ex-PM Imran Khan be given proper care while in custody.

The cricketer-turned-politician has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges which he denies.

In a letter to Pakistan's current leader Shehbaz Sharif, the 21 former skippers aired concern that Khan, 73, was allowed "only a few hours" at a hospital last week where he was examined by a state-appointed team.

Khan's party has also filed a contempt petition against the government for not giving him access to his own doctors, as ordered by the top court.

The former cricket captains laid out three demands in their letter, the first of which is that Khan be assessed by a medical board directed by Pakistan's Supreme Court â which would include his personal physicians â particularly on the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

They also urged authorities to allow weekly visits by Khan's family, as ordered by the court, "without interruptions or administrative delays".

Finally, they asked that any treatment recommended by the medical board be "provided without delay".

"Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody," read the letter initiated by former Australian captain Greg Chappell.

"Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request."

Among the other signatories were England's Michael Atherton, Michael Brearley, Nasser Hussain, Andrew Strauss and David Gower, India's Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, and Australia's Belinda Clark, Adam Gilchrist, Steve Waugh and Kim Hughes.

Fourteen of the former skippers had also supported an earlier appeal for "humane treatment and proper medical care" for Khan which was submitted in February.

Khan's lawyer claimed at the time that his client had 15% vision left in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

The signatories of both letters had described themselves as "former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field", adding that the bond "transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

He was imprisoned in August 2023 and has faced charges in more than 100 cases, ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts, all of which he and his party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf say are politically motivated.

His jailing sparked large-scale protests by supporters, which were met with a crackdown by authorities.

Pakistan's Supreme Court had on Tuesday directed the government to transfer Khan to a private hospital to be examined by physicians.

He was instead seen by doctors at a government-run hospital in Islamabad, who deemed him "medically fit", before he was moved back to prison.

World.title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 30
World.content:
At least 30 people have been killed after a mound of rubbish at a major waste site collapsed onto nearby homes in Guinea's capital Conakry, the government has said.

Another 22 people were injured, including six seriously, in the city's Dar-es-Salam area.

"Significant" resources and personnel - including the military - were deployed to search for survivors after the collapse at about 02:00 local time following heavy rain overnight, the government added in a statement.

One woman told local media her five children had died in the disaster. There are fears that the death toll will rise further.

Rescuers were later seen using excavators to comb through a mountain of scattered rubbish at the site as local residents gathered nearby.

Guinea's Prime Minister Mamadou Oury Bah visited the scene to assess the situation and oversee the search efforts.

Neighbourhood leader Lancine Sylla had earlier told the AFP news agency that he feared there would be a heavy death toll.

"We have pulled out 18 bodies that were taken to the morgue," he said.

Another landslide at the site killed 10 people in 2017.

World.title: Nearly three million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles
World.content:
Minimalistic retractable door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations.

Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

Made popular by multi-billionaire Elon Musk's Tesla, hidden door handles are designed to tuck seamlessly within the car's door panel and only extend outwards when an owner approaches their vehicle.

The design came under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim".

This could hinder occupants or rescuers from quickly opening the doors in an emergency, such as during a "severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail."

Tesla said it will place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision.

It is not clear if the affected firms plan to make a similar recall for the rest of the world.

The BBC has contacted Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely for comment.

The use of the hidden handle design has "snowballed" after Chinese brands were quick to copy the "sleek" look of Tesla's Model S sedan since 2014, said Tu Le, the founder of consultancy Sino Auto Insights.

The use of warning labels and a software update is more of a "band-aid" than a lasting solution for the issue, he added.

In February, Chinese authorities announced a ban on hidden door handles.

Under new rules due to take effect on 1 January 2027, cars will only be allowed to be sold in China if they have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors.

Tesla's door handles were also involved in a probe by US safety regulators after reports that they suddenly stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars.

In July, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suggested creating a new formal safety standard for all carmakers.

The BBC has contacted the agency for comment.

World.title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' ball sells for £2.5m
World.content:
The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for Â£2.5m.

Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England.

After the game, he told reporters it had been scored "a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".

Maradona later scored what became known as the 'goal of the century' in the same game, dribbling past five England outfield players before slotting the ball past Shilton.

Though it sold for $3.3m (Â£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday, the ball had been expected to fetch nearer $10m (Â£7.3m).

Speaking to Reuters before the auction, Mike Provenzale, a specialist auctioneer at Heritage, said: "It's a true one-of-one item. Arguably the most significant soccer item that exists."

Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser, who refereed the match in 1986, collected the Adidas Azteca ball at full-time and kept it for more than three decades.

In 2023, he signed a letter to confirm it was the only ball used during the match, which has also been confirmed by further independent authentication.

Bin Nasser sold the ball in 2022 for $2.37m (Â£1.74m). Its new owner again put it up for auction in 2023 though it did not sell as bids did not meet the minimum value set.

The shirt worn by Maradona during the same match sold for Â£7.1m at auction in 2022.

World.title: Amnesty demands rescue of worshippers abducted in Niger mosque attack
World.content:
Amnesty International has called on Nigerian authorities to ensure the safe rescue of worshippers abducted at a mosque during the Muslim Friday prayers in Kpenya, Dekara District, Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.

The rights organisation said in a statement published on its verified social media handle that an unspecified number of worshippers were abducted during the attack on 21 August, while residents claimed that more than 80 people may have been taken.

Amnesty urged the Nigerian authorities to act urgently to secure the victims’ release and address the growing wave of abductions targeting rural communities across northern Nigeria.

The organisation said the incident was particularly concerning because the victims were abducted while observing Friday prayers, adding that survivors of previous mass abductions had reported torture, starvation, sexual violence, amputation and being forced to witness or participate in atrocities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Niger State Government confirmed the attack in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Obed Nana, saying suspected terrorists stormed Kpenya Mosque while worshippers were observing Juma’at prayers.

According to the government, the attack occurred at Gidan-Zana and Kpenya communities. Some residents fled into nearby areas, while the attackers abducted an unspecified number of worshippers.

The government said efforts were ongoing to establish the precise number of people abducted.

Governor Mohammed Bago directed security agencies to intensify efforts to locate and safely rescue the victims.

“A joint security operation has been deployed to assess the situation, track the attackers, and facilitate the rescue of the abducted worshippers,” Mr Nana said.

He said the government would not disclose operational details that could compromise the rescue effort, while urging residents to avoid spreading unverified figures and provide credible information to security agencies.

Amnesty also called on President Bola Tinubu’s administration to urgently address the rising incidence of mass abductions in northern Nigeria.

The organisation said at least 1,100 people were abducted between January and April 2026, while acknowledging that estimates vary and may significantly understate the scale of the problem.

Worsening insecurity

The Kpenya attack occurred barely a week after gunmen killed at least 32 people during Friday prayers at a mosque in Ungushi community, Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State. The Imam of the mosque, Malam Aliyu, was also killed.

The incident adds to a series of attacks PREMIUM TIMES has reported in Borgu, particularly around the Kainji Lake National Park and the Niger-Kebbi border corridor.

In January, PREMIUM TIMES reported that at least 35 people were killed and several others, mostly women and children, abducted when gunmen attacked Kasuwan Daji in Borgu.

Following the attack, Governor Bago ordered residents of communities around the Kainji Lake area to evacuate, warning that military operations could be conducted against terrorists operating in the surrounding forests.

In February, PREMIUM TIMES reported that attacks on Feyi, Tungan Makeri and Nkpaso communities over three consecutive days left about 26 people dead and several houses burnt.

ALSO READ: Niger State orders security forces to rescue abducted worshippers in Borgu

In June, suspected Boko Haram terrorists attacked Pissa, killing an unspecified number of residents, abducting others and setting houses ablaze. The attackers also threatened neighbouring communities, including Kabe and Sukumba.

PREMIUM TIMES also reported in April that a medical doctor, Anthony Enahoro, was abducted by terrorists operating around Kainji National Park in Wawa District, Borgu.

In June, armed bandits were also reported to have entered Zugurma, a community near Kainji Lake National Park, where they held a gathering and delivered a sermon. Residents and security analysts linked the fighters to jihadist groups operating in the Kainji forest, although their identities could not be independently verified.

The repeated attacks have heightened concerns over the vulnerability of rural communities, travellers and worshippers in the Borgu-Kainji corridor.

Amnesty International said the Nigerian government must ensure that civilians are protected and that victims and their families receive effective assistance and remedies.

The organisation also urged authorities to strengthen measures to prevent further attacks and ensure that those responsible for the abductions are held accountable.

World.title: Gunmen kill two security operatives, seize rifles in Plateau
World.content:
Two security operatives were reportedly killed on Sunday after some gunmen attacked Tanjol and Tarai communities in Jol District of Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The incident occurred at about 2:30 p.m., with the attackers reportedly seizing the firearms of the slain personnel, according to a report by PUNCH newspaper, which quoted residents of the affected communities.

Residents told the newspaper that security personnel responded to the attack but encountered resistance from the gunmen, leading to a gun battle that lasted several minutes.

“Information available indicated that at least two security operatives were killed during the encounter, while their firearms were reportedly taken away by the attackers,” a resident, John Dalyop, was quoted as saying.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Another resident, Chollom Jerry, said that several people were injured during the attack while a civilian was also reported missing.

He said the incident had heightened fear among residents of Jol and surrounding communities, with residents worried about the safety of their lives and property.

“Residents were worried about the safety of their lives and property, urging security agencies to intensify efforts to protect vulnerable communities in the area,” Mr Jerry said.

Efforts by PREMIUM TIMES to obtain official reactions from security agencies, including the Plateau State Police Command, were reportedly unsuccessful. Sources at the command headquarters in Jos, however, said additional security personnel had been deployed to the affected communities.

Repeated attacks

The latest incident adds to a series of attacks involving civilians and security personnel in Riyom and other parts of Plateau State in recent weeks.

On 4 August, PREMIUM TIMES reported that gunmen ambushed a joint security patrol along the Ganawuri-Sabon Gida Road in Riyom Local Government Area, killing a police inspector and a Nigerian Air Force corporal.

The attackers reportedly took the service rifles of the slain personnel, after which security forces launched cordon-and-search operations in surrounding communities.

Following the attack, troops of Operation Enduring Peace reportedly arrested 19 suspects in Tongoron community, Riyom, for profiling and investigation as the military intensified efforts to identify those responsible for the ambush and recover the stolen weapons.

ALSO READ: Gunmen kill former Plateau councillor in Riyom

The latest attack also occurred in the same local government where PREMIUM TIMES recently reported the killing of former councillor Daniel Chong, popularly known as “Hon. Star,” during a late-night attack on Torok community.

Mr Chong, a former councillor representing Rim Ward, was reportedly killed at about 11:45 p.m. during the attack, while another resident sustained gunshot injuries.

The renewed attacks have heightened concerns over security in Riyom, which has recorded repeated incidents involving armed groups and attacks on security personnel.

The seizure of service rifles in the latest incident also raises concerns over the proliferation of firearms and the possibility of weapons taken from slain security personnel being used in subsequent attacks.

Security agencies are yet to publicly provide details on the identities of the slain operatives or the circumstances surrounding the attack as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: 2027: Kwankwaso knocks APC campaign council, says election choice between oppressors, oppressed
World.content:
Former Governor of Kano State and vice presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has criticised the newly constituted All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 general election.

In a statement posted on X on Sunday, Mr Kwankwaso said the election is an impending battle between the “oppressed Nigerian masses” and political figures who have sustained policies responsible for widespread economic hardship.

Mr Kwankwaso argued that the composition of the campaign council, which includes key figures associated with the current administration, gives citizens a clear preview of the choices ahead in 2027.

“The council brings together many of the same political actors who have supported, defended or participated in the present administration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Their coming together raises a fundamental question: what exactly are they asking Nigerians to vote for in 2027, a new beginning, or the continuation of the same system that has brought severe hardship to our people?” Mr Kwankwaso questioned.

The former governor said families are struggling with food inflation and basic costs of living, young Nigerians face diminishing job opportunities, and businesses, farmers, and public services—such as healthcare and education—remain under severe strain due to ongoing insecurity.

“This ruling campaign structure presents another scenario between the oppressors and the oppressed,” Mr Kwankwaso asserted. “We must use it come the 2027 election to reject continued oppression and demand accountable, people-centred governance. If Osun people can do it, so can all other parts of the country.”

Appeal to Abdul’aziz Yari

In a direct message to former Zamfara State Governor, Abdul’aziz Yari, who was appointed Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Kwankwaso urged Mr Yari to reconsider taking up the assignment.

Mr Kwankwaso stated that Mr Yari, as a prominent northern leader and former governor, is fully aware of the socioeconomic and security collapse in the North-west and across the federation.

“I particularly appeal to my brother, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, who has accepted to serve as Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, to reflect deeply and reconsider accepting this responsibility,” he said.

“As a former governor of Zamfara State and a prominent leader from the North-west, I believe Senator Yari has a clear understanding of the devastating consequences of insecurity, poverty, unemployment, displacement and the destruction of livelihoods in the region and the country at large.

“I therefore will be surprised if in his good conscience, [he] will lead a campaign whose principal objective is to secure the continuation of a government under which many of the people he once governed… remain trapped in these challenges”, Mr Kwankwaso said.

Concerns over neutrality of institutional heads

Mr Kwankwaso also raised concerns over the inclusion of key public finance officials in the partisan campaign council, pointing out the appointment of Zacch Adedeji, Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, and Tanimu Kurfi, Director-General of the Budget Office of the Federation, into the campaign’s financial and fundraising organs.

Highlighting the need for institutional integrity, Mr Kwankwaso questioned how public officials managing national treasury infrastructure could simultaneously serve active political roles without compromising public trust.

“The leadership of critical public institutions demands neutrality, integrity and public confidence,” Mr Kwankwaso maintained. “It is therefore legitimate to ask whether the responsibilities of senior officials entrusted with managing public revenue and national finances can appropriately coexist with senior partisan campaign roles.

“The government and the APC should explain how such arrangements are consistent with institutional neutrality and public trust”, he stated.

Mr Kwankwaso expressed confidence in the electorate, declaring, “Ultimately, no campaign council is more powerful than the Nigerian people.”

Reaction

Responding directly to Mr Kwankwaso’s statement on X, former presidential media aide Bashir Ahmad, countered Kwankwaso’s assertion that the upcoming contest would be between “the oppressors and the oppressed.”

​Mr Ahmad stated that Mr Kwankwaso’s criticism of the APC Presidential Campaign Council “does little to advance serious national debate.”

“I respectfully disagree with this characterisation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council. It is fair to scrutinise government and demand better governance, but reducing the 2027 contest to a simplistic battle between oppressors and the oppressed does little to advance serious national debate.

“The APC’s campaign council should be judged by the policies, programmes and vision it presents to Nigerians, not merely by the political identities of the individuals serving in it and the 2027 election should be a contest of ideas, records, competence and competing visions for Nigeria’s future.

“On Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, we all believe he is experienced enough to make his own judgement about whether to accept a national responsibility. His experience as a former governor and senior political leader should be seen as an asset to the political process, not automatically interpreted as complicity in every challenge confronting the country.

“Nigerians are not passive victims waiting for political actors to tell them what their choices are. They are intelligent citizens capable of examining the records of governments, comparing alternatives and deciding for themselves what direction they want the country to take.

“The 2027 election should therefore be about performance, ideas and the future of Nigeria, not inflammatory labels of ‘oppressors’ and ‘oppressed.’” Let Nigerians decide”, Mr Ahmad stated.
