World.title: New Zealand's PM Christopher Luxon proposes banning children from using social media
World.content:
New Zealand's Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has unveiled a proposed law banning children younger than 16 from using social media platforms, citing what he said Monday (August 24, 2026) was “harm being done to a generation” of young people.

However, the bill hasn't yet attracted enough support to pass into law because two of the three parties in Mr. Luxon's coalition government will vote against it. Passage would require support from Opposition lawmakers, who have yet to decide how they would vote.

“There also wasn't enough time for lawmakers to hold a vote on the proposal before Parliament dissolved on Oct. 1 ahead of November's election,” Mr. Luxon said. Bills are required to pass three rounds of voting, usually over a period of months, before they become law.

If reelected, Mr. Luxon is seeking to make his government the latest worldwide to enact age restrictions for social media platforms after dozens of countries have either introduced or are mulling such measures. He said 2025 research showed a third of New Zealand teenagers spent at least five hours a day on social media.

“Social media is exposing them to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with and it's affecting their family life, mental health, sleep, and education,” Mr. Luxon said.

The proposal would require social media platforms including Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Facebook, to “take reasonable steps” to check users were older than 16, according to material supplied by Mr. Luxon's party Monday (August 24). This could include “existing account information, facial age estimation, digital ID services and formal ID”, the material said.

Excluded from the proposed law are messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, online gaming platforms like Roblox and AI apps with productivity uses, including ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot.

No penalties are proposed for parents or children, but tech firms could be fined up to 10% of their global revenue for failing to meet their obligations. Platforms regularly used by children would be required to assess and report on the risks their networks posed, Luxon said.

Mr. Luxon's government has mulled such a law since Australia's world-first social media ban for under 16-year-olds took effect in December 2025. However, it's been vehemently opposed by the other two parties that make up the government along with Luxon's center-right group National — libertarian ACT and populist NZ First.

Both minor parties repeated on Monday (August 24) their plans to vote against the law. Lawmakers from the largest Opposition party, center-left Labour, haven't decided if they'd vote for it, leader Chris Hipkins said.

Since Australia's law came into force, countries including Canada, Brazil and Indonesia have enacted bans too, while many other countries are studying or developing laws. Child safety advocates and some parents have welcomed age restrictions, while privacy groups say the rules can be cheated and that forcing users to supply identification raises privacy concerns.

In January, a month after Australia's ban was enacted, social media platforms told an Australian regulator they had revoked access to about 4.7 million accounts identified as belonging to children.

Mr. Luxon's government enacted a ban in 2024 on the use of cellphones during the school day for students of all ages.

World.title: Keralam govt approves SOP for euthanasia of rabid, incurably ill stray dogs
World.content:
The Keralam government has approved standard operating procedures (SOP) for mercy killing of rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous stray dogs. The SOP, approved recently, relies on the Supreme Court's Order in May this year allowing euthanasia in such cases.

A stray dog management committee, which will be formed in every local body, will bear the responsibility of deciding whether mercy killing has to be done in a particular case.

As per the relevant portions of the Supreme Court judgment on May 19, 2026, "In areas where the population of stray dogs has assumed alarming proportions and where incidents of dog bites or aggressive attacks have become frequent and pose a continuing threat to public safety, the authorities concerned may, subject to due assessment by qualified veterinary experts and strictly in accordance with the provisions of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023 and other applicable statutory protocols, take such measures as may be legally permissible, including euthanasia, in cases involving rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably aggressive dogs, so as to effectively curb the threat posed to human life and safety."

The stray dog management committee, which will have the local body chairperson as its head and the secretary as the convener, will include the respective ward councillor, veterinary officer and medical officer of the local body, Animal Birth Control (ABC) centre project-in-charge officer and a representative of the Animal Welfare Board.

Procedure norms

The procedure for mercy killing should be carried out by a qualified veterinary surgeon. Only sodium pentobarbital or thiopental sodium should be administered intravenously. Other chemicals or methods which could cause pain should not be used. All local bodies will have to maintain a separate register to record cases of euthanasia of stray dogs. The register will have the information about each such dog, including the area from which it was caught, photographs and the exact reasons for deciding on euthanasia.

The dogs which are caught for euthanasia have to be kept for two-three days in the local body's isolation kennels or an ABC centre. During this period, approved agencies or animal lovers who are willing to take care of the dog can claim responsibility for the dog. The mercy killing should not be carried out in the presence of other dogs.

The SOP cites the apex court ruling regarding legal protection for the officers who are carrying out the act. As pet the ruling, the officials are "entitled to due protection for acts performed by them in good faith and in bona fide discharge of their official duties and compliances carried out pursuant to the present order and the earlier orders passed by the Court.. Accordingly, no First Information Report, criminal complaint or coercive proceedings should be initiated against such officials" .

The State-level ABC Implementation and Monitoring Committee will carry out the auditing of mercy killing of stray dogs in local bodies.

World.title: Hopes of rescuing crew members alive fade around sunken cargo ship in Bay of Bengal
World.content:
The search and rescue operation for the sunken Panama-flagged bulk carrier in the Bay of Bengal has been expanded to cover a wider area, as hopes of finding the 22 remaining crew members alive diminish with every passing hour.

Despite days-long search operations in the Bay of Bengal, neither the debris of the ill-fated vessel nor any of its 22 missing crew members could be traced, an Indian Coast Guard (ICG) spokesperson said on Monday (August 24, 2026).

The Indian Navy and the ICG are jointly coordinating the search and rescue operation about 700 km east of Visakhapatnam in the Bay of Bengal.

“On August 22, two Chinese nationals were rescued after a distress call was received from MV Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530), which had sailed with iron ore from Paradip for China on August 20. The vessel sank at a location in the Bay of Bengal where the sea is extremely deep,” said Commandant Amit Uniyal, ICG spokesperson.

According to Commandant Uniyal, apart from an oil slick detected near the reported position of the vessel and two floating liferafts spotted by the Indian Navy’s P-8I maritime reconnaissance aircraft, no other trace of the vessel or its crew has been found.

He said the search area was being expanded as the operation progressed, with the passage of time making the rescue effort increasingly challenging.

The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC), Vijaya Puram, had received information about the loss of communication with MV Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530) and a request for search and rescue at 11:48 a.m. on August 22, 2026. Subsequently, a merchant vessel sailing nearby was diverted to the location, resulting in the immediate rescue of two crew members.

Thereafter, coordinated search and rescue efforts by the Indian Navy and ICG have yielded no further success.

MV Ocean Winner had 24 crew members on board, comprising 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.

The bulk carrier MV Ocean Winner has an overall length of 225 metres and a beam of 32.26 metres, with a cargo-carrying capacity of around 73,000 tonnes.

The vessel is owned by a company based in Fujian, China and is covered by Protection and Indemnity (P&I) insurance, which provides compensation for loss of life and other liabilities.

World.title: TMC MP Mahua Moitra moves Supreme Court alleging eviction from Nadia Circuit House in Bengal
World.content:
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra made an urgent oral mentioning before the Chief Justice of India’s Bench on Monday (August 24, 2026) alleging that the Nadia district administration in West Bengal has evicted her from her constituency accommodation in the dead of the night. Ms. Moitra is a Lok Sabha MP from Krishnanagar in Nadia district.

Ms. Moitra said that on August 14 she was directed by the Nadia district administration to vacate the Circuit House in Nadia district late in the evening. In a video message, Ms. Moitra stated that as an MP of the Nadia district she was entitled to a stay at the Circuit House and she was not vacating it as per district administration orders. In her messages, Ms. Moitra repeatedly claimed that a crowd had gathered outside the Circuit House chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’.

The counsel said that the eviction of a sitting MP from her constituency accommodation in Circuit House by local officials, who took the law into their hands, was a direct attack on federalism in violation of court orders.

The counsel argued that the eviction took place despite a High Court order in her favour.

The lawyer sought an urgent hearing of Ms. Moitra’s writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution to protect her fundamental rights against State action.

“A sitting lady MP was evicted from her constituency accommodation by local officials, the Additional District Magistrate and the District Magistrate, in the dead of the night at 11 p.m. This requires an independent investigation and comprehensive directions,” Ms. Moitra’s counsel submitted.

The Court said it would look into her plea for early listing.

World.title: Police take BJP leaders into custody as they try to lay siege to Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru
World.content:
Several BJP leaders, including leaders of the Opposition in both the Houses of the State legislature, were taken into custody by the police on Monday (August 24, 2026) when they tried to lay a siege to Vidhana Soudha, demanding the resignation of Minister B. Nagendra.

BJP State President B.Y. Vijayendra, former Deputy Chief Minister Dr. C.N. Ashwath Narayan, Opposition Chief Whip in Council Ravikumar, MLC C.T. Ravi and former minister B. Sriramulu besides a host of party workers were among those taken into custody by the police.

The BJP members, who have been staging a protest both inside and outside the Legislature demanding resignation of Mr. Nagendra in the wake of him being chargesheeted in the case of embezzlement of funds meant for welfare of ST communities, stepped up their campaign on August 24. They gathered at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru and later marched towards Vidhana Soudha to lay siege.

They indulged in slogan shouting and accused the Congress government of cheating Dalits by shielding Nagendra.

There was a minor scuffle when the police tried to stop the protesters from marching forward in view of prohibitory orders in force due to the ongoing monsoon session of the state legislature.

Finally, the police took the leaders and a large number of protesting members into custody to foil their bid to lay siege to Vidhana Soudha. The leaders were released later.

More than 500 police personnel, along with KSRP platoons, had been deployed around the legislature complex and security had been tightened in and around Vidhana Soudha to prevent protesters from barging into its premises.

Before being taken into custody, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok alleged that the situation resembled the Emergency days when rights of people had been curtailed. He declared that the Opposition parties would not stop their protest till Mr. Nagendra quits.

Metro entrances blocked, reopened

Amid the protest, two entrances at the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar metro station (Vidhana Soudha) were temporarily closed from 10.17 a.m. following the advice from local authorities, the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) said.

Entrances E and F, including the lift entrance, were closed temporarily. However, by 12.45 p.m. all entrances were fully reopened and normal passenger movement was completely restored across the station.
