SOCAR has also faced questions over transparency in the past, including in connection with the Azerbaijani Laundromat scandal.

Azerbaijan’s state oil company is also entering Uzbekistan’s retail fuel market and plans to establish a network of filling stations there. At the same time, the company plans to cooperate with BP and Uzbekneftegaz on the Ustyurt field. SOCAR has also faced questions over transparency in the past, including in connection with the Azerbaijani Laundromat scandal. Other projects: Other businesses entering the Uzbek market include the Matanat-A gypsum plant, Landau STEAM schools, the Sur gold and silver processing plant, Gold Fresh Fruits orchards, the Baku City residential complex and other projects. Some are being implemented as public-private partnerships.

Statements by the two presidents

President Ilham Aliyev said in a statement to the press that relations between the two countries were built “on a very solid foundation, both spiritually and materially”. He said the range of projects under discussion in energy, transport, investment, tourism, mining, automotive manufacturing, agriculture, processing and banking gave the cooperation an “unprecedented character”.

Aliyev said that on every visit he was struck by the rapid development of Tashkent and Uzbekistan as a whole. He said increasing bilateral trade to $1bn was “no longer a dream of the distant future, but a target that can be achieved within a few years”. He also highlighted Mirziyoyev’s particular role in attracting investment to Karabakh and invited him to make a state visit to Azerbaijan at a time convenient to him.

Shavkat Mirziyoyev described Aliyev’s visit as a “historic event”, saying the “Treaty on Eternal Friendship” was evidence of this and that the provisions on strategic partnership and alliance were being backed up by concrete action. In his remarks, he highlighted a threefold increase in bilateral trade over the past five years, the goal of raising it to $1bn, the joint development of the Middle Corridor, and the idea of creating a separate Azerbaijani-Uzbek corridor across the Caspian Sea with a single operator.

Mirziyoyev also said the two countries spoke “with one voice” on the international stage. He described Azerbaijan’s full participation in the consultative meetings of Central Asian heads of state as a historic step and praised Aliyev’s policy of restoring Azerbaijan’s territorial integrity, as well as the meeting in Washington and the declaration signed there.

Hikmet Hajiyev, a representative of the Azerbaijani presidential administration, said before and during the visit that relations between the two countries had reached a new level: moving from strategic partnership to alliance and then to “eternal friendship”. He said this was the first such step in the history of Azerbaijani diplomacy. According to Hajiyev, the “eternal friendship” that had already existed de facto between the two peoples had now been formally enshrined at the political level as well.

World.title: “When the state serves an oligarch, villages and cities empty out.” Video podcast “Protests in Georgia”
World.content:
Video podcast “Protests in Georgia”

The traditional pro-European “Saturday march” in Tbilisi on August 22 was dedicated to Georgian citizens who have left the country in search of work and better opportunities.

Participants said the growing emigration is driven by the policies of the ruling Georgian Dream party, which they say have pushed the country away from the European integration path enshrined in the Constitution.

Many blame the party’s founder and honorary chairman, oligarch Bidzina Ivanishvili, personally.

“Villages and cities are emptying out when the state serves Ivanishvili” — this was the central message of the march, reflected in the slogans and statements by speakers.

Organisers announced that throughout September, the traditional “Saturday marches” will be held in support of Georgian emigrants.

For more than a year and half – since November 2024 – continuous protests have been taking place in Georgia, with demonstrators demanding that the country return to the path of European integration. The results of the parliamentary elections held in autumn 2024 are still not recognised by part of Georgian society. Every evening thousands, and often tens of thousands, gather in Tbilisi and several other cities. Over this time dozens of participants have been detained, many have faced criminal charges, and some have been sentenced to prison terms. For the first time in the history of independent Georgia, the country has up to 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the popular outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti. In 2025 she was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer. Protesters demand the release of all political prisoners and the repeal of all anti-democratic laws adopted over the past two years. To suppress the protests, the ruling Georgian Dream party has increasingly tightened repression against civil society and the media. However, protests in various forms continue.

News in Georgia

World.title: Armenia’s new parliament: balance of power, tools of government and opposition’s dead end
World.content:
Balance of power in Armenia’s new parliament

The parliamentary election results in Armenia have confirmed the continuity of the country’s political system while exposing deep structural contradictions. Political competition has shifted decisively towards intense polarisation. The National Assembly risks turning into little more than a platform for mutual accusations resembling a television talk show, rather than the country’s highest legislative body.

Political analyst Alexander Iskandaryan’s assessment

Continuity of the system, limits of influence and a fragmented opposition

“The new National Assembly has retained the key feature of its predecessor. The Constitution allows the ruling Civil Contract party to make almost any decision on its own, except on issues that require a constitutional majority. The two opposition factions — former president Robert Kocharyan’s Armenia Alliance and businessman Samvel Karapetyan’s Strong Armenia — have access to the media and the parliamentary platform, and can openly express their views and criticise the government. However, they have no real leverage over current policy.

The opposition forces have undergone a reshuffle. In the eighth National Assembly, Kocharyan’s faction held the largest number of seats. In the new parliament, however, it is the smaller of the two opposition factions. They are also unlikely to build a stable coalition or an “umbrella” structure. Because of their different origins and the lack of a practical basis for cooperation, even if they unite, they will not secure 50% of the seats needed to take the initiative. A long-term alliance is impossible. In 35 years of the Third Republic, the opposition has never managed to produce a successful example of unity. The minority is therefore left with little more than keeping the protest movement alive.”

Legitimacy, voters and the government’s narratives

“The ruling party has significant external legitimacy. This includes recognition of the election results by the US, EU, Turkey and Azerbaijan, as well as Russia’s refusal to withhold recognition from Nikol Pashinyan. The ruling force also relies on support from the bureaucracy. In fact, bureaucratic legitimacy has grown stronger. Civil servants clearly understand their ties to the political leadership and recognise the risks that a change of elites could bring.

At the same time, the government’s social legitimacy remains low. Kocharyan won 10% despite his high negative rating, while Karapetyan’s party, hastily assembled over six months with its leader under arrest, won a quarter of the vote despite high turnout. This is a serious signal of the level of public dissatisfaction.

Realising that its support will not grow, the government abandoned any real ideology. Political strategists pragmatically discarded the “high-minded Yerevan intelligentsia”, which would not have voted for the government anyway and would not have gone to the polls. Instead, they focused on their target audience: residents of small towns and villages with lower levels of education, young people and older generations.

To maintain control, the government uses several narratives:

“Peace versus war” — portraying opponents as the “party of war” and frightening voters with the prospect that an opposition victory would lead to a new war in September.

“Democrats versus oligarchs” — selectively labelling businesses. Wealthy entrepreneurs who support the government are simply called “businessmen”, while any affluent opponents are automatically branded “oligarchs”.

“Europe versus Russia” — systematically linking the entire opposition to Moscow. Karapetyan is portrayed this way because he came from Russia, Gagik Tsarukyan because of his ties to Belarus, and Kocharyan as Putin’s personal friend.

Accusing voters of supporting the opposition solely for money. This new level of polarisation has emerged in official statements by the authorities.”

The government’s geopolitical narrative and the opposition’s dead end

“The government’s anti-Russian discourse found fertile ground. These sentiments had been developing for years, and the events of 2020 and 2023 — the war in Karabakh, followed by the exodus of the entire Armenian population from Nagorno-Karabakh — only strengthened them.

At the same time, people across the post-Soviet space have traditionally associated the word “European” with quality and development: European healthcare, European education, European cars and so on. The government has effectively exploited this perception. Direct public support for Pashinyan from senior US officials, up to and including the US president, also played an important role.

The opposition has found itself in a strategic dead end. It cannot openly say “we are pro-Russian” or “we are not pro-Russian”. Unable to reject the geopolitical trend that enjoys broad public support, opposition parties have had to adapt and repeat that they are “also in favour of cooperation with Europe, but for a more carefully calibrated policy”.

Personal attacks instead of alternative programmes

“Instead of substantive work, the opposition is sliding into negative rhetoric and personal attacks: who is corrupt, who got their wife a job, who owns which flat and who once “didn’t even have a washing machine”. Armenian society knows perfectly well how the bureaucratic hierarchy works, so such “exposés” do not work. All these scandals only play into the government’s hands, allowing it to say: “Look who we have to work with in parliament.”

A constructive alternative would be to develop concrete programmes in different areas — healthcare, pensions, the economy, the army and so on. Even if the ruling majority rejects, say, 15 such professional programmes in a row, a systematic effort to offer solutions will eventually resonate with society. For now, trolling has replaced politics.”

Real state priorities: security, energy and meritocracy

“While parliament is busy trolling, the country’s key problems remain unresolved. One of them is security.

It is wrong to call the situation with Azerbaijan peace. You can see what real peace looks like on the border with Georgia, for example: people can cross freely using an ID card, while there are no transport corridors, European observers, military guards or concrete walls, even though 30% of the border remains undelimited. With Baku, however, there is only a state of “no war”. That is far from peace. At the same time, Azerbaijan is rapidly expanding its military capabilities in every sphere, including its air force.

Armenia needs to make foreign policy decisions and find ways to overcome the energy crisis.

Relations with all four neighbours — Russia, Turkey, Azerbaijan and Iran — are in crisis. Meanwhile, the Armenian-American TRIPP “Trump Route” project — a transit route through Armenia — remains little more than a political narrative. At the same time, launching new facilities, such as an AI data centre in Hrazdan, could create an acute electricity shortage that talk of American small modular nuclear reactors alone cannot solve.

In the Armenian city of Hrazdan, Firebird AI’s artificial intelligence factory has begun operations. The facility is the largest AI data centre in the region. The first phase of the project, worth more than $500 million, uses advanced NVIDIA accelerators and server equipment from leading global manufacturers. Some experts believe the factory’s launch could put additional pressure on the country’s energy system. (firebird.ai)

The state needs a competent administration to overcome these challenges.

The country needs to embrace meritocracy, appointing people based on competence rather than loyalty.

Finally, the country’s leadership needs to reconsider its attitude towards citizens.

Nikol Pashinyan is the prime minister of all Armenians, not just the voters of Civil Contract. The claim that people could only have voted against the government in exchange for money is false and toxic. The government now faces a vast array of real problems. Its first task is to recognise the scale of those challenges and start addressing them.

Balance of power in Armenia’s new parliament

World.title: Anea the raccoon’s favourite activity at Tbilisi Zoo – video
World.content:
Anea the raccoon at Tbilisi Zoo

Raccoons love water. You can often see them swimming, wetting their fur or carefully washing their paws. Anea, a resident of Tbilisi Zoo, is no exception.

On hot days, Anea particularly enjoys dipping her paws in water and having a cool shower. So her keepers set up an improvised shower in her enclosure, which, as you can see in the video below, delighted her.

There is a metal container in her enclosure for drinking water, but who says she cannot take a bath in it too? Despite its small size, Anea fits perfectly inside, happily splashes around in the water and uses it to escape the summer heat. After noticing the raccoon’s love of bathing, her keepers have already ordered a bigger “bath”.

Tbilisi Zoo‘s history spans nearly a century. It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status.



The zoo was originally built on 70 hectares in the Vere River gorge. Over the years, the expansion of the capital — and later the devastating flood of 13 June 2015 — significantly reduced the territory of the old zoo. Today, it covers five hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals, each with its own story. In this video series, we will introduce you to the residents of Tbilisi Zoo.



We will show how their day unfolds, how they interact with other animals and people, and how their behaviour changes depending on the weather and the season. Get ready to hear many fascinating stories.

Anea the raccoon at Tbilisi Zoo

World.title: Opinion: ‘Moscow’s main fear is that Armenia will choose European Union’
World.content:
Opinion on Russia’s demand for a referendum in Armenia

In recent days, Russia‘s demand for Armenia to hold a referendum on whether the country should remain in the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) or choose the European Union has increasingly been seen as a threat. Experts from the “Armenian Council” think tank made the assessment in an article.

Russia has long demanded such a referendum, including at the highest level. But there are now threats to initiate proceedings concerning Armenia’s membership of the EAEU. Decisions within the bloc require consensus, and Yerevan has the right to veto them.

“Russia’s main phobia is that the situation will deteriorate over time, leading the Armenian people to choose the European Union,” the authors argue.

They stress that this is not only Russia’s “main phobia”, but also its “main misconception”. The analysts believe that even the “economic pressure and blackmail” that Russia began applying to Armenia in May, during the pre-election period, have not changed Armenian public opinion. They cite the results of the parliamentary election on 7 June as evidence: Armenia’s ruling party won, rather than pro-Russian forces.

Ahead of Armenia’s parliamentary election, Russia imposed restrictions on imports of Armenian agricultural products. It also banned imports of flowers, Jermuk mineral water, certain alcoholic drinks and fish products. The authorities justified the measures by citing failures to meet required quality standards. However, Armenian experts and officials viewed the issue in the context of the election campaign. They therefore expected the pressure to end after the election. But that did not happen. Moreover, Russia introduced new restrictions after the election. At the same time, in early June, four EAEU member states called on Armenian authorities to hold a referendum as soon as possible on choosing between the Eurasian bloc and the EU. Yerevan responded that there were currently no grounds for such a vote because Armenia’s European integration process had not yet reached the stage at which citizens could make a choice. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has repeatedly said that Armenia should first obtain EU candidate status or, at the very least, put the issue on the agenda. However, Moscow continues to insist. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin said the EAEU expects Armenia to hold a referendum by December. Otherwise, the bloc’s leaders would “take this fact into account when determining appropriate further joint steps”. He said a report on the possible consequences of suspending the EAEU Treaty in relation to Armenia would be discussed at the December meeting of the Supreme Eurasian Economic Council.

Armenia’s prime minister spoke about a referendum on EU membership

“No one in Armenia has ever talked about holding a referendum on EAEU membership or an alternative in the form of the EU.

On 9 January 2025, when the Armenian government discussed and approved a bill to launch the EU accession process, Prime Minister Pashinyan said:

“Armenia can begin the process of joining the EU only if a certain number of referendum participants vote ‘yes’ in accordance with the procedure established by the Constitution.”

Senior Armenian officials later repeated this point on various occasions.

The key point is that Armenia will hold a referendum on joining the European Union, not on whether to remain in or leave the EAEU.

This fundamental difference significantly changes the forecasts for the expected outcome. However, if Armenia votes to join the EU, it will inevitably leave the EAEU at some stage of the subsequent process.”

Russia is pushing for a referendum on a different question

“Armenia’s willingness to hold a referendum on EU membership is fundamentally different from what Moscow wants to impose.

Russia is clearly manipulating the situation by demanding a referendum on the EAEU now, when Armenia is at least a decade away from joining the EU.

We need to understand the real reason for this urgency.

The Kremlin understands that if EU membership becomes a genuine possibility, no rational society could vote against it.

Therefore, to keep Armenia in the EAEU and have a chance of stopping its move towards the EU, a referendum must take place as soon as possible, while the prospect of EU membership remains unclear and uncertain.”

Moscow is trying to “beat” Europe by exploiting Armenian businesses’ dependence

“The EAEU mechanisms currently work in favour of Armenian businesses, creating influence and dependence.

At the same time, Armenia is steadily diversifying its economy, reducing that influence and dependence.

The question of whether to remain in the EAEU directly affects many companies with specific interests in Russia. By contrast, EU membership remains a more abstract issue for them for now.

Moscow does not expect to “beat” Europe in economic competition over the next few years or even decades and offer Armenia more attractive conditions. It therefore believes it still has an opportunity to influence the situation now. That is why it is in such a hurry.”

Opinion on Russia’s demand for a referendum in Armenia

World.title: Armenia-Azerbaijan exports could begin ‘soon’: Pledges, figures and remaining barriers
World.content:
Exports from Armenia to Azerbaijan

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told journalists that “exports from Armenia to Azerbaijan could begin in the near future”. He also said that bilateral trade was already on the agenda. According to Pashinyan, Azerbaijani specialists visited Armenia in September 2025 and January 2026 to discuss infrastructure issues, including power lines, railways and pipelines.

The statement comes against the backdrop of tangible but still highly asymmetrical trade relations between the two countries, which began to take shape following the signing of the declaration in Washington in August 2025.

Official data and figures

According to Azerbaijan’s State Customs Committee, Azerbaijan exported around $17.4m worth of goods to Armenia between January and July 2026. The shipments consisted mainly of petroleum products, particularly diesel and petrol. Over the same period, Azerbaijan’s indirect imports from Armenia amounted to just $960. This figure was recorded in March, with imports falling to zero in subsequent months.

Following the lifting of transit restrictions in October 2025 and the start of the first fuel deliveries in December, Azerbaijan has facilitated both direct exports to Armenia and the transit of goods from Russia and Kazakhstan, including grain, fertilisers and other products. Volumes remain small, but the direction of travel has changed: borders that had been closed for decades have effectively begun to open.

There has yet to be any official commercial export from Armenia. In January 2026, Armenian Economy Minister Gevorg Papoyan said the two sides had exchanged lists of potential goods for bilateral trade. These included aluminium foil and raw materials for its production, ferromolybdenum, textiles, flowers, greenhouse produce including tomatoes and peppers, raw materials for brandy production, and other goods.

The specific contents of the lists and the expected volumes of shipments have not yet been officially published. Further development of trade will depend on agreements between companies.

What could be traded, and why?

Azerbaijani experts note that, at the initial stage, developing trade in industrial goods and raw materials appears more realistic than focusing primarily on food products. Vugar Bayramov, an MP and member of the Milli Majlis Committee on Economic Policy, citing preliminary estimates, puts the potential annual trade turnover for 38 categories of goods at up to $300m. These include food and industrial products as well as raw materials. In his view, mutual supplies of goods other than fuel could begin between the two countries in the near future.

Economist Natig Jafarli says the process is developing gradually. According to him, Azerbaijan has an advantage in energy resources, while potential Armenian exports could include agricultural products, fish, fruit and iron ore. However, Azerbaijan is not yet importing goods from Armenia, while the necessary infrastructure, including bank transfers, insurance and contractual mechanisms, has yet to be fully established.

Akif Nasirli, chairman of the Centre for Liberal Economists, believes food products could also be viable export candidates, including fruit and vegetables such as apricots, peaches, cherries, tomatoes and peppers, as well as fish, mineral water and wine. In his view, restrictions on the Russian market are forcing Yerevan to seek alternative export markets.

Former Finance Minister Fikret Yusifov has previously argued that, if trade relations are restored, a trade deficit for Armenia would be inevitable, but that these economic ties should nevertheless be developed for the sake of peace.

There is also a widespread view among experts that food and beverages are psychologically more sensitive categories of goods. Construction materials, cable and electrical products, industrial raw materials, chemicals and light-industry goods, by contrast, may be perceived considerably more favourably.

Psychological barrier

This is one of the deepest and most sensitive aspects of the issue. Expert assessments published by Caliber note that memories of the 44-day war remain fresh. The appearance of products labelled Made in Armenia on shop shelves could initially provoke mixed reactions, ranging from curiosity to social media campaigns. Trust in food and beverages, including wine and brandy, is particularly important, as some consumers may have irrational concerns about their safety. With industrial goods and construction materials, by contrast, the country of origin is less visible to consumers and purchasing decisions tend to be more pragmatic.

During a transitional period, neutral packaging in English or Russian, or rebranding, could potentially be used. The appearance of Azerbaijani fuel on the Armenian market has already created a precedent for a kind of “economic truce”. A similarly pragmatic approach could work in the opposite direction, although this will not happen automatically.

In both societies, support for peace does not yet necessarily translate into an equally positive attitude towards goods from the neighbouring country. Traders from border areas who wished to remain anonymous, as well as entrepreneurs with experience of informal “re-exports” through Georgia using channels that have existed since the 1990s, say that price and quality could eventually become the decisive factors. However, this process could take years.

Practical obstacles and possible timeframes

Issues surrounding certification, phytosanitary controls, customs procedures, bank transfers and insurance have yet to be fully resolved.

Logistics currently operate mainly through Georgia. Direct rail links and the TRIPP corridor are still at the infrastructure development stage. Competition also remains high, with suppliers from Turkey, Russia and Iran already present in the market alongside domestic producers. The competitiveness of Armenian goods will therefore depend on their price, quality and logistics costs.

Under an optimistic scenario, small-scale shipments of industrial goods and raw materials could begin within several months to a year. A more realistic scenario would see trade gradually expand over one to three years, while under a pessimistic scenario, political fluctuations and public reaction could delay the process considerably.

What to watch next

Key indicators could include the first genuine commercial shipments from Armenia appearing in customs statistics, the introduction of banking mechanisms for cross-border payments, official approval of a list of potential goods for trade, and changes in the procurement policies of retailers such as Bravo, Araz and others.

Independent polling and sociological research in both countries will also be needed to assess public attitudes towards goods labelled “Made in …”. Without such data, statements about future trade will remain largely expressions of intent.

World.title: ‘From crisis management to stability’: Pashinyan unveils new government programme
World.content:
Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

The Armenian government has approved its programme for 2026-2031. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said it marked a shift from crisis management to stability. Looking back on his eight years as prime minister, he said the coronavirus pandemic, followed by the war and the post-war situation, had forced the government to operate in crisis-management mode. Now that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established peace, the government can “return to the unfinished part of the agenda of the 2018 Velvet Revolution”.

The new programme focuses on stability, he said. Pashinyan stressed that it rests entirely on the concept of “Real Armenia” and the principles underpinning the establishment of the Fourth Republic.

In 2025, the ruling Civil Contract party announced a new strategic goal: establishing the Fourth Republic of Armenia. The party congress unanimously adopted a declaration to this effect. According to the document, the Fourth Republic “will be based on the concept of preserving the internationally recognised sovereign territory of the Republic of Armenia, covering 29,743 sq km, in accordance with the 1991 Alma-Ata Declaration”. The declaration says the party reached this decision after analysing the history of the Third Republic. The Third Republic refers to the present-day Republic of Armenia, which declared independence following a nationwide referendum in 1991. The First Republic refers to the republic proclaimed on 28 May 1918. Accordingly, Soviet Armenia is considered the Second Republic.

“Following the 7 June 2026 election, the ideology of ‘Real Armenia’ won. This means it has become the official ideology. Armenia is therefore entering the stage of its history that we call the Fourth Republic. We must continue and give new momentum to democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms,” the prime minister stressed.

Government plans for the next five years

According to the new programme, the Armenian government will pursue the following goals in 2026-2031:

strengthening and further institutionalising the peace established between Armenia and Azerbaijan;

maintaining and further developing a favourable security environment around Armenia, in particular by normalising and developing relations with countries in the region and deepening existing partnerships beyond it;

unblocking Armenia through the Crossroads of Peace project and the “Trump Route” (TRIPP) transit programme;

liberalising the visa regime with the EU for Armenian citizens;

deepening democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms.

With whom does Yerevan plan to deepen partnerships under its “balanced foreign policy”?

In 2026-2031, the Armenian government will pursue a “balanced and proportionate” foreign policy.

“It has proved effective in stabilising Armenia’s external environment. Regionalisation plays a key role in foreign policy, whose goal is to ensure conditions in which Armenia can not only live without external support, but do so comfortably,” the document says.

Based on this approach, the government places particular importance on further developing relations with Georgia, Iran, Turkey and Azerbaijan. The government has outlined the following steps for each neighbouring country:

Georgia

Yerevan will continue implementing the measures set out in the Declaration on Establishing a Strategic Partnership between Armenia and Georgia. This will create new mutually beneficial opportunities for political, trade, economic, energy and transport cooperation, as well as regional and joint infrastructure projects.

Iran

Armenia will continue energy cooperation with Iran, develop cross-border infrastructure and expand transport routes through Iran, including North-South and Persian Gulf-Black Sea corridors.

Turkey

The Armenian government will continue efforts to establish diplomatic relations with Turkey, open the Armenian-Turkish border and put at least two modern border crossing points into operation. It also plans to restore and expand transport, energy and digital infrastructure, as well as bilateral and multilateral trade.

Azerbaijan

The government plans to continue efforts to sign and ratify a peace agreement and carry out work on the delimitation and demarcation of the state border. Contacts between civil society and business communities in the two countries will continue, helping to establish bilateral trade.

The foreign policy priorities specifically include deepening strategic partnerships with the European Union, the US, France and China. With Russia, Armenia plans to “transform and deepen its partnership”.

Against the backdrop of tensions over the ban on Armenian food and other exports to Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), which Russia leads, the programme says:

“Work will continue to ensure the full and uninterrupted exercise of the EAEU’s fundamental freedoms — the free movement of labour, services, goods and capital — as well as to develop relations with member and observer states.”

Regarding relations with the European Union, the programme stresses that Armenia will continue working to meet standards in democracy and the rule of law, as well as in the economic, financial and other spheres.

Armenia intends to deepen its partnership with the United States further. Cooperation will continue based on the principles set out in the Strategic Partnership Charter and bilateral memorandums of understanding.

“The TRIPP project, the ‘Trump Route’, will be implemented, at least in terms of operating energy and railway infrastructure, while integrating Armenia into major regional infrastructure projects,” the programme says.

Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

World.title: Parrots Rocky and Kiki: Tbilisi Zoo’s brightest residents – video
World.content:
Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

Tbilisi Zoo is home to two species of macaws: scarlet macaws (Ara macao) named Rocky and Kiki, and blue-and-yellow macaws (Ara ararauna) named Chico and Paco. Their bright plumage catches visitors’ attention at first sight.

The macaws at Tbilisi Zoo are currently in the middle of their breeding season. Chico and Paco are expecting chicks. They usually incubate their eggs for 24–28 days. During this period, both parents actively protect and care for their future offspring.

Rocky and Kiki have become particularly cautious during this period. They often hide from people and rarely leave their enclosure. If you are planning to visit them at the zoo, keep in mind that they may be difficult to spot at the moment.

Macaws are known for their strong bonds. Pairs almost always stay together: they preen each other’s feathers, look for food together and protect each other when danger threatens.

With proper care, macaws can live for 50–60 years, and sometimes even longer — more than 70 years. Rocky’s exact age is unknown, but he is the oldest parrot at Tbilisi Zoo. Despite his advanced age, Rocky still has the same short-tempered and grumpy nature he has always had.

Once, when a keeper was a little late with a treat — a nut — Rocky immediately made his “protest” known by biting him on the finger. Because of their powerful beaks, macaw bites can be very painful and may cause serious injuries.

Macaws are incredibly intelligent birds. They have excellent memories, and some can even imitate human voices and words.

Although macaws are often kept as pets, caring for them is no easy task. They need plenty of space, daily attention, mental stimulation and constant variety in their surroundings.

Tbilisi Zoo‘s history spans nearly a century. It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status. The zoo was originally built on 70 hectares in the Vere River gorge. Get ready to hear many fascinating stories.

World.title: OTS highlights Kurultai elections as milestone in Kazakhstan’s representative governance
World.content:
ASTANA, Kazakhstan, August 24. The Kurultay elections offer an opportunity to strengthen public participation, build citizens’ trust, and advance the development of the country’s representative institutions, Deputy Secretary-General of the Organization of Turkic States, Nuru Guliyev, said, Trend's special correspondent reports.

Nuru Guliyev made the statement during a briefing in Astana.

He noted that the mission included officials from the OTS Secretariat, as well as representatives of the central election commissions and government agencies of member states: Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Türkiye, and Uzbekistan. The mission carried out its activities in accordance with the national legislation of Kazakhstan, as well as with universally recognized norms of international law governing the organization and conduct of elections and referendums.

“The mission welcomes the establishment of the new Kurultay as a unicameral legislative body and the holding of the first elections to it, which is an important milestone in the development of the institutional system of the Republic of Kazakhstan.”

“In this context, the mission welcomes the efforts of the electoral authorities and other stakeholders aimed at implementing the new electoral system within a relatively short timeframe following the constitutional reform. The mission views this first electoral process as an opportunity to strengthen public participation, citizen trust, and the development of the country’s representative institutions,” Guliyev said.

He noted that the mission welcomes the efforts of electoral authorities and other stakeholders aimed at implementing the new electoral system within a relatively short timeframe following the constitutional reform.

Furthermore, Guliyev added that the OTS mission views this first electoral process as an opportunity to strengthen public participation, citizen trust, and the development of the country’s representative institutions.

“In total, the mission visited 33 polling stations to observe the voting process. The mission found no evidence of interference by administrative or law enforcement agencies in the activities of the polling stations visited. It was also noted that the necessary administrative measures had been taken to ensure citizens’ freedom to express their will,” he stated.

World.title: President Ilham Aliyev sends a congratulatory letter to Volodymyr Zelensky
World.content:
Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 24. Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev has sent a congratulatory letter to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

This was reported by the press service of the President of Azerbaijan.

"Dear Mr. President,

On my own behalf and on behalf of the people of Azerbaijan, I sincerely congratulate you and, through you, the friendly people of Ukraine on the significant occasion of the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence and convey my best wishes.

The current level of Azerbaijan–Ukraine friendly relations, which have rich traditions, is a source of satisfaction. Our political dialogue, high-level reciprocal visits, and cooperation in the economic and humanitarian fields are important aspects of our strategic partnership. I would particularly like to note our effective cooperation in the energy sector, which has continued for many years.

I highly appreciate the results of your working visit to Azerbaijan in April this year and our meeting. Undoubtedly, our regular meetings and contacts, as well as our mutual support on issues concerning the territorial integrity and sovereignty of our countries, are among the main factors contributing to the strengthening of interstate relations.

The existence of an active dialogue at the highest level creates a favorable basis for deepening our cooperation in various fields, particularly in trade and the economy, humanitarian affairs, agriculture, investment, and other areas. We will continue to provide humanitarian support to the friendly people of Ukraine in the future as well.

I am confident that we will continue to make joint efforts to strengthen Azerbaijan–Ukraine friendly relations for the benefit of our peoples.

On this festive day, I wish you robust health and happiness, and peace, tranquility, and prosperity to the friendly people of Ukraine," the letter reads.

World.title: Visa calls for balancing fraud prevention with seamless customer experience — VP
World.content:
TASHKENT, Uzbekistan, August 24. Financial institutions need to strengthen fraud prevention while ensuring that security measures do not undermine the customer experience, Yevgen Lisnyak, Vice President and Head of Strategic Partnerships, Fintech, Acquiring & Merchants for the CISSEE region at Visa, said, Trend’s special correspondent reports from Tashkent.

He made the remark while speaking at the Silk Road Finance & Technology Forum.

According to Lisnyak, fraudsters are constantly adapting to technological developments and new security measures, making fraud prevention an ongoing process that requires both awareness and proactive action. “The turning point, and where we need to pay attention always, is to be informed and to be aware of what's going on with them, to be able to protect from them. This is first of all some kind of preemption. And the second is, of course, proaction,” Lisnyak said.

He noted that proactive protection requires financial institutions to maintain robust anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) systems. At the same time, he stressed the importance of avoiding excessive security barriers that could make digital financial services unnecessarily complicated for customers. “If we build too many walls, people will not go through it. And this is also this challenging task — to be secured from one way, but also keeping the customer experience smooth and seamless from the other side,” he said.

Lisnyak said Visa works with its partners to address both aspects, using technologies including artificial intelligence to identify and anticipate fraudulent activity.

He noted that information on fraud attempts detected in different markets can be used to help protect financial institutions in other countries. “We collect all the fraud attempts across the world and actually bring it here to Uzbekistan and say, ‘Hey guys, there is in Colombia such type of fraudsters who is trying to cheat you. Here is the rule that will protect you,’” he said.

According to Lisnyak, the global scale of payment networks allows information about emerging fraud patterns to be shared across markets, helping local financial institutions strengthen their defenses.

At the same time, he emphasized that not all fraud results from weaknesses in technological security, with social engineering and human behavior also playing a significant role. “Plenty of frauds happen not with broken security level, but because of social engineering, just because of people,” Lisnyak said.

In this regard, he highlighted the importance of financial literacy initiatives and cooperation with regulators and central banks.

He said Visa has been working with the Central Bank of Uzbekistan and other partners on financial literacy programs, noting that educating consumers can serve as an additional layer of protection against fraud. “We believe that we need to work on this layer too,” Lisnyak said.

World.title: Kazakhstan advances AI infrastructure plans with Presight AI
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 24. Kazakhstan and Presight AI are exploring expanded cooperation on artificial intelligence infrastructure, smart city solutions, digital transport systems and data processing, as the country accelerates its digital transformation.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Transport of Kazakhstan, following a meeting between Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov and Thomas Pramotedham, CEO of international technology company Presight AI.

The sides discussed opportunities to develop AI and digital infrastructure, Smart City projects, digital transportation systems, and data storage and processing infrastructure.

Presight AI, part of the international G42 group, specializes in applied artificial intelligence and big data analytics. With the company’s participation, a Smart City project has been implemented in Astana, while the national supercomputing infrastructure Alem.Cloud has also been established.

Particular attention was given to expanding digital solutions in the transportation sector and developing intelligent infrastructure at Astana International Airport. The sides also discussed using AI to improve urban management, public safety and the quality of services, as well as developing domestic technological expertise and human capital.

Bektenov said Kazakhstan is entering a new stage of digital transformation, noting that President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence.

“Kazakhstan is creating favorable conditions for attracting long-term and technology-intensive investment,” Bektenov said, according to the government.

Pramotedham, in turn, expressed Presight AI’s readiness to expand its presence in Kazakhstan and pursue new joint projects in applied AI, digital infrastructure and technology solutions for key sectors of the economy.

At the end of the meeting the sides identified priority areas for further cooperation.

World.title: Azerbaijan facilitates new Russian shipment to Armenia in transit
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 24. Another shipment has been delivered from Russia to Armenia in transit through Azerbaijan.

A seven-carriage shipment carrying 242 tons of propane was sent from Bilajari station toward Boyuk Kesik on Aug. 24.

To date, more than 50,000 tons of grain, nearly 9,000 tons of fertilizer, 1,172 tons of propane, 133 tons of aluminum, 1,114 tons of coal and 67 tons of timber have been shipped from Russia to Armenia in transit through Azerbaijan.

At the same time, up to 15,000 tons of diesel fuel and up to 5,000 tons of AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline have so far been exported from Azerbaijan to Armenia.

World.title: Azercell launches exclusive partnership with Steam
World.content:
For the first time in Azerbaijan’s telecom market, Azercell subscribers can top up their Steam balance directly from their mobile number, with no additional fees or VAT

Azercell has launched Steam Top-Up, becoming the first mobile operator in Azerbaijan to offer direct Steam top-ups from a mobile balance. The service allows subscribers to add funds to their Steam balance without any additional fees or 18% VAT.

Steam Top-Up allows subscribers to top up their balance without a bank card or any other payment method. Using the service is simple: subscribers open Steam Top-Up in the Azercell app, enter their Steam account name and select the amount they want to add. The payment is then charged directly to their mobile balance.

The new service makes it easier for subscribers to manage their Steam accounts, from adding funds to purchasing games and other digital content on the platform. With payments made directly from their mobile balance, the process is simpler and more accessible.

Steam is one of the world’s largest digital gaming platforms, offering millions of users access to thousands of games and other digital content. Popular titles on the platform include Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, PUBG: Battlegrounds, EA SPORTS FC 26, Elden Ring and Baldur’s Gate 3, among many others.

The launch of Steam Top-Up gives Azercell subscribers a more convenient way to access international digital services directly from their mobile account, while further expanding the range of digital services offered by Azercell.

Subscribers can access Steam Top-Up by updating the Azercell app. Further information is available on Azercell’s official website.

World.title: HUMO aims to expand from regional to international payment network — chairman
World.content:
TASHKENT, Uzbekistan, August 24. Uzbekistan’s HUMO payment system aims to expand its operations from the regional level to the international market by developing cooperation with payment systems in other countries, HUMO Chairman Aleksey Maslov said, Trend’s special correspondent reports from Tashkent.

He made the remark while speaking at the Silk Road Finance & Technology Forum.

According to Maslov, HUMO’s initial goal was not to create another local payment player, but to build a system capable of expanding beyond the domestic market. “From the very beginning, our goal was to create a player which can be at least regional from the beginning, but then we decided to move into international operation,” Maslov said.

He noted that HUMO operates its own local card network and also issues co-branded cards with international payment systems, including Visa. “The co-branded card can be used as a local [card] inside the country and can be used as Visa outside the country. It's a typical thing for a local payment system,” he said.

At the same time, HUMO is developing direct cooperation with other national payment systems in the region. “For example, we have cooperation with some other local payment systems, like Elcard in Kyrgyzstan. Elcard can be accepted in our country. Our cards can be accepted in Kyrgyzstan. We do a similar thing with Kazakhstan. We do similar things with some other countries,” Maslov said.

He added that HUMO will continue expanding its cooperation geographically, with the aim of strengthening its position as a regional, subregional and eventually international payment player.

World.title: Police charge man over attempted $1 million prison drone drug delivery
World.content:
A 47-year-old man has been charged over allegedly using a drone to deliver more than $1 million worth of drugs into a Townsville prison.

Corrective services officers brought down the drone in May when it was spotted over the Townsville Correctional Centre.

Officers found a package attached to the drone containing methylamphetamine and GBL, a large quantity of prescription drugs, syringes, a glass pipe, a mobile phone and a SIM card.

A 47-year-old man has been charged with five counts of supplying dangerous drugs into a correctional facility.

The drone was carrying contraband estimated to be worth $1 million. (Supplied: Queensland Corrective Services)

He has also been charged with trafficking dangerous drugs, dealing with a prohibited item in a corrective services facility, supplying a medication and drone-related offences.

The man will face the Townsville Magistrates Court on Tuesday.

Detective Acting Inspector Erica Gray of the Corrective Services Investigation Unit said the charges are a "disruption" to the supply of drugs into Queensland prisons.

"Preventing drugs from entering correctional facilities is critical to the safety of staff, prisoners and the broader community," she said.

A similar incident was reported at the prison in 2022 when officers found a drone that had crashed while carrying illicit drugs and tobacco.

A man faced charges in 2023 over the incident.

World.title: Activist seeks 'urgent' injunction to stop aerial brumby cull
World.content:
A last-minute emergency legal application has been made to stop aerial culling of brumbies at a national park on the New South Wales north coast.

The operation, led by the National Parks and Wildlife Service, was meant to begin today for four days at the Yuraygir National Park, which is about 100km north of Coffs Harbour.

Brumby protection activist Carmen Jackson's application to stop the week-long aerial pest control operations in the park was first heard at 1am today in the state's Land and Environment Court.

Carmen Jackson outside NSW parliament earlier this month. (Facebook: Australian Human Rights Heritage)

Justice Rachel Pepper heard the early morning motion, standing the matter until the court opened at 9am to allow the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water the opportunity to respond.

During the proceedings at 9am, plaintiff Carmen Jackson told the court she was "very concerned" the culling would cause "irreparable harm" to the brumby population in the park.

Justice Pepper said the court received a phone call last night to proceed with an "urgent" case to stop culling operations.

The National Parks and Wildlife Service advertised the culling operation within the Yuraygir National Park on August 3, closing the park from 6am today for a one-week period.

An alert on the National Parks and Wildlife Service website about aerial shooting operations in Yuraygir National Park. (Supplied: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service)

Ms Jackson told the court she had sent the court injunction application to the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) this morning at 7:15am.

Justice Pepper said the application was given at "very late notice".

"What has concerned Ms Jackson is she can't find the statutory instrument permitting the culling to proceed and is concerned there is no lawful authority for the cull to be taking place."

Granting leave for Ms Jackson to file a motion, Justice Pepper adjourned the court to reconvene this afternoon for a response from the DCCEEW.

The DCCEEW solicitor advised the court the aerial culling operation would be commencing tomorrow at 2pm to allow the motion to be heard tomorrow morning.

Brumbies like this wild horse known as "Matagi" by activists evoke strong emotions in discussions about feral animal control. (Supplied: Michelle J Photography)

Justice Pepper advised Ms Jackson to file documentation as soon as possible.

"Nothing is going to happen between now and 2pm tomorrow," she said.

"I can see no reason why I can't allow the respondent time to get their documentation in order."

World.title: Judge declares mistrial as sharp-eyed juror discovers evidence error
World.content:
A Queensland jury has been discharged and the fraud trial of a Cape York Peninsula traditional owner declared a mistrial over "irregularities in the evidence".

Ankumuthi traditional owner Larry Joe Woosup has pleaded not guilty to two aggravated counts of fraud, with the prosecution telling the court he allegedly misused mining royalties in 2014.

After six days of evidence, statements and summaries beginning in Cairns District Court last Monday, Judge Joshua Treviño KC today dismissed the jury a little over two hours after it had retired to deliberate.

This afternoon, the court heard a juror noticed redacted information relating to an exhibit in an evidence folder and raised it with the bailiff.

Judge Treviño then told the jury that, following an examination, another juror's working copy of the evidence was also irregular.

"This raised issues about substantial prejudice that might be caused if that irrelevant material was put before the jury. There was a risk of unfair prejudice to the defendant in that material," Judge Treviño told the court.

He said the irregular evidence might have been before the jury since the start of the trial.

"If I could be satisfied that that was the only error or difference … then I may have given more consideration to whether I give strongly worded directions," he said.

"It was the crown's responsibility to prepare those documents and ensure that the documents that you were provided were the same as those that were tendered.

"You have been deliberating on, potentially, documents and material that is not evidence. That's a significant irregularity that I cannot cure."

In another error, Judge Treviño said the jury's phones were not removed when they were sent out to deliberate at 1.43pm today, until the error was realised an hour later.

"They had not been collected from the jury as would be the normal practice," Judge Treviño told the court.

Judge Treviño said the events were most unfortunate and thanked the jurors for their service.

Crown prosecutor Christian Peters (right) has taken responsibility for "irregular" copies of evidence provided to jurors in his case against Larry Joe Woosup. (ABC Far North: Brendan Mounter)

During the trial, the court heard Mr Woosup and another community member arranged a deal with a mining company over the right to mine bauxite on traditional lands a year after a separate deal with the community reached a stalemate.

Mr Woosup then set up trust accounts with two different banks for the Ankumuthi community, for which he was sole trustee.

The jury was told it was an undisputed fact that Mr Woosup then used the overdraft capacity on one account to transfer and withdraw $110,000 and deposited a cheque for $95,000 from the mining company into the other account, which was then also withdrawn.

The requirement for both trusts was for all money to be used for the benefit of the Ankumuthi community, the court was told.

Mr Woosup's matter has now been adjourned and will return to the District Court for mention on September 28.

World.title: Redland City Council reveals plans for 62ha precinct including lagoon
World.content:
Redland City Council has released plans to build an outdoor lagoon that the acting mayor has said will be "better than Brisbane's" South Bank Beach.

Today, the council released the final plans and artist impressions of its Birkdale Community Precinct, a 62 hectare tourism and leisure zone about 23 kilometres from Brisbane.

The lagoon will be next to the controversial Whitewater Centre, which will be used for slaloming in the Brisbane 2032 Olympic Games.

An artist's impression of the Birkdale Community Precinct. ( ) The venue is expected to be open by 2030. ( ) The precinct will include restaurants and hotels. ( ) The whitewater centre would be used as a lazy river when not hosting athletes. ( )

The precinct would include a 2,000-square-metre lagoon, zip-line, hotels, restaurants, event venue, bushwalking track and a "dive-in" movie screen to watch from the pool.

Acting Mayor Julie Talty said construction would start mid-2027 and it would, hopefully, be open by 2030.

Cr Talty hit back at criticisms the Whitewater Centre would be a continual drain on the local economy after the Olympics had come and gone.

The Whitewater Centre would be maintained and run by council at ratepayers' expense.

However, Cr Talty said the council's financial modelling suggested the Whitewater Centre would pay for itself and also subsidise the cost of the lagoon precinct.

Opponents of the Whitewater Centre have said it is a waste of money. ( )

"We've got a small minority of naysayers in this city who want to shout 'white elephant' every time it's mentioned," Cr Talty said.

"I've been in council for 14 years and the one thing the community have been asking for the whole time is a lagoon like South Bank.

"It will be better than Brisbane's [lagoon].

"For a small council like us, we don't have the ability to provide that standalone, but the opportunity of the Olympics and the Whitewater Centre means we can do all of this."

Cr Talty said the Whitewater Centre would be used as a lazy river when it was not being used by athletes or emergency service training programs.

World.title: Perth modular home builder's sudden closure shocks customers
World.content:
Perth-based manufacturer Bella Modular, which built transportable granny flats and home office buildings to order, wrote to all its customers to notify them it would be unable complete their projects and had already vacated its premises.

"Due to unforeseen and significant financial difficulties, Bella Modular is unable to complete your project directly," it wrote on Wednesday last week.



"To ensure your build is protected and delivered through to Practical Completion and final handover, Bella Modular has entered into an arrangement for an independent, fully resourced third-party modular builder to step in and take over the management and construction of your home."

The letter does not name the new third-party builder nor make mention of what has happened to customers' deposits, but said they would be given the new company's details within 14 days.

Customer Peter Elliot, who ordered a granny flat intended for his parents in May 2025, told Nadia Mitsopoulos on 102.5 ABC Perth he was shocked to receive the letter.

"About three weeks ago, I'd had a phone call with the production manager on site," he said.

"He told me that our steel was on site and just ready to be assembled."

There had already been substantial delays in the build.

Mr Elliot paid a $90,000 deposit — 50 per cent of the cost of building — to guarantee a three-month completion time and had been hoping to have his parents living in his backyard by Christmas 2025.

"My parents are devastated," he said.

" This was a disability-ready home for them to move into as they progress further in their lives. "

Concern for deposits

Because the modular homes are built in a factory off-site and customers arrange transportation and cranes for the homes themselves, builders' indemnity insurance does not apply.

"The business model, which made sense to me at the time, was they construct a dwelling; we take ownership of the dwelling; we transport it and we are the owner-builder," Mr Elliot said.

He is uncertain how a new company is going to complete his modular building, or where his $90,000 deposit is now.

"I can't envisage another company taking on, effectively, the 50 per cent debt against the buildings that are either underway or promised to be underway," he said.

Bella Modular's premises in Hopeland, on Perth's southern fringe, has been vacated by the company. (ABC News: Kate Leaver)

Another customer left wondering is Steve Evans, who has paid almost $160,000 towards a modular home from Bella Modular that is yet to be built.

He initially paid a deposit of $28,000, then was contacted by the company four weeks ago to ask for a further $130,000, which he paid.

"It had a due date, which I found very odd at the time, of four days after I received the invoice, which is highly unusual because you need time to arrange funds to be able to transfer into accounts," Mr Evans said.

" I feel like a bit of a patsy … and I've got a horrible pit in my stomach that I've lost the money. "

A Credit Watch report shows the company has a debt to the Australian Taxation Office of $576,614.68. It is also facing three court actions for payments totalling just over $170,000.

Communication issues

On April 30 this year, Bella Modular wrote to clients apologising for the delays in their builds and the lack of communication with customers, promising improvements to its production schedule.

"Over the past 12 months, the level of customer service and communication you have received has been, quite frankly, atrocious," it wrote. "We are currently playing catch-up, and while we are implementing solutions that should have been brought to you months ago, we do have a strategic plan in place."

Caroline Marsh, another of the company's former customers, said she received her building more than two years after first placing her order in March 2024.

"In May this year, we received the delivery of the two modules that we ordered, and it was a very stressful time," she said.

"We had basically no communication with barely any of the staff through that two and a half years. I had to constantly go down there to check if any progress was happening.

"A week before we actually got delivery of ours, we were told it was definitely finished so I went down there and I looked at it and it wasn't finished.

"I still had a checklist of things that they hadn't done."

Bella Modular's owners have been contacted for comment.

World.title: Bail for teacher on child exploitation charges
World.content:
A teacher in Western Australia's Wheatbelt has been granted bail after being charged with possession and distribution of child exploitation material.

Darrel Calvin Scott, 28, appeared in the Northam Magistrates Court via video link from Hakea Prison today on two counts of distributing child exploitation material, and one count of possessing child exploitation material.

Police prosecutors told the court Mr Scott was working as a teacher at a high school in the Wheatbelt region, 100km north-east of Perth, at the time of the alleged offending and had since lost his job as a result of the charges.

There is nothing from his court appearance to suggest that any of the alleged offending related to students or his work at the school.

Northam Senior High School sent a letter to parents and carers last week outlining support services for students impacted by the "court appearance relating to a staff member".

"This is currently a WA Police Force matter, and the Department will assist should this be required," the letter read.

"Please be assured that student safety and wellbeing remain at the forefront of any decisions.

"Our school has support staff available for students as needed."

Darrel Calvin Scott was granted bail in the Northam Magistrates Court. (ABC Midwest & Wheatbelt: Eliza Bidstrup)

The court heard Mr Scott was arrested at an address in Northam earlier this month where a preliminary search of his mobile phone uncovered three videos alleged to contain child exploitation material.

It is alleged Mr Scott also shared the videos with two users on private messaging app Session.

Police prosecutors, who opposed his application for bail, told the court online conversations found on the phone included Mr Scott discussing fantasies of inappropriate conduct with students.

The court heard Mr Scott had admitted to saving the videos to his device and subsequently deleting them.

Magistrate Sarah Wisbey granted Mr Scott bail and said it was due to his lack of prior criminal record and strict conditions.

His bail conditions include a $5,000 personal undertaking and an additional $5,000 surety, as well as living with his parents, one of whom is a police officer, no internet access or unsupervised access to children.

Mr Scott did not enter pleas to the charges and will next appear in October.

World.title: 14yo Chinese exchange student to stand trial for murder
World.content:
A 14-year-old Chinese exchange student is set to stand trial in the NSW Supreme Court accused of murdering another Chinese student a year ago.

The accused, who can only be known as JY for legal reasons, is accused of murdering the 14-year-old near Newcastle in August 2025.

The teenager died from stab wounds.

At the time a spokesperson for the Council of Australian Student Exchange Organisations (CASEO) told the ABC in a statement the girls were not part of a student exchange program but were on a "study tour".

JY has pleaded not guilty to murder.

On Monday in the Broadmeadow Children's Court, Judge Stephan Herridge committed her to stand trial in the Supreme Court on a date to be fixed.

This would make the girl one of the youngest people to stand trial for murder in NSW.

Principle of doli incapax

In a court hearing in April, the prosecution asked the Children's Court for access to JY's psychiatric, education and custodial records.

It was in an attempt to rebut the presumption of doli incapax, which is a legal term presuming that children are incapable of committing a crime due to their lack of mental capacity.

The girl, now 14, objected to prosecutors accessing her records, arguing they were confidential and privileged.

The court rejected that defence.

After a lengthy hearing, access was granted in order to enable the prosecution to investigate the background and possible mental state of JY.

The matter is now listed for a call-over hearing in the Supreme Court in October.

World.title: Teen 'infatuated' with girl carried out shopping centre murder, court told
World.content:
A jury in Victoria's Supreme Court has watched footage of the moment a shopping centre fight between two boys turned deadly, resulting in one being stabbed to death.

The killer, who was 15 at the time, faced the jury today and pleaded guilty to the manslaughter of Oscar Hamilton, 16.

The boy remains on trial after pleading not guilty to murder on the basis that he did not intend to kill or seriously hurt Oscar.

The court heard Oscar was stabbed three times, including once in the heart. (Supplied)

Prosecutor Erin Ramsay said Oscar was hanging out with his girlfriend Briannan and two other children at the Woodgrove Shopping Centre in Melton West on September 24, 2024.

The accused approached the group in an outdoor dining area and grabbed Oscar by the collar, before assaulting him and stabbing him three times in quick succession.

"The third stab wound went right into Oscar's heart and killed him," Ms Ramsay said.

"Manslaughter is insufficient in the circumstances of this case."

Members of Oscar's family were in tears as footage of the attack was played to the court. Metres away, the killer, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, sat in the court dock.

Friends gathered at the shopping centre after the fatal stabbing. (ABC News)

Unproven sexual assault allegation was motive, prosecutor says

Ms Ramsay said the killer had been told by his ex-girlfriend, who he had only dated for a week, that Oscar had sexually assaulted her.

Ms Ramsay said Oscar's friends would testify that Oscar denied doing anything wrong.

The unproven sexual assault allegation was the motive for the murder, the prosecutor said.

The jury was told it was not their role to determine whether the allegation was true.

Ms Ramsay said the killer called his ex-girlfriend shortly after the stabbing and said, "I stabbed him, Oscar. I didn't mean to do it."

Ms Ramsay said the teenager was "infatuated" with the girl and later called his mum from youth detention, saying he hoped the girl would marry him.

When she failed to get in touch, he was recorded saying, "I came in here for nothing. She's a bitch."

"I only did it for her," he allegedly said.

"Even if that guy didn't touch her, I still would have done it."

Police at the scene of the fatal stabbing in 2024. (ABC News)

Defence barrister Richard Edney said the key issue for the jury was whether the boy intended to kill Oscar.

"He was 15 years of age at the time of this incident. That will be a matter you can consider," he said.

"It's desperately sad and tragic. A 16-year-old has passed. A 15-year-old boy at the time has been charged with murder.

"It's really important in a case like this, where you are judges of the facts, not to let emotion or sympathy guide your decision-making."

Witnesses in the trial will include Oscar's friends at the scene and teenagers, along with police and medical experts.

The trial continues.

World.content:

Loading Emergency services attempted to provide first aid, but she died at the scene. World.title: Reynolds admits defeat in bid for Suncorp farewell as curtain falls on NRL career
World.content:
Updated SportNRLNRL 2026 Reynolds admits defeat in bid for Suncorp farewell as curtain falls on NRL career Christian Nicolussi Updated August 24, 2026 — 6:21pm ,first published August 23, 2026 — 4:30pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Brisbane halfback Adam Reynolds has played his last game in the NRL after the two-time premiership winner reluctantly calling time on his career with two matches of the season remaining. Reynolds completed training on Monday and was targeting a Suncorp Stadium swansong on Thursday night against the Melbourne Storm. Adam Reynolds goes down injured against Parramatta in March. Injuries have plagued his final season in the NRL. Getty Images But coach Michael Maguire and the club’s medical team were worried about Reynolds breaking down and were not prepared to entertain images of him being helped from the field on his final home appearance. The 36-year-old who played 323 games – including grand final wins in 2014 with Souths and last year with the Broncos – phoned up to 50 family and friends to tell them not to fly to Brisbane for his farewell.



“I got through training, I felt pretty good, but after talking with ‘Madge’ and the medical staff, they weren’t keen to see me go out there and finish with another potential injury, then go out like that,” Reynolds said. “They’ve worked with me behind the scenes for years, they know me better than myself. They didn’t want me being injured to be last image fans remembered me by. Adam Reynolds says he doesn’t regret playing on in 2026 and no retiring after Brisbane’s premiership win in 2025. Getty Images “I knew it was coming to an end, be it this week or next week. Once the decision was made, I thought I’d get it out there, get on with life, and keep the focus on the team because they’ve still got to go out there and perform. There are other players preparing for their last game at the club, so it’s important to celebrate them as much as myself. I just hope we get the win.” Reynolds said he did not want any fuss or presentations. “If I had my way, I don’t want any parades, and I’d prefer to go out the back door quietly,” he said.



Reynolds said Mad Monday celebrations “would now become a mad month”, before he returns next season in a coaching role, where he will work with the club’s halves and pathways. Reynolds told this masthead on Sunday he had no regrets about playing on this year, despite injury and a concussion limiting him to just 14 games. Adam Reynolds celebrates a try against the Dolphins in March. Getty Images Reynolds has been struggling with nerve pain in his left calf for most of the season, then suffered a slight strain in his right calf at training a couple of weeks ago. “The year hasn’t worked out like I had hoped for myself and the club – but there are no regrets about playing on,” he said.



“Hindsight is a wonderful thing. I’d love to go around again, to be honest, but it won’t happen with where I’m at in my career. It’s easy to say I should have finished up at the end of last year, but there was that opportunity go back to back and do something special. That doesn’t come around too often in your NRL career. Related Article NRL 2026 Record $3.3m offer not enough to end star back-rower’s PNG interest “If there is one thing we’ve learned this year, it’s knowing what is required to be at the top level week in week out, and the processes you need to get right in the pre-season and the early parts of the year.” Reynolds backed Michael Maguire to remain the long-term coach at Red Hill. “There’s always noise around ‘Madge’ – [but] he sticks to his guns, he’s got the results, and he’s a winner,” Reynolds said.



“We’ve had injuries and suspensions and inconsistent games – none of that is down to the preparation and input Madge has over the playing group. We just haven’t lived up to our potential.” Sports news, results and expert commentary.

Mark McVeigh will leave his role as an assistant coach at the Swans for the Bombers’ top job. AFL Photos “We’re not looking backwards, we’re building the next great era of this football club. Our job is high standards, real connection, and total clarity on how we want to play and what it means to pull on the red and black. What excites me is what this group can become together.
