World.title: Man stabbed on street in Auckland suburb of Blockhouse Bay dies in hospital
World.content:
A man who was stabbed on a suburban street in Auckland on Saturday afternoon has died in hospital.

A homicide investigation has been launched after the incident in Blockhouse Bay at the weekend.

Acting Detective Inspector Craig Bolton, of Auckland City CIB, said there was a "violent confrontation" about 3.40pm on Saturday on Holbrook Street, near the intersection of Shoreham Street.

"The male victim has sustained a stab wound during this confrontation, before he has got into a vehicle with his associates and driven away to a nearby bus stop on Blockhouse Bay Road."

An ambulance was called and the man was taken to Auckland City Hospital in a critical condition, while police were notified.

Bolton said the victim underwent emergency surgery and was in intensive care, but died on Sunday night.

Police are seeking any witnesses to the initial confrontation on Holbrook Street, or near the bus stop on Blockhouse Bay Road.

Scene examinations took place in two locations on Saturday, including where the victim was found by ambulance staff and the scene where the initial altercation took place.

"I'm asking anyone who was in the area at the time and has information, to come forward.

"If you have dashcam footage, CCTV footage or saw anything - we need to hear from you," Bolton said.

He said police had contacted the man's family.

"Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time, and we will continue to update them on progress in our enquiries."

But Bolton also said police had been granted interim non-public orders around the victim's name from the Coroner's Office.

World.title: Too early to tell if large Wānaka blaze suspicious, fire investigators say
World.content:
Fire investigators are still working to establish whether Saturday night's large vegetation fire in Wānaka was suspicious and want to hear from people in the area.

The fire blazed through trees and scrub about 7.30pm on Saturday in Albert Town near Lagoon Ave, forcing 22 homes to be evacuated.

Eight fire crews battled for two-and-a-half hours in windy conditions to bring it under control, before rain began to fall at 10pm.

Fire and Emergency New Zealand said it was too soon to say if the circumstances were suspicious and fire investigators were working to confirm where and how the fire had started.

Burnt vegetation overlooks nearby houses at Albert Town. RNZ/Katie Todd

A spokesperson called for help from the public, asking anyone who had been in the area shortly before 7.30pm that night and seen anything that could be relevant, to get in touch.

This could be done by emailing the fire investigation team at OtagoDistrictCRM@fireandemergency.nz the spokesperson said.

Photographs and videos from the early stages of the fire, especially anything taken around the lagoon end of the reserve south of Lagoon Ave between 7.15pm and 7.45pm would be useful, they said.

Any information received would be treated in confidence.

After witnessing the tall, wind-fanned flames tearing through the patch of kānuka, local resident Estelle earlier told RNZ there was no doubt the community was lucky.

"Just the astounding thing was the speed with which it moved...

World.title: Mining company Bathurst Resources lodges fast-track application to extend West Coast coal mining
World.content:
The mining company Bathurst Resources has lodged its fast track application for approval to expand its coal mining operations on the West Coast.

It wanted to extend its Stockton mine near Westport and extract 20-million tonnes of coal from the Denniston and Stockton Plateaux over the next 25 years.

Stockton was the largest opencast mine in the country and produced steel making coal for export.

Bathurst's coal mining licences for the area expired at the end of March 2027.

In its application it said there was no guarantee new consents would be granted under the usual process and even if they were permission might not be given in time to avoid all operations coming to a stop in March.

The company employed 390 people in the Buller area.

It said consenting coal mines was now highly contentious, attracting significant opposition and leading to many rounds of court cases.

Forest and Bird was opposed to expanding mining across the Denniston Plateau arguing much of the area was vital conservation land which was home to great spotted kiwi, giant snails and unique lizards.

In 2025, dozens of protesters camped on the Plateau and attempted to shut down part of the mining operations.

World.title: Free-range hens likely to go in and out of lockdown as bird flu cases continue to emerge
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands of hens in lockdown Checkpoint Download MP3 7m

While the threat of bird flu still hangs over the egg industry, the Egg producers Federation says it's likely free-range chickens will be going in and out of lockdown in coming months.

Hundreds of thousands of hens have been in lockdown as the third case of bird flu was confirmed in a wild bird in Aotearoa.

But chairperson of the Egg Producers Federation and Mainland Poultry chief executive, John McKay told Checkpoint they would let half a million of their hens back outside on Wednesday.

McKay said there was now good data out there for farmers to decide the risk level for their birds and whether to let their hens out of temporary lockdown.

Many egg suppliers that have the ability to do so have put their hens into lockdown, restricting their roaming as a precaution to protect them from bird flu, meaning free-ranging was not always possible.

The most recent data McKay had seen showed there was a low risk for chickens, he said, even with the third detection.

"It's in a petrel and it's likely we will continue to find those ocean going birds occasionally washed up on our shores.

He said Mainland Poultry had decided to prepare its farms on Tuesday for the hens to be let outside on Wednesday morning.

"This is an evolving situation so we will continue to look at it and judge the risk - the welfare of our birds is paramount and the risk is likely to change in the future. As the risk level changes it might be time to bring those birds back in again."

McKay warned it might be something Aotearoa had to get used to with free-range farming going forward.

"We are free-range farmers because we want our birds roaming outside and we value that highly and people who buy free-range eggs care deeply about welfare.

For consumers who were worried about whether their eggs were still free-range, McKay said stickers would be be put on Mainland Poultry cartons, next time the birds went into lockdown, alerting potential buyers to the fact the birds were temporarily kept inside.

He said the stickers would very clearly state the eggs had been laid by birds temporarily housed for their own welfare.

World.title: Fences along Wellington waterfront a highly charged matter council says, despite death of teacher Isaac Levings
World.content:
Wellington City Council's chief operating officer is adamant the decision to install balustrades along the waterfront is too highly charged to be made by officials - despite multiple drownings.

James Roberts made the comments during evidence at the coroner's inquest into the 2023 drowning of Christchurch teacher Isaac Levings.

Since 2013, eight people have drowned in the harbour.

The inquest into Leving's death, following a concert by the band The 1975, resumed on Monday.

Earlier this month, the inquest heard from former council city and parks manager Shane Binnie, who said recommendations from another inquest, into the death of Sandy Calkin two years earlier, were not acted on.

He said while proposals to improve lighting went ahead, protection along the waterfront edge in the form of balustrades, or benches and bollards, did not.

The Wellington waterfront pictured last year. (File photo) RNZ / Samuel Rillstone

Binnie said in his opinion, the council senior executive refused to accept the safety options being put forward.

Lighting upgrades were undertaken in 2024, but a proposal to erect a waterfront fence was ultimately shot down by council vote on 7 August 2025.

In Wellington District Court on Monday, Roberts hit back at Binnie's claims and rejected any assertion that waterfront safety was not a council priority.

He said he did not agree with Binnie's assessment that edge protection - balustrades - was an operational matter to acted on by officials.

Roberts said even in instances where officers and the executive had the authority to make decisions, "high-profile" or "politically sensitive matters" could be escalated to elected members.

"On this occasion, and in accordance with the relevant delegations, officers were required to put the decision to councillors and abide by the decision that they made. It was not a decision that could have been lawfully made by officers."

'Crass' proposition put to top official

The month after the 7 August vote, counsel assisting the coroner Josh Shaw said elected members requested an assessment of how lighting improvements had mitigated the waterfront risk.

Under questioning from Shaw, Roberts confirmed an analysis was to take place once the project had been completed and pushed back on the implication that, in the meantime, other work on waterfront protection stopped.

In response to further questions, Roberts said the council was yet to figure out how to undertake such an assessment.

"I'm sorry to be crass," Shaw said, "but it's important that I put this proposition to you."

He said one interpretation of the council's actions was: "Let's see if more people die, now that we've improved the lighting - or if that deals with the issue."

That was labelled "a deeply cynical interpretation" by Roberts who said a review of the lighting was "reasonable" given the substantial changes.

He said evaluating whether the lighting was enough would likely require third-party expertise.

Notion that advice was watered-down rejected

On the stand on Monday, Roberts also defended the advice put to councillors about waterfront balustrades ahead of the 7 August vote.

Binnie had previously told the court that he had been sidelined from the waterfront safety work after presenting options for physical barriers.

Shaw put to Roberts that the exclusion of staff perceived to be advocates for barriers, weakened the advice ultimately given to elected members.

"What I'm suggesting is that this focus on neutrality and balance, this removal of anyone who you think might be straying into the territory of advocating for a particular position, it runs the risk of watering down and removing the urgency, the imperative, the need to deal with something that's a 20-year-plus issue to make sure that more people don't die."

Roberts rejected the notion that the advice was watered-down.

"We have to be careful how we construct and provide advice and guidance to council and the processes we follow to get that," he said.

"We have on a number of occasions been subject to judicial review for decisions and the processes related to those decisions made by council."

Roberts said balustrades was the option recommended to councillors, which followed multiple discussions, briefings, workshops and evidence provided to elected members, such as previous coroners' reports into waterfront deaths.

"Ultimately, we got a decision in front of councillors as soon as we could, as thoroughly as we could, with the right information that would be robust and would hold up to a future interrogation.

"And I believe we did emphasise the balustrade option as the recommended one."

The temporary fencing which had now been removed. (File photo) RNZ / Samuel Rillstone

Roberts said he acknowledged issues surrounding protection on the waterfront edge were "serious, ongoing and had been the subject of considerable work, debate and difficult decision making".

He said the council had, and would continue, to invest "significant time, resources, and funding" into improving waterfront safety, noting $11.1 million in funding for potential edge protection works had been carried forward to the 26-27 financial year.

He said the work undertaken since the inquest into Calkin's death demonstrated a "genuine commitment" to learning from past incidents and responding to the coroner's recommendations.

Calkin's father Roger Calkin, who was sitting in the inquest on Monday, told RNZ he disagreed with Roberts' assertion and felt a Water Safety New Zealand Drowning Blackspots report was dismissed.

Roger Calkin said the report made it clear that there had been no deaths along Auckland's waterfront since balustrades were installed in the central business district in 2017, while there had been five deaths on Wellington's waterfront.

The report said the difference between the cities was observational but consistent with "edge protection acting as a mitigating factor".

World.title: Travellers who already booked Fiji holidays could pay more, travel groups warn
World.content:
The Fiji government's new five percent Tourism Services Tax (TST) has been criticised by international travel associations.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) and the Travel Agents' Association of New Zealand (TAANZ) say the tax will penalise visitors who have already booked their travels to Fiji.

ATIA and TAANZ have called on the Fijian government to withhold implementing the new tax, scheduled to take effect from 1 September.

ATIA chief executive Dean Long said the tax would mean a Fiji holiday could become more expensive for Aussie travellers.

The new tax will be in place for large-scale tourism operators and travel industry experts are warning the costs are likely to be passed on to customers.

"The design and rollout reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," Long said in a statement.

"Retrospective application is an absolute no-go. Once a customer has paid, that price is locked in. Sending a fresh bill after the fact is not tax collection, it is a broken promise dressed up as policy."

He said many travellers are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago.

"That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith," he said.

Fiji remains a popular travel destination for Aussies and New Zealanders, but a new tax could threaten that.

TAANZ chief executive Julie White said travel was routinely booked, contracted and paid for many months in advance and the sudden announcement puts all that into chaos.

"Our concern is simple: travellers who booked and agreed a price before 1 September should not be hit with an additional tax simply because they are travelling after that date," White said.

"There is a significant volume of existing Fiji bookings where the price has already been agreed, and in many cases the customer has paid in full. Those travellers have every reasonable expectation that their holiday is paid for.

"They should not suddenly be faced with an additional cost because a new tax has been introduced after they made their booking."

White said the timing is particularly concerning as it comes immediately before the busy September and October school holiday travel period.

"Families have planned and budgeted for these holidays months in advance. There are also group, wedding, corporate and other large bookings where contracts and pricing have already been finalised," White stated.

"Reopening those arrangements creates uncertainty for travellers. Travel agents, wholesalers and tour operators are stuck in the middle. They are being asked to explain and potentially administer a cost they did not create, could not have anticipated and have no control over.

"At the same time, basic practicalities remain unclear, including who is responsible for collecting the tax, how it applies to net rates and existing contracts, and where a supplier ends and an agent begins. These questions need clarity not only for existing bookings, but for new bookings from 1 September as well."

TAANZ said the issue is compounded by a lack of clarity around the practical implementation of the tax, including how it will be treated across different types of bookings and existing contractual arrangements

The new tax will apply to tourism operators, including hotels, tour operators and cruise businesses, with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (NZ$1.4m).

Fiji's Minister for Finance Esrom Immanuel said the Tourism Services Tax was introduced as part of the coalition government's broader efforts to support Fiji Airways. RNZI/Sally Round

Local concerns

The new tax has also raised concerns locally, with members of the business community also voicing their disappointment.

J Hunter Pearls boss Justin Hunter said the government's decision showed a lack of understanding.

"One really has to question the economic brain trust behind this," he said in a Facebook comment on the issue.

"It shows remarkably little understanding of how the international tourism wholesale mechanism actually works. Product is contracted, priced and sold months in advance. You cannot simply change the cost retrospectively and assume somebody in the supply chain will absorb it.

"Fiji doesn't have that sort of leverage. If Fiji becomes too expensive, unpredictable or difficult for wholesalers to sell, they won't argue with us forever. They'll simply remove Fiji from the menu."

Tony Whitton, the managing director at Rosie Holidays and Ahura Resorts Fiji, said they had been in discussions with government line ministries about repealing or delaying the tax to cover those bookings made later in the year.

"The tourism industry (hotels, tour operators, activity companies, marine) have been in discussion with our line Ministry and the tax office for over 6 weeks to either repeal or at least apply the new tax to only new bookings made after 01 September 2026, warning that retroactively applying a tax on an existing contract that is already in place is a breach and there will be push back," Whitton said.

"So here we are 10 days before implementation."

Businessman Grahame Southwick questioned the tax idea.

"One wonders if these economic " super brains " in Govt even realize that this 5% tax on GROSS turnover can easily represent 20-50% of the profit ??? Am I missing something here?

"What that can translate to is closing the doors for properties than are currently marginal. As for retro charging.. are they serious ??

"Words fail me."

The Fiji Hotel and Tourism Association (FHTA) said businesses remained unclear about how the new TST would work, with concerns that taxing turnover rather than profit could significantly increase the tax burden on tourism operators, particularly those with smaller profit margins.

FHTA chief executive Fantasha Lockington told fjivillage.com they continue to receive thousands of questions from businesses in Fiji and abroad about how the levy would apply to existing bookings, deposits and transactions through wholesalers and agents.

She said that a resort in the Yasawas had asked whether a booking paid in full in April for travel in October would be subject to the new levy, while a Sydney-based wholesaler wanted to know whether it needed to return to clients who paid deposits months ago and ask for an additional 5 percent.

"The concern is not simply about the additional cost, but how the tax is calculated," she told fijivillage.com.

Lockington explained that a business retaining 25 percent of its revenue as profit would see the 5 percent turnover tax take a significant share of its actual profit when combined with the existing 25 percent corporate income tax, while an operator retaining 15 percent of revenue as profit, the 5 percent turnover tax would consume a third of its profit, resulting in a total tax burden equivalent to 58 percent of its income.

Government stand

In a statement, Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel said the government was concerned by the continued delaying tactics being employed by the FHTA and a number of industry players in relation to the implementation of the tax.

He said government had engaged with the FHTA and key tourism industry stakeholders since June to discuss the introduction, application and implementation of the new tax.

According to the government, it had also provided the industry with additional time to prepare for the new measure, with the implementation date adjusted from 1 July, to 1 August, and subsequently to 1 September.

"These extensions were provided in good faith to allow the industry sufficient time to prepare its systems, communicate with customers and ensure compliance. Despite this, government is concerned that some industry players, with the support of the FHTA, continue to create negative publicity around the TST and its implementation," he said.

He said the industry should recognise that protecting Fiji Airways meant protecting the connectivity on which hotels, resorts, tour operators, restaurants, transport operators, cruise services and thousands of other tourism-related businesses depend.

He added, for many years, the tourism industry had benefited from significant tax holidays, duty concessions and other incentives designed to encourage investment and support the development of the sector.

"Many hotels and tourism service providers have received tax holidays ranging from 13 to 20 years, together with various duty concessions and other forms of government support.

"The industry also benefits from taxpayer-funded tourism marketing and other public investments that help promote Fiji as a destination and support visitor arrivals.

"Today, the entire tourism industry contributes only around 5 percent of the total corporate taxes collected by government. The other 95 percent is paid by non-tourism sectors.

"Government recognises the importance of tourism and the investment that the industry brings to Fiji. However, the industry must also recognise that it has a responsibility to contribute to the wider national effort when the country and its critical tourism infrastructure require support."

He also claimed that under the previous Government, the tourism sector was subject to a combined 16 percent turnover-based tax through the 10 percent ECAL and 6 percent STT, which remained in place for a number of years.

World.title: New rules for the Dunedin's alcohol licences don't go far enough - councillor
World.content:
A Dunedin councillor wants the public to get involved in changes to the city's alcohol laws, saying proposed changes do not go far enough.

Consultation begins this week on new rules for the city's alcohol licences, including capping the number of off-licences in high depravation areas - including the student quarter - and reducing alcohol trading and delivery hours.

City councillor Russell Lund told Checkpoint that Invercargill had a ban on supermarket sales of alcohol, and there were nearly half the level of alcohol-related emergency department admissions there than were seen in Dunedin.

"[In Dunedin] one in 25 visits is alcohol related harm. So if we want to be serious about it we've got to start having a good hard look at the idea that we should allow supermarkets to devote a huge amount of floor-space to selling alcohol," Lund said.

Lund said the council should not be "threatened" by supermarket opposition to restricting alcohol sales.

He said he also strongly opposed any scheme to allow alcohol purchases to be made under buy now-pay later schemes.

"No. 1000 percent no. It's not a necessity. It defies any sort of logic or common sense to me," Lund said.

Lund said capping the number of new off-licences in high depravation areas would be a useful tool to limit the extent of alcohol related harm about the city.

"If you want to control behaviours or try and get better results for society you have to put subtle barriers - you have to make it essentially a little bit harder and less convenient - and that's just one obvious things you can do," Lund said.

He appealed to the public to get involved and make submissions to the consultation process.

World.title: Final emergency services test underway as opening date for Auckland's City Rail Link draws near
World.content:
More than 75 actors have been helping Auckland's emergency services test their responses to a range of scenarios ahead of the city's underground train network opening next month.

The City Rail Link (CRL), would open in three weeks on Sunday, September 13.

The last emergency exercise was taking place this week, simulating a fire on a train near one of the main stations.

In total, 15 emergency exercises have tested police, paramedics and fire fighters' responses to a range of scenarios including train derailments, station fires and mass evacuations.

These have each involved more than 300 volunteer passengers and also, actors, to help bring the scenario to life.

CRL Karanga-a-Hape Station on open day. (File photo) RNZ / Lucy Xia

The volunteers reflected the diversity of Auckland's daily commuters including older people, those with health conditions, people with limited English, and those with hearing, visual or mobility needs.

Auckland Transport (AT) General Manager Rail Services, Mark Lambert, said the testing programme has provided confidence the CRL was ready to welcome Aucklanders when it opened.

"The City Rail Link is unlike anything else in New Zealand's rail network, so it has been vital for everyone involved to practise how we would respond in a range of different situations. The strong collaboration between emergency services and our rail partners has helped build confidence that Aucklanders will be well supported should an incident ever occur."

The tests were comprehensive and looked at frontline responses through to the supporting systems behind the scenes, including ventilation and smoke extraction, alarms, communications, CCTV, lighting and control room operations.

Hato Hone St John Area Operations Manager, Kim Moser, said these realistic exercises help ensure emergency services were well prepared to respond safely and effectively if they were needed once the CRL opens.

"For Hato Hone St John, this testing has been an important opportunity for our ambulance personnel to build familiarity with the CRL's new underground environment and practise coordinated responses alongside our emergency service and transport partners."

The exercise builds on an extensive emergency testing programme completed last month, which involved more than 1400 volunteer passengers.

KiwiRail leads and coordinates emergency response to incidents in the CRL tunnels via its Auckland Rail Operations Centre. Auckland One Rail responds to unplanned events on trains and in the CRL stations - with the assistance of emergency services as needed.

City Rail Link chief executive Patrick Brockie said it was a unique environment.

"The City Rail Link's underground environment, with tunnels more than 40 metres below ground in some parts, presents unique challenges around access, evacuation and communication, requiring specialist planning and coordination."

Fire and Emergency New Zealand region manager Ron Devlin said they were carrying out site visits and additional training in the weeks leading up to opening.

"People may have seen our fire trucks parked outside the stations at all hours of the day," he said.

World.title: 'I'm a has-been': Injury ends Broncos captain Adam Reynolds's career
World.content:
Brisbane Broncos captain Adam Reynolds will end his NRL career sidelined by injury after failing a fitness test ahead of Thursday's game against the Melbourne Storm.

The Broncos have two games left, but the Storm clash marks their final home game of the year.

Reynolds had hoped to overcome a calf injury to play on Thursday and bid farewell to the stadium he has called home since 2022.

"I trained today, obviously thought I'd be a chance to play one last home game and then hand it over to the rest of the boys to finish off the season," he told Triple M.

"But it's not to be. … I'm officially a has-been."

Initially struggling with nerve issues in his left calf, Reynolds then suffered a strain in his right calf.

Reynolds said he "felt pretty good" during the training session, but the call was made for him to not play.

"I had some conversations with Madge [coach Michael Maguire] and the medical staff and they were quite concerned with the limited training I've done in the past couple of weeks," he in a club statement.

Reynolds has endured a number of lower-body injuries over his career and has not played since suffering a concussion in round 22 against the Knights.

"You wanna play the game forever but that's not reality," the 36-year-old said.

"The reality is you get old and you get brittle and at the end of the day you can't keep competing forever. I knew this day was coming, I knew in the back of my mind that I had to say goodbye at some stage and unfortunately it's today."

Reynolds confirmed 2026 would be his last year in the league before the season started.

The diminutive halfback played 323 NRL games over 15 seasons and is the league's second-highest point-scorer with 2,598 points.

He leaves the game as a two-time premiership winner — in 2014 with South Sydney and 2025 with Brisbane — and a State of Origin player.

"I've had a great career," he said.

"I'm extremely fortunate I get to carry some great memories moving forward."

World.title: Zak Butters informs Port Adelaide he will depart club
World.content:
Port Adelaide's three-time best and fairest winner Zak Butters has requested to leave the club via free agency and return home to Victoria.

The 25-year-old dual All-Australian's future has dominated headlines all season with reports of offers of up to $18 million over eight years from Richmond, Geelong, Collingwood and the Western Bulldogs.

"I've made a decision to head home. It's obviously been one that I've wrestled with for a while now," he said.

"It's been a tough decision and one that I haven't taken lightly.

"Although I've loved my time in Adelaide … I'm probably at a stage in my life where I'd like to get back around some family and friends and enjoy some more time with them.

"There are so many special memories I'll take with me and hold with me forever … I'll be forever in debt to the football club for drafting a skinny club from Darley."

Butters said he would "always be a Port Adelaide person" and would "always value this club and what it's done for me".

"The supporters have been everything, they've always got around since day one of being drafted, even this year they've been awesome and showed nothing but love and support," he said.

"I feel like I've always tried to repay them in the right way and play football in the right way."

Zak Butters is a dual all-Australian. (Supplied: Port Adelaide Football Club)

In a club statement, the Power said they would now work to facilitate his request whilst securing the best outcome for the club.

"Port Adelaide has been informed by Zak Butters and his management that he intends to exercise his rights as a restricted free agent and explore a return home to Victoria," the statement said.

"Zak has been an outstanding servant to the football club since debuting in 2019.

"He is a three-time John Cahill Medallist and dual All-Australian and we thank him for everything he has given to Port Adelaide."

ABC Sport reported Zak Butters had informed some teammates in June of his decision to move to Victoria; a story that was denied by the club at the time.

Butters played 17 games this season before a syndesmosis injury in Round 18 prematurely ended his campaign, with coach Josh Carr admitting the star midfielder was likely departing after their 10-point win over Essendon on the weekend.

Port Adelaide has been adamant all season they would match any bid on Butters and force a trade to try maximise their draft capital.

Speaking to ABC Sport in May, chief executive Matthew Richardson said the club would focus on their best interests.

"There will be offers that we can match and we will match. It does give the club a fair bit of control in what happens," he said.

World.title: Ex-NBA player who says he identifies as woman ejected from WNBA game
World.content:
Former NBA centre Enes Kanter Freedom has been ejected from an Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after Sky guard Natasha Cloud yelled and pointed in his direction late in the third quarter.

Freedom was sitting along the baseline on Sunday night (Monday AEST). He had on a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female".

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then went to confront Kanter, who held his arms out and took one step on the court. Security and a handful of Sky players stepped in between the two before the dispute escalated.

Freedom was then escorted from the court area. He displayed his shirt as he walked toward the lobby. He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing Wintrust Arena.

Sky coach Tyler Marsh said the team had rallied around Cloud.

"Tash didn't wanna feel like she was a distraction and I told her she wasn't," he said.

"I told her that we all embrace her as someone that protects our team and protects people that need to be protected. Tash is always going to stand on that, and we stand for Tash."

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft this month, saying they identified as women.

The argument that's hijacking the WNBA Sophie Cunningham insists she wants to protect the sanctity of women's sport, but her comments have opened her league up to an unprecedented attack.

"I'm transgender. I'm a woman … I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purposes of … professional basketball," White previously said.

"I think I'd be unstoppable."

Freedom said he and his team had reviewed the WNBA's eligibility criteria and its approach to self-identification and inclusion, and argued that if declaring an identity were sufficient, then he met the requirements to compete.

The confrontation came in a game that Indiana star Sophie Cunningham was playing in. Cunningham previously voiced support for barring transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports in an extensive ESPN profile.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans," Cunningham said.

"And I'm like, 'I never once said that.' I think that I am here to extend love.

"But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

Protesters from both sides of the argument have gathered outside a number of WNBA games, with fans at the Sky-Fever game calling out Kanter as he entered the arena.

Sophie Cunningham (left) has been at the centre of the controversy, highlighted by Enes Kanter's (right) stunt. (Getty Images: Michael Reaves)

One was heard telling the former NBA centre to get his "bitch ass out of Chicago", while another said "I'm not touching him I'm just saying f*** you, bitch".

"Knowing that rallies are happening on both sides shows the platform that the W has and the stunts for attention are just continuing to try and ride the wave that we have,” New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart said.

"I want Liberty fans and even Indy fans that are going to come here tonight to be able to have this arena be a safe space."

There has never been a transgender woman player in the WNBA.

Commissioner Cathy Engelbert last week denounced people she said were trying to "sow divisiveness" over the issue.

Engelbert's comments in a pre-game gathering before a Fever-Wings game in Dallas were her first public remarks since the league called out what it said were bad faith efforts to use the debate to "demean or marginalise others".

"People are trying to use the league to sow divisiveness," Engelbert said.

"We're being the centre of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA, never have written about the WNBA or reported on the WNBA."

The league's collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA", but it does not include any more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

Engelbert sent a memo this month to team presidents and general managers saying the league would discuss the subject of transgender women in women's basketball.

"There's always going to be haters out there and we denounce it," Engelbert said last week.

"But that's what happens when you have made it as a legitimate sports media and entertainment product."

World.title: AFL boss says suspended Swans will not be invited to Brownlow ceremony
World.content:
AFL boss Andrew Dillon has spoken to the media about the Sydney Swans scandal, saying "the actions of a few don't define the actions of the entire industry".

Dillon was at the launch of the men's AFL finals series and the first-ever wildcard round but was mainly asked about the AFL's handling of the Sydney Swans scandal, as well as details on allegations of drug use by the players.

Players Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon have been stood down by the Sydney Swans for breaching the club's standards on drinking and staying out late after last Sunday's win over Essendon in Melbourne.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad are separately investigating a report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a player allegedly touching a woman without her consent.

A police investigation is still underway, but no charges have been laid or arrests made.

Dillon and the AFL released a statement on Tuesday evening, the day after the story emerged, but today marked the first time Dillon or any of the league's higher-ups had fronted the media on the matter.

Chief executive Dillon said it was fair to say the scandal had "overshadowed" the start of the finals, but that he hoped football could bring people together, as evidenced by the emotional scenes after the Swans' men's and women's double header at the SCG on Sunday.

Swans fans descend on SCG amid club scandal Sydney Swans fans react to an emotional week, where a scandal continues to engulf the club, as they prepare to watch a historic double header at the SCG.

"The actions of a few do not take away from the thousands of people involved in football at all different levels who do great things all the time," he said.

"But what we do know is that we can do things better and we will continue to do that and we will continue to learn to be better.

"I think the actions of a few don't define the actions of the entire industry."

Dillon said the five suspended players would not be invited to the Brownlow Medal ceremony, held on the Monday before the grand final, but remained eligible for the award.

Dillon said the league would not conduct its own enquiries into the incident until after the police investigation was finished.

On Saturday, police provided an update about the investigation being undertaken by detectives from the Sexual Crimes Squad.

"The exact circumstances of the matter are still being established, and a number of people have been spoken to," the statement read.

"As the investigation remains active and ongoing, we will not be commenting further, including providing information on the specific circumstances of the matter, movements of detectives and any statements or interviews taken."

In a statement, the Sydney Swans said the club "supports the action taken by Victoria Police in releasing today's statement regarding the investigation".

The club's statement also addressed comments relating to other men, beyond the five players identified by the club, being present in the hotel room at the centre of the allegations.

"The Sydney Swans categorically confirms that no member of staff is involved in the investigation. This includes being in the hotel room central to the police investigation," it read.

"The club reiterates that no player has been interviewed by police at this stage."

Live Moment Look back at how ABC readers and other Australians responded to this live moment. That's the end of the press conference 'It is a privilege to play AFL': Dillon Dillon is asked a follow up whether the five named players relating to the scandal have been held accountable. "There's been accountability for those players," he says. "It is a privilege to play AFL and with that comes responsibilities." AFL has reviewed illicit drugs policy Dillon is asked whether the alleged drug use that has created part of the story around the Swans scandal has prompted a rethink over the league's illicit drugs policy. "We've just undergone an extensive review of the illicit drugs policy," Dillon says. "That will be taking effect from this off season. "There's accountability for the players and there will continue to be." Show more

World.title: Runner smashes half-marathon record, heads straight to the football
World.content:
Yomif Kejelcha has smashed the half-marathon world record, running a staggering 56 minutes and 51 seconds at the Media Maratón Ciudad de Buenos Aires in Argentina on Sunday.

The Ethiopian shaved 29 seconds off the previous mark of 57:20, which had been set by Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo in Lisbon in March.

Kejelcha's time and that of the record he just beat are still subject to ratification by World Athletics.

The Media Maratón Ciudad de Buenos Aires is a World Athletics Label road race and took place under favourable conditions of 6 degrees Celsius and with a slight breeze.

As ever, the super shoe gets plenty of post-race love from Yomif Kejelcha. (Instagram: @maratondebuenosaires)

Tadese Worku (59:20) and Bereket Nega (1:00:20) of Ethiopia completed the podium.

"I'm over the moon," Kejelcha told World Athletics.

"I'm super happy and right now I don't feel any tiredness. The travel from Ethiopia was too long and I was tired the first days here, but later I felt better and today I was full of beans.

"I had planned to run conservatively over the early stages, but I felt good and decided to give it my all.

"This time is unbelievable. I can't describe it with words.

"I now hope to try the Argentinian meat, which has a very good reputation, and this afternoon I have been invited to watch the River Plate-Vélez football match. I'm very grateful."

At the historic Estadio Monumental, Kejelcha showed off his new record on a new River Plate shirt, although would have been disappointed as Vélez Sarsfield came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 in their Argentine Primera División clash.

Clearly Los Millonarios don't share Kejelcha's stamina.

Yomif Kejelcha showed off his record on a new River Plate kit at at the Estadio Monumental. (Instagram: @maratondebuenosaires)

Kejelcha's time allowed him to reclaim the record, which he previously held with a 57:30 in Valencia in October 2024.

The time is slower than that recorded by Kiplimo in Barcelona last year, when he ran what he described as "the perfect race" to stop the clock in 56:42.

But World Athletics did not ratify that time because race conditions did not comply with their regulations.

Kejelcha ran the race at an average pace of 2 minutes and 42 seconds per kilometre — which would give you a 5km parkrun time of 13 minutes and 28 seconds.

However, as was the case when he became the second man to run an official race marathon in less than two hours in London last year, he negative split the race, running the second half faster than the first.

Super shoes won't be banned despite 'technological doping' claims Lord Sebastian Coe says World Athletics has a duty to "enable" super shoe development despite concerns.

He set out behind two pacemakers, going through the first 5km at 13:45, while the second 5km was run in 13:34.

His subsequent 5km split was a remarkable 13:22, with the Ethiopian holding that pace through the next 5km, running it in 13:23.

Last April at the London Marathon, the 29-year-old two-time Olympian ran 1:59:41, finishing second behind Kenya's Sabastian Sawe, who set the world record with a 1:59:30.

In the women's race, Ethiopia's Fotyen Tesfay stormed to victory in 1:03:57, comfortably beating her two Kenyan rivals Nelvin Jepkemboi (1:05:06) and Catherine Amanang'ole (1:05:11).

World.title: 'Disappointed' Hird congratulates McVeigh ahead of Bombers coach call
World.content:
Mark McVeigh appears set to be unveiled as Essendon's next senior coach, with fellow applicant James Hird congratulating his former teammate on the impending appointment.

Bombers legend Hird had been vocal in expressing his desire to return for another stint as coach, after Brad Scott was sacked in May.

Fremantle assistant Jaymie Graham and Adelaide assistant Murray Davis were also in the mix.

But McVeigh, an assistant to Dean Cox at Sydney, is reportedly on the verge of being appointed, with an announcement expected as soon as tomorrow.

Mark McVeigh is in the box seat to be offered the Bombers job. (Getty Images: Jason McCawley)

Interim coach Dean Solomon hands over the reins after the Bombers (2-21) completed the worst season in club history with a 10-point defeat to Port Adelaide on Sunday.

"Firstly, congratulations to Mark. He's a great friend of mine and I'm very proud of him that he's going to be named the coach, so good on him," Hird said on Nine yesterday night.

"From a personal point of view, it's very disappointing. I'm disappointed. I put my heart and soul into the effort, but obviously fell short and that's the way it goes."

Hird indicated he was yet to hear an official decision from Essendon, but said "maybe that's coming".

The 53-year-old ruled out returning to the Bombers in a different role, but said he still had the passion to coach.

James Hird, Dean Solomon and Mark McVeigh together in 2022 when they were all at the Giants. (Getty Images: Daniel Pockett)

Hird is director of coaching with VFL club Port Melbourne.

"We have a finals series to play," Hird said.

"We'll see what plays out at the end of the year with some other clubs who have contacted me and we'll see what happens."

McVeigh is reportedly set to present to the Essendon board again today, with an announcement imminent.

The 45-year-old played 232 games for Essendon and was one of the 34 players suspended over the club's devastating drugs saga, when Hird was coach.

McVeigh currently serves as Sydney's defensive coach, but could leave the club immediately to play a role in the Bombers' end-of-season exit meetings and list management decisions.

The second-placed Swans are preparing for a finals campaign while bracing for more fallout from the scandal that has rocked the club.

"That's one thing this football club's done well for a long period of time … be ready for the unexpected or if something does arise," Sydney coach Cox said last week about the potential of losing McVeigh to the Bombers.

"We've had those meetings [and] discussions. We're really clear on what will happen if he was or wasn't to get the [Essendon] position."

Two-time Essendon premiership champion and former captain Hird first took over as Bombers coach in 2010.

He was suspended for the 2014 season amid the fallout from the drugs saga, returned as coach in 2015 and resigned in August that year.

Hird had garnered plenty of support from Bombers fans in his latest bid to return as coach, after he narrowly missed out when Scott was appointed in 2022.

World.title: Former Roosters premiership star unveiled as PNG Chiefs' '007' signing
World.content:
Joey Manu has been unveiled as the much-hyped PNG Chief 007, with the two-time premiership winner to return to the NRL in 2028.

The Chiefs officially confirmed today the former Sydney Roosters utility signed a two-year deal with the club, which now boasts a backline that will be the envy of the NRL.

PNG had long hyped their seventh signing, with speculation Penrith superstar Nathan Cleary was bound for the club as their inaugural halfback.

But with a staircase at their home base showing each of their signings and "007" listed as "reserved", that honour will now go to code-hopper Manu ahead of the 2028 season.

Loading Instagram content

"We're thrilled to add Joey to our squad moving forward," Chiefs general manager Michael Chammas said.

"He is a world-class footballer with versatility across several positions and can change a game in a single moment with the skills he possesses.

"His experience and demonstrated success at the highest level will be a great benefit to our team and we can't wait to see him have a significant impact in the Chiefs jersey."

Manu joins a list that already includes Jarome Luai, Alex Johnston, Connor Watson, Zac Lomax, Brian To'o and Englishman Matty Lees.

But the move appears likely to have ended the 30-year-old's boyhood dream of representing the All Blacks.

To'o is still just the beginning for PNG Brian To'o is the fourth player to sign for Papua New Guinea who has played State of Origin in the past two years. It's a sign of things to come, with the NRL's richest club yet to truly enter free agency.

Manu left the NRL for an overseas rugby union career after the 2024 season, starting in Japan before a move to French team Racing 92 last year.

But his French rugby deal runs to the end of 2027, and New Zealand Rugby only selects players for the All Blacks if they play domestically.

Manu will be 33 by the time his Chiefs deal finishes.

Manu became one of the NRL's most prized utility players across 181 games, including the 2018 and 2019 premiership wins, with the Roosters.

He was named Dally M centre of the year in 2022 and won the Golden Boot award as the sport's best international player later that year.

The athletic New Zealand representative is equally adept in the centres and at fullback, and can also capably slot into the halves in a pinch.

On leaving the NRL after the Roosters' 2024 finals campaign, Manu offered no guarantees of ever returning to the 13-man code.

But any possible comeback had widely been expected to come with the Roosters, who scouted him as a teenager.

Instead, Manu becomes the latest jewel in the crown of the NRL's forthcoming 19th team, which can offer lucrative tax-free salaries to its signings.

PNG will be able to officially hit the market on November 1, with Cleary headlining a list of players who could still become free agents at that time.

The club has also been linked to Gold Coast utility AJ Brimson and Canberra second-rower Hudson Young, both of whom are State of Origin players, in recent weeks.

Isaah Yeo, Latrell Mitchell and Bradman Best are among other household names without deals beyond the 2027 season.

World.title: Aussie athletes continue top form with trio of medals at Diamond League
World.content:
Commonwealth Games champions Eleanor Patterson and Rose Davies have kicked on from their Glasgow triumphs, along with double silver medallist Jessica Hull, as Australia's athletes have continued to shine on the Diamond League circuit in Poland.

All three made the podium at the Diamond League Silesia meet in Chorzów overnight, with high jump champion Patterson soaring to third place, Glasgow 5,000/10,000 metre double winner Davies grabbing bronze in the 5,000m and Hull running her fastest race of the year to finish 1,500m runner-up.

But there was disappointment for Glasgow sprint hero Lachlan Kennedy, who after his Australian-record run for silver at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium, failed to make the 100m final in Chorzów.

Pride of place went to Olympic silver medallist Hull, who tried out new tactics, sitting back in the field in the Silesian Stadium and kicking for home at the top of the straight, only to be reeled in by Ethiopia's Tsige Duguma. She needed a 2026 world-leading time of three minutes and 55.06 seconds to pip Hull's 3:55.20.

"I got caught in the last few metres but it was a big step forwards in confidence today," said Hull, who is eyeing the inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest next month.

"That's the fastest I've run all year and we have some good races to come over the next few weeks."

Davies earned her second career Diamond League podium as she pursued Italian favourite Nadia Battocletti, fresh from her own 5,000/10,000 double at the European Championships.

Davies eventually finished third in 14:55.39, pipped by Ethiopia's Freweyni Hailu and Battocletti, who won in 14:54.09.

"Every race is a step forward and to come top three at a Diamond League shows I'm in good form," Davies said.

"I really look up to Battocletti, she's a great athlete and I would love to be like her."

Australia's Eleanor Patterson earned bronze during the women's high jump final. (Getty Images: Maja Hitij)

Patterson again defeated teammate, world champion Nicola Olyslagers, just as she had done in Glasgow when they took gold and silver.

It was a strong effort considering Patterson was battling illness, but she had to settle for third behind Ukrainian rivals, Olympic champion Yaroslava Mahuchikh and Iryna Gerashchenko.

Kennedy took his first strides back on the international circuit after his historic 9.85sec silver medal-winning run in Glasgow, but his 10.08sec run in the heats in Chorzów was not enough to earn him a place in the final, which was later won by Jamaica's world champion, Oblique Seville, in a searing 9.83sec.

"I didn't come out as well as I would've liked but I'm just trying to shake the rust off a bit. I'll get back into some training and better form — I'm happy," Kennedy said.

Triple Commonwealth pole vault champion Kurtis Marschall cleared 5.90m but it only earned him fifth place while his mate Armand Duplantis earned yet another effortless triumph with a 6.20m winner.

Queensland's two-time Diamond League champion Matthew Denny finished eighth in the discus (66.38m), as Lithuania's world record holder Mykolas Alekna won with a competition record 72.58m.

The international highlight was world champion Melissa Jefferson-Wooden handing Olympic champion Julien Alfred her first loss of the season to win the women's 100m, 10.78sec to 10.83.

Tech.title: GTA VI: all the news on Rockstar’s next entry in the Grand Theft Auto series
Tech.content:
It’s been over a decade and two console generations since GTA V came out, and its sequel is still a work in progress. GTA VI has faced multiple delays, with developer Rockstar Games bumping back its predicted release date twice, first to May 26th, 2026, then again to November 19th, 2026, a full year after its originally planned release window of fall 2025, and facing accusations of union busting after firing more than 30 employees.

Early official glimpses offered a look at the game’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, as the game will follow the pair around Vice City as they attempt to navigate a criminal conspiracy after a job goes south. After leaks of early builds a few years ago, a new “CyberLeek” series of posts have popped up, showing sequences of the game just days ahead of Rockstar’s planned Netflix-exclusive (for six hours) event on August 27th.

Tech.title: We’re All Going to the World’s Fair is an intimate coming-of-age horror film
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Jane Schoenbrun’s latest film, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, is making a splash in theaters right now. So it seems like the perfect time to revisit their first film, We’re All Going to the World’s Fair. I fell in love with this film when I first saw it at Sundance in 2021.

We are immediately introduced to our protagonist, Casey, as she engages in the World’s Fair Challenge, a sort of ARG creepypasta meets ice bucket challenge. There’s a creepy mantra, some bloodletting, and a mysterious video — basically a speedrun of horror movie tropes. But having them all delivered by this young girl alone in her room who just stares directly into her webcam the whole time is unsettling. And I actually physically recoiled when she jabbed herself repeatedly with a pin to draw blood.

The idea is that people perform the ritual and then they’re supposed to change in some sort of nebulous way. It’s set up as some sort of “game” where people are supposed to report their symptoms, as they turn into plastic or their guts and become Tetris pieces.

Ultimately, World’s Fair is a coming-of-age story about a lonely young girl. She’s never shown talking to kids her own age. Her father is never seen, only heard, and does nothing but yell. She desperately attempts to connect with others by uploading videos documenting the changes she experiences after performing the challenge.

Importantly, unlike many other coming-of-age films, World’s Fair isn’t about Casey’s sexual awakening and avoids sexualizing her entirely. Instead, it’s about her search for belonging in an extremely online world.

Basically the only other character to get any screen time is JLB, a lonely middle-aged man who claims Casey is in danger. The relationship between JLB and Casey adds another layer of unease to the film, which already blends horror elements with uncomfortably intimate glimpses into the life of a young girl. The whole thing has a voyeuristic quality. It’s never explicitly stated, but it certainly seems like JLB is attempting to groom the vulnerable Casey.

The movie stews in its uncomfortable ambiguity. And that’s part of what makes it great. It may not reach the surreal or campy heights of I Saw the TV Glow or Camp Miasma, but it’s a rare indie cinema original that uses body horror tropes in new and interesting ways.

We’re All Going to the World’s Fair is available to stream on Criterion Channel, Kanopy, and Hoopla.

Tech.title: Grand Theft Auto VI exists in its own universe
Tech.content:
This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on GTA VI and the state of the video game industry, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.

How it started

Four years ago, fans got a long-awaited look at Grand Theft Auto VI with a huge cache of videos that showed off Rockstar’s latest open-world epic. There were 90 videos in total, providing a glimpse at the next-generation take on Vice City, introducing the game’s new dual protagonists, and generally showing off the crime-fueled mayhem the series is known for. The twist? This wasn’t some official reveal. The videos were part of a massive leak in September 2022 that ultimately ended with a life sentence in a secure hospital for the hacker, and they dropped months before Rockstar properly unveiled GTA VI to the world with its debut trailer.

For many video game studios, a leak of that magnitude would be devastating. But not Rockstar: Following the unprecedented success of GTA V, which has sold more than 230 million copies across PC and three generations of consoles, it seems like there is little that can impact the studio in the lead-up to the sequel’s much-hyped launch. GTA VI’s first trailer was leaked less than a day before it was set to premiere in December 2023, and yet the official video went on to garner nearly 290 million views on YouTube.

How it’s going

The lead-up to the Netflix premiere hasn’t exactly been smooth. Over the last week further leaks have spread unofficial gameplay clips across platforms like Discord and X, and Rockstar has flexed its legal muscles, subpoenaing both Microsoft and Discord in hopes of finding the culprit. This had led to some frustration internally, and potentially changes to how Rockstar approaches security, according to a Bloomberg report. But, once again, it doesn’t seem to have put a dent in the fervor around the game. GTA VI is so big that even small updates, like a cover art reveal, rack up millions of views. And this has allowed Rockstar to do things no one else can. It can reveal gameplay through a mainstream platform like Netflix, and maintain sustained interest in the game despite only releasing two trailers over the span of several years.

“Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right,” Netflix exec Brandon Riegg said when announcing the gameplay reveal. “The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first.”

This mentality isn’t entirely new for Rockstar, but the success of GTA V has allowed the studio to be more confident with how it reveals and launches games, eschewing the traditional news cycle in favor of, well, whatever it wants. Back in 2016, on a random Sunday afternoon, the studio released an image that was simply its logo on a red background. The internet promptly went into a craze, correctly surmising that Rockstar was teasing the next Red Dead Redemption, an open-world Western series that had been dormant for several years. That game, Red Dead Redemption 2, went on to sell nearly 90 million copies, giving Rockstar another blockbuster to fill the gap between GTAs.

Open-world games have become widespread over the last decade or so, but there’s still no developer that renders its virtual worlds with the level of detail and realism that Rockstar does. That’s true whether we’re talking about a fictional version of modern California or the Wild West at the turn of the century. It’s also probably why the studio can get away with taking so long with GTA VI; fans have been given plenty of reason to believe that it’ll be worth the wait.

And that’s why the steady stream of leaks has done little to diminish the hype around the game. In fact, they’re almost serving as a form of marketing; Rockstar may be content with a drip feed of news and details, but anxious fans are eager to soak up every new detail about the game, whether it’s official or not.

What happens next

GTA VI isn’t a fix for everything ailing the industry, and most of its benefits will be temporary for everyone but Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive. There are also still plenty of questions ahead of its release, like what the future for the enduring multiplayer spinoff GTA Online looks like, or whether GTA VI’s satirical slant on Florida will still feel relevant after such a long development cycle. But for at least a few weeks later this year, players can pretend everything is normal while they lay waste to Vice City once again.

Tech.title: Doodle generative compositions in your browser with Musical Spirograph
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

I remember having a Spirograph as a kid and being obsessed with it. Its geometric patterns are hypnotic and gorgeous. I also love generative music composition. So bringing those two things together in a browser tab, I’m hooked. Musical Spirograph is a relatively simple concept. A set of points dash around the screen according to mathematical equations, generating hypotrochoids and epitrochoids. Those points pass through a series of concentric rings which trigger specific notes.

Honestly, that alone is fun enough, but you can customize it quite a bit. There are six different virtual rotors to pick from, you can have up to three arms drawing simultaneously, and there are a bunch of other parameters to tweak the pattern. Then there are six different scale options, or you can completely customize the notes, and there are six different synth presets. Plus you can change the quantization and BPM, or even expand the number of rings out to two octaves.

Sure, the sound engine isn’t great, and it’s prone to clipping and artifacts. And I really wish there was a way to get MIDI out of it to control other instruments. But it’s still a ton of fun to get lost in for a while.

Tech.title: W. Kamau Bell has the most practical ‘most indispensable tool’
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

W. Kamau Bell is one of those people who has always just seemed to be there. From Totally Biased, to Politically Re-Active, United Shades of America, and We Need to Talk About Cosby, his blend of comedy, social commentary, and political activism has helped him stand out. He’s won a Peabody and four Emmys, been a Celebrity Jeopardy! champion, received honors from the ACLU, and been crowned the Ambassador of Fishbone by founding member Chris Dowd. Bell is, if nothing else, a busy man.

So we’re very grateful that he took time between episodes of his podcast Who’s With Me, his comedy tour, and Substack of the same name, promoting his upcoming children’s book Rock Paper Scissors Cheese (out October 27th), and, of course, being a dad, to answer our weekly questionnaire.

What is your most indispensable tool?

A charger. All of this is just shiny paperweights without a charger.

Which app is the most underappreciated?

I probably use the map app every day. I wish MapQuest’s app was better, so I didn’t have to use the Trump Billionaire guys’ apps. You know who I’m talking about. The map apps that have the Gulf of Mexico listed as the Gulf of America. SOOOOOOOOO EMBARRASSING!!!

What is the first app you install on a new phone or computer?

It’s been a long, loooong time since I had a phone that didn’t just transfer my old apps over, but I would guess that if I had a clean phone with only the basic apps on it, I would quickly install YouTube. What do you expect me to do? Just think my own thoughts all day? I need somebody constantly telling me something about something. Or singing me something about something.

What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone?

Just come in a hard case with that piece of plastic that claims it stops your screen from cracking already on the phone. I just bought it. I don’t need a project, and I’m not comfortable asking the person at the cellphone place to do it for me. Also, I’m sure it is a scam, but I just put it on there anyway.

How many tabs do you have open right now?

I have 17 windows open across two different browser windows. That’s light work. When I’m writing a Substack article, I can get to 30 windows… easy. I only close them when I hit “publish” on an article. I have to earn the right to close a window.

Which social media platform do you use the most (if any)?

I really want to thank Elon Musk for breaking my addiction to Twitter. It wasn’t healthy, so I can say that he really improved my life by ruining Twitter. These days, I’m an Instagram and Threads guy. Not that Zuckerberg is significantly better than Elon, but as a public-facing person, I do need these platforms. But Zuckerberg better be careful. My generation isn’t afraid to leave social media platforms. We left MySpace and Friendster, just like I left Twitter.

What is your happy place online?

Watching the latest Japanese video on YouTube or watching Lionfield videos with my 8-year-old on Instagram

What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned?

Afro pick with extra-long metal teeth with a fist as the handle.

Which was the most disappointing?

A brush that claimed it could effectively comb Afros. I bought it because of Shark Tank. But I think my hair is just too long. Or the X-ray specs they used to sell in comic books.

What game do you have the fondest memories of?

It is a tie between Civilization on the PC and NBA Live on Sega Genesis. I’m talking like NBA Live ‘95. I’M SOOOOO OLD!

Which tech trend do you wish would go away?

AI.

What is one thing you wish you had created?

Flappy Bird. But I would have let it rock instead of deleting it. Maybe because I have three kids, I can’t look a gift app in the mouth like that. You all would have had at least eight Flappy Bird movies by now. It would have out-Minioned the Minion movies.

What creation are you most proud of?

My three daughters. It was a collab project.

What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

“Don’t think you are going to make it just by doing stand-up comedy. You need to learn how to write other things,” – Kevin Kataoka.

What is your current obsession?

The NBA off-season. It is way better than the actual season, even with the Knicks winning.

What do you do when you need to focus?

Coffee and extreme quiet… like leave me the eff alone… so I can listen to YouTube while I work. Middle of the night is the best time to work, but I can’t do that as often as I like… those three kids like it when both their parents are awake at the same time. My wife likes that better, too.

What do you do when you’re feeling stuck?

Change the song or play a silly cellphone game for four hours. Do you know YouTube has games now for free???

When was the last time you went somewhere without your phone?

Excuse me? EXCUSE ME??? WHY WOULD I DO THAT?

What’s the last piece of physical media you bought?

I’m a middle-aged-dad-who-buys-records-years-old. The guy at the shop (Mars Records in Oakland) holds things for me. I bought Fishbone’s first EP recently. I should really buy a record player.

What do you think is worth splurging on?

If you need a new computer, GET A NEW COMPUTER!

What would the tagline for your biopic be?

Doing the best he can.

What’s the last GIF or meme you used?

Tech.title: Amazon just hiked the prices for Echo, Fire TV, and Kindle products by up to 60 percent
Tech.content:
is a senior reviewer with over twenty years of experience. She covers smart home, IoT, and connected tech, and has written previously for Wirecutter, Wired, Dwell, BBC, and US News.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Citing “significant increases in memory and storage component costs,” Amazon has raised prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs, and Eeros by up to 60 percent, as first reported by Fortune.

The cheapest products in Amazon’s lineup were hit hardest, with the Echo Dot smart speaker jumping from $49.99 to $79.99. The Fire TV Stick 4K Max also rose by over 40 percent to $84.99, and the base level Kindle now costs $149.99, a nearly 37 percent increase.

In a statement to The Verge, Kristy Schmidt, senior communications manager of Amazon’s Devices & Services divison, said, “The consumer electronics industry is facing significant increases in memory and storage component costs. After absorbing these increases for as long as we could, we recently adjusted pricing across our product lines. Our approach has always been to offer great products at accessible prices, and that commitment hasn’t changed.”

Amazon’s flagship Echo Dot Max smart speaker, which launched last year, now costs $119.99, up from $99.99. Apple increased the price of its comparable HomePod Mini this summer to $129 from $99.99, also in response to rising costs. The Google Home Speaker remains at $99.99 for now.

Amazon hardware products apparently not affected include its line of Ring cameras and video doorbells, and the Echo Studio, its higher-end $219.99 smart speaker.

Tech.title: An okay laptop with 16GB of RAM is better than a nice laptop with 8GB, and this $520 HP OmniBook proves it
Tech.content:
is a reviewer covering laptops and the occasional gadget. He spent over 15 years in the photography industry before joining The Verge as a deals writer in 2021.

Laptop prices are out of whack. $500 used to get you a tolerable laptop, and $900 got you a really good one. They often had similar CPU, RAM, and storage options because that stuff was comparatively cheap; the difference was often in build quality and screen rather than power. But RAMageddon has thrown everything off. Even laptops like the $950 Surface Laptop now start with 8GB of RAM, which isn’t enough. And on the lower end, where manufacturers are struggling to compete with the $700 MacBook Neo, they’re cutting corners on storage, CPU, and build quality too.

However, one low-cost laptop has bucked this and genuinely surprised me. HP’s 16-inch OmniBook 3 is a basic productivity laptop that regularly goes for around $520 at Walmart and Amazon. It has Qualcomm’s base Snapdragon X chip, meaning passable everyday performance and excellent battery life. But it also has a humdrum screen, mediocre speakers, a run-of-the-mill trackpad, and a plastic build. Pre-RAMageddon, it would be nothing to write home about.

But 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD in an okay laptop for around $500? That counts as good news in 2026.

The entry-level OmniBook 3 I tested has an 8-core Snapdragon X processor, 16GB of RAM, 512GB SSD, and a 16-inch 1920 x 1200 anti-glare IPS LCD. And the OmniBook 3 is fairly portable for a larger laptop with lots of ports. It’s barely heavier than a 14-inch MacBook Pro, and at a maximum thickness of 0.63 inches / 16mm it’s decently thin. This big laptop doesn’t feel big. And despite a plastic chassis and low price it doesn’t feel too cheap either.

Component report card Screen: D

Webcam: C

Keyboard: C

Trackpad: C

Port selection: B

Speakers: D

Number of ugly stickers to remove: 2

As much as I would like to see more cheap Windows laptops with the sleek looks and sturdy all-metal build of the MacBook Neo, I wouldn’t mind if more of them were like the OmniBook 3. Its screen, keyboard, trackpad, and webcam are all at least passable to decent. There isn’t anything special here, but unlike the Chuwi UniBook there’s also nothing that feels like a punishment.

The 1920 x 1200 / 60Hz screen isn’t high-quality or bright enough to combat the sun when taken outside (it maxes out at 300 nits of brightness and covers a paltry 62.5 percent of the sRGB color space), but it isn’t washed out or bleeding light at its edges. The mechanical trackpad has a basic diving board-style hinge, but a confident and decent-feeling kachunk-y click. The 1080p webcam is actually fairly sharp, and it does a good job handling backlight from a bright window — with only a hint of green color cast. But hey, at least it has Windows Hello face unlocking. And at least this not-too-large large laptop has lots of ports and charges via USB-C with a very compact 65W GaN charger.

Just one USB-A and an audio jack on this side. But another USB-A, two USB-C, and HDMI over here. The left-aligned keyboard and trackpad allow for a generously sized numpad.

My biggest gripe is the dual speakers (unsurprisingly), which lack bass and sound too treble-y, but they’re just tolerable enough to live with. My next biggest is the keyboard (surprisingly). I usually like HP keyboards, but this one feels too stiff. If you’re the type to hammer your fingers down and you love a generously sized number pad you might be fine, but I get more typos than I’m used to from keys not registering. I could learn to live with it, but I’d still prefer not to have to.

HP OmniBook 3 16 / Qualcomm Snapdragon X X1-26-100 / 16GB / 512GB MacBook Neo / Apple A18 Pro / 8GB / 256GB Chuwi UniBook / Intel Core 3 304 “Wildcat Lake” / 8GB / 256GB Microsoft Surface Laptop 13-inch (2026) / Qualcomm Snapdragon X Plus X1P-46-100 / 8GB / 256GB Acer Aspire 14 AI / Intel Core Ultra 7 256V / 16GB / 1TB Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x / Qualcomm Snapdragon X X1-26-100 / 16GB / 256GB CPU cores 8 6 5 8 8 8 GPU Adreno X1-45 A18 Pro (5 GPU cores) Intel Graphics (1 GPU core) Adreno X1-45 Intel Arc 140V (8 GPU cores) Adreno X1-45 Geekbench 6 CPU Single 2142 3402 2385 2348 2769 2137 Geekbench 6 CPU Multi 10593 8508 6187 9421 10930 9728 Geekbench 6 GPU (OpenCL) 9577 19798 6019 9554 28556 9689 Premiere 4K Export (lower is better) 12 minutes, 8 seconds 8 minutes, 30 seconds 1 hour, 9 minutes, 29 seconds Crashed 7 minutes, 28 seconds 12 minutes, 59 seconds Sustained SSD reads (MB/s) 5017.12 1735.91 2394.57 3804.31 6391.51 5738.86 Sustained SSD writes (MB/s) 4370.35 1684.05 2092.66 3310.94 5524.22 2801.02 Price as tested about $520 $699 $449 $949.99 $1,049.99 $749.99

What I can totally live with is the performance. The OmniBook’s 8-core Snapdragon X processor is a little slower than the one in the $950 Surface Laptop I tested, but the OmniBook’s day-to-day performance is better because it’s not starved for RAM and its larger SSD is a little faster. Like other lower-end Snapdragon laptop chips it’s not going to wow you with graphics performance or tackle heavy content creation in Adobe apps, but it’s perfectly adequate for everyday multitasking work. Even when running several apps with a couple dozen Chrome tabs left open, including a video podcast playing, I didn’t feel it slow down the way the Surface Laptop or Chuwi UniBook, each with only 8GB of RAM, did.

And while a Snapdragon chip means this Windows laptop isn’t ideal for gaming, it does make it great on battery. You can pretty easily get around 12 hours of mixed web usage with a bit of music or video streaming.

It feels like the money went into the core specs of the OmniBook 3, and HP just barely stuck the landing on the right compromises elsewhere. As much as I adore the build quality of Microsoft’s Surface Laptops, if I were spending my own money I’d choose the OmniBook 3, never worry about how much RAM is in use, and save over $400.

Previous Next













1 / 8 The screen is bright enough to use it near a big window, but outside it’s difficult to see even in the shade.

If we reviewed the OmniBook 3 a year ago I might feel different, but it’s been a tiny breath of fresh air to use something this cheap and mostly think, “Not too bad!” Especially coming right after I tested the $450 Chuwi UniBook. An employee being issued this laptop for work shouldn’t feel like their IT department totally hates them. And while I think a MacBook Neo would still be a better all-around experience for a school-age kid, I’d totally understand saving nearly $200 to get the OmniBook 3 if a budget can’t be stretched.

My only worry is that the OmniBook 3’s price will go up like everything else. While there are more sub-$800 laptops coming, and I’ll be testing more very soon, the OmniBook 3’s price — and that of the OmniBook 5 I reviewed back in December — feel anomalous right now. The RAMageddon storm could eventually ruin them like it did many other laptops and devices. But, for now, there’s some safe harbor with this lowly OmniBook.
